cf0fd5ef620b.title: Agentic harness
cf0fd5ef620b.content: TR… . On this page . | Interaction states . | Idle state | Workflow state | . | Session lifecycle | Request classification . | The feature-request detection rule | . | Content workflows | Deterministic and agentic processing | BPMN execution: one skill, two engines | Feature-request workflow (CRDM) . | How the agent enters CRDM | What the user sees | How the agent exits CRDM | . | User-provided content and sources . | For CRDM specifically | . | Issue and bean discipline . | Issues vs beans | Rules for agents | . | Consolidated skill references | What is not built yet | . This page is generated from docs/source/concepts-agentic-harness/ — each section below links to its own source. ✎ Edit QA… TR… . The agentic harness is the interaction model that folio-assistant runs on — the rules, states, and workflows that govern how an agent and a user collaborate inside this platform. This page gathers in one place what individual skills describe separately, so an agent entering a session can look up the expected behaviour rather than reconstruct it from scattered rules. This is not about the agent’s internal architecture. It is about the observable contract between the agent and the user: what states the interaction can be in, how requests are classified, which workflow the agent enters for each class, and what the user should expect at each stage.

e6b2c08beaf3.title: Interaction states
e6b2c08beaf3.content: ✎ Edit QA… TR… . A user–agent interaction is always in exactly one of two states: . Idle state . The agent has no active workflow. It is waiting for a user request. On receiving one, it classifies the request (see Request classification) and transitions into the appropriate workflow state. Workflow state . The agent is executing a named workflow — each represented by a BPMN process diagram with the agent and user in separate swim lanes. The active workflow determines what the agent does next and what it expects from the user. Active workflows in this platform (the authoring, content-lifecycle, draft-to-publication and evidence-retrieval diagrams ship with the content layer, not this one): . | Workflow | BPMN source | Entered when | . | Authoring (paper) | authoring-a-paper.bpmn | User requests content authoring in a paper folio | . | Authoring (document) | authoring-a-document.bpmn | User requests content authoring in a document folio | . | Content lifecycle | content-lifecycle.bpmn | Content moves through validate → render → publish | . | Document ingestion | document-ingestion.bpmn | User drops a file in uploads/ | . | Draft to publication | draft-to-publication.bpmn | Content moves from draft to published | . | CRDM requirements | crdm-requirements.bpmn | Agent detects a feature request | . | Evidence retrieval | evidence-retrieval.bpmn | Agent searches for evidence to support a claim | . State transitions: a workflow can be suspended when the user asks to switch context. The agent records where it was (the current BPMN activity) and can resume later. Only one workflow is active at a time, but suspended workflows form a stack — the most recent is resumed first. The key rule: the agent always knows which workflow it is in. If it does not, it is in the idle state, and the next request starts a new workflow.

f81d26977c98.title: Session lifecycle
f81d26977c98.content: ✎ Edit QA… TR… . Every agent session follows the same lifecycle: . | Start — run the session-start sweep (beans prime, beans list, scripts/session-start-coord-sweep.sh). This surfaces the current work-plan, how far the default branch has moved, and recent sibling branch activity. See the todo-manager skill. | Classify — each user request is classified (see next section) and routed to the appropriate workflow. | Execute — the agent works within the active workflow, following its BPMN process. Each turn reports the work item being worked on and what is next. | Commit — every meaningful unit of work gets its own commit and push. PRs are opened at the first commit, not the end. See the continual-progress skill. | Handoff — when the session ends (user leaves, context limit, token exhaustion), the agent’s durable state is: . | Committed and pushed code | Work items updated with status and notes | Issue comments with summaries of what was accomplished | The chat is ephemeral; everything else survives | . | .

776c6b77854e.title: Request classification
776c6b77854e.content: ✎ Edit QA… TR… . Every user request is classified into one of these categories. The classification determines which workflow the agent enters. | Category | Description | Workflow entered | . | Content authoring | Write, edit, extend folio content (chapters, blocks, sections) | Authoring workflow (paper or document) | . | Content review | Review, validate, provide feedback on existing content | Content lifecycle / editing-HCI workflow | . | Content ingestion | Ingest a source document into the folio | Document ingestion workflow | . | Feature request | Request new platform capability (see crdm-detect) | CRDM requirements workflow | . | Information request | Ask about the platform, content, or process | No workflow — answer directly | . | Tool invocation | Run a specific tool (content_validate, qa_sweep, etc.) | No workflow — execute and report | . | Work-plan management | Create, update, or query work items | No workflow — execute and report | . | Bug report | Report broken behaviour in existing features | Triage: fix directly if small, CRDM if redesign needed | . The feature-request detection rule . The critical classification boundary is between content authoring and feature request. The crdm-detect skill (skills/process/crdm/crdm-detect.md) provides the detailed detection signals. The summary rule: . If implementing the request would require changes to folio-assistant (the platform repository) rather than to a folio repository, the request is a feature, and the agent should enter the CRDM workflow. When uncertain, the agent asks: “This sounds like it might need a platform change — is that right, or is this something I can do within the current content model?” .

fffb879ec15d.title: Content workflows
fffb879ec15d.content: ✎ Edit QA… TR… . When a request is classified as content work (authoring, review, ingestion), the agent follows the corresponding BPMN workflow. These pages describe them: . | Publication workflow — the content lifecycle from draft through validation, rendering, and publication. Covers roles (author, reviewer, editor), the base processes, activities and skills. | Document ingestion — how a dropped file becomes an L1 source: extract structure, derive content, build the L1 knowledge graph, completeness gate. | Writing guides: . | Writing a paper | Writing a document | WHO SMART DAK | WHO SMART IG | . | . The harness does not redefine these workflows. It provides the entry point — classifying the request and routing to the right one — and the exit point — returning to idle state when the workflow completes, or suspending if the user switches context.

6d83b2073c9b.title: Deterministic and agentic processing
6d83b2073c9b.content: ✎ Edit QA… TR… . Workflow processing here is a spectrum, not a switch, and the harness sits at four points on it: cat-harness.processes:policy enforcement decides whether a step that is not enabled is refused or merely noted; relaxable="false" decides whether a package may negotiate a base step away; cat-harness.processes:decision decides whether a branch is computed from a table rather than chosen; and the commit-boundary gate refuses the write by something that is not the agent. Those are not one axis, and treating them as one is the first thing to get wrong. At least three questions are being conflated — who decides the branch, what happens if the decision is wrong, and who enforces. A step can be fully agentic on the first and fully deterministic on the third: the commit boundary is exactly that, an agent deciding freely and a hook refusing the write regardless. A gateway now says which it is. <cat-harness.processes:decision> means a table computes it and a hand-supplied outcome is refused; <cat-harness.processes:judgement reason="…"> means somebody’s call, with the reason required. The marker exists because “no table because this is a judgement” and “no table because nobody wrote one” otherwise look the same. bun run cat check:workflow-refs prints the three-way split (table, judgement, neither), so how much of this is decided by a model? is counted rather than asserted. What that count is for is research, and it is open. Which judgement points are safety risks, how much must be deterministic, and how models compare across sub-workflows under a controlled overlay of context and memories are three questions this repository can now ask and has not answered. The agenda, with each claim marked as measured, decided or hypothesis, is deterministic-and-agentic.

6f486e19ca86.title: BPMN execution: one skill, two engines
6f486e19ca86.content: ✎ Edit QA… TR… . The skill this spectrum is about: . BPMN Execution Skill: given a Process, Context, State and Role, utilize one or more Skills in order to execute a Task. One skill, two kinds of Tool. The skill is the same at both ends: take the process, the context, the current state and the role, pick the skills, and do the task. What changes is the Tool that runs it, and a Tool is swappable behind a skill in the way every other Tool here is. |   | deterministic end | agentic end | . | Tool | any open-source BPMN 2.0 engine | an agentic swarm | . | Scope of an agent | one task at a time, handed to it by the engine | most or all tasks | . | State | held by the engine, strictly | ungoverned: the swarm holds it | . | Swimlanes | enforced: only the lane’s role may perform its task | relaxed: an agent may act across lanes | . | What keeps it honest | the engine refuses a step before it happens | mechanical + agentic QA/QC reports find it after it happened | . The two ends differ in when a rule is checked, not in which rule. The same process, the same roles and the same permissions govern both. The engine checks them before a task starts and refuses; the swarm acts and a QA/QC report checks them after, from the record of what was done. That needs the rules and the record to be data a report can read: W3C ODRL 2.2 is the permission language and W3C PROV-O the execution log. Most real runs sit between the ends, and per task rather than per process: the previous section already counts which gateways are computed and which are judgement calls. A signing step can be engine-enforced inside an otherwise agentic run, and that is a property of the task, not of the whole diagram. Partly built. No BPMN engine is wired in. The mechanical QA/QC report is bun run cat prov:qaqc: it writes each workflow instance’s history as a PROV-O log and re-checks every step against the ODRL policies, as advice (the task-authorization skill). The agentic QA/QC report does not exist yet.

92a09e026547.title: Feature-request workflow (CRDM)
92a09e026547.content: ✎ Edit QA… TR… . When a request is classified as a feature request, the agent enters the CRDM requirements workflow (full documentation, BPMN). How the agent enters CRDM . The detection logic is in skills/process/crdm/crdm-detect.md. Three scenarios: . New session, first request is a feature: → Acknowledge, explain you will help work through requirements first, enter Phase 1. Existing session, already in CRDM: → Incorporate the new request into the current requirements document, continue. Existing session, doing content work: → Synthesise the feature need, ask user whether to pause content work and address it now or work item it for later. What the user sees . The agent does not say “entering CRDM mode” or use methodology jargon. Instead: . “This sounds like a platform change — something we’d need to add to folio-assistant itself. Before I build anything, let me help you work through exactly what’s needed so we get it right. I’ll document the requirements on the issue so others can weigh in.” . How the agent exits CRDM . The CRDM workflow exits when: . | All work items from the signed-off requirements are resolved, OR | The user explicitly defers the remaining work | . On exit, if a content workflow was suspended, the agent resumes it.

317a3b45e390.title: User-provided content and sources
317a3b45e390.content: ✎ Edit QA… TR… . Users provide content and source material through multiple channels. The agent should accept all of them and route them into the appropriate pipeline: . | Channel | Example | Routed to | . | uploads/ directory | User drops a Word doc, PDF, Excel file | Document ingestion pipeline | . | library/ references | User references an already-ingested L1 source | Direct citation in content | . | content/ edits | User edits a .md block directly | Content authoring workflow | . | GitHub issue attachments | User attaches a file to an issue comment | Agent downloads and processes | . | Chat upload | User uploads a file in the LLM chat interface | Agent saves to uploads/ or processes inline | . | URL reference | User pastes a link to a document | Agent fetches and ingests if appropriate | . For CRDM specifically . During requirements gathering, user-provided content is input to requirements, not content to author. The agent should: . | Read and understand the provided material | Extract requirements-relevant information | Synthesise it into the needs statement or requirements document | Reference the source in the issue comment (with link or attachment) | . Example: a user uploads a public consultation feedback Excel spreadsheet. The agent does not try to ingest it as folio content; it reads the feedback items and synthesises them into requirements for the review triage tool.

4d65215241d9.title: Issue and bean discipline
4d65215241d9.content: ✎ Edit QA… TR… . Feature work must be linked to a GitHub issue. Content work uses work items. The two are related but not synonymous. Issues vs beans . |   | GitHub issue | Work item | . | Scope | A feature, requirement set, or user story | A single PR-sized unit of work | . | Audience | Stakeholders, requestor, BA | Agent, developer | . | Lifecycle | Open → requirements → sign-off → implementation → close | Created → in-progress → resolved | . | Relation | One issue has many work items | Each work item references its parent issue | . Rules for agents . | Feature work → issue first. Before implementing, check: . | Is there an existing open issue? Search by keywords. | If no open match, check recently closed issues. | If no match at all, ask the user to create one. Do not create an issue without user permission. | . | Always feature branch + PR. No exceptions for feature work. The branch name should reference the issue number (e.g. feat/197-word-import). | Always ask before merging to main. The user must explicitly confirm. Feature changes affect the platform. | Post round summaries to the issue. After each round of implementation (one or more work items resolved), post a comment on the linked issue containing: . | What was accomplished in this round | What remains to be accomplished (open work items) | Links to updated content for review (staging URLs, docs pages) | Before/after comparison table for changed pages | . | Never close an issue without explicit authorization. The BA or stakeholder closes it. The agent closes it only when the BA explicitly says to. An agent must never assume completion. | Requirements may span multiple issues. The agent should link to all relevant issues and note the relationships. | Work items are not issues. beans create is for work-plan items. Issues are for stakeholder-facing requirements. Do not conflate them. | .

7444ff12c167.doc: Publish an ArchiMate model — every picture derived from it
7444ff12c167.title: Publish an ArchiMate model — every picture derived from it
7444ff12c167.content: Process_ArchimatePublish · strict · 4 step(s) . An ArchiMate model is authored in Archi and committed; everything a reader sees is derived from it by three mechanical Tools, in order, in the pipeline lane: archimate-check (it parses and resolves), archimate-metamodel (the element types and relationship patterns it uses, each checked against ArchiMate’s relationship table), and archimate-pages (a page and an IRI for every view, element and relationship, every view drawn, and the “Metamodel in use” page). No step draws a diagram by hand, and none runs Archi or a JVM (skill archimate-models). The metamodel is the second step’s output, so it cannot disagree with the model. i i i i

2e30481b076e.title: Обзор
2e30481b076e.content: Правила, стоящие за этой страницей. Архитектура описывает форму; Навыки определяют решения. Адаптеры относительно профилей — content-profiles. Куда относится новый узел до его создания — placement. Структура репозитория и каждый вид графа — directory-conventions. Формирование и верификация поверхности MCP — mcp-assembly и mcp-contract. При разногласиях между этой страницей и Навыком приоритет имеет Навык. folio-assistant — это MCP-сервер с подключаемым уровнем адаптеров контента, системой навыков, типизированной объектной моделью контента, RBAC и стратегией развертывания. Контент, с которым он работает, находится в отдельном репозитории — платформа не зависит от контента. flowchart TD subgraph Harness["LLM-харнесс · Claude Code / Antigravity / Gemini"] LLM["Агент"] end LLM <-->|MCP stdio/http| Server["FolioServer · src/server.ts"] Server --> Tools["Основные инструменты<br/>check-deps · skill-fetch · preview · preferences · work_plan_prime"] Server --> Adapter{"Адаптер контента"} Adapter --> Paper["адаптер paper<br/>lean · validate · render"] Adapter --> Future["другие адаптеры …"] Server --> RBAC["Доступ · src/core/rbac.ts + access.ts → ODRL policies/"] Server --> Git["Помощник Git · src/core/git.ts"] Server --> Feedback["Хранилище отзывов · src/core/feedback.ts"] Tools --> Skills["Пакеты навыков<br/>schemas/skills/*"] Paper --> Model["Объектная модель контента<br/>schemas/types.ts · constraints.ts · builders.ts"] .

d41aeead3f01.title: Разделение ответственности — текущее и будущее состояние
d41aeead3f01.content: Сегодня этот репозиторий представляет собой репозиторий инструментов (Tool repo) и репозиторий контента (Content repo) в одном рабочем каталоге; целевое состояние — пять компонуемых инстансов folio-assistant. Дочерние страницы раскрывают эту тему: . | страница | на какой вопрос отвечает | . | Таксономия репозиториев | Какие виды репозиториев существуют — Tool, Test, Content, Consumer — и что может содержать каждый из них | . | Текущее состояние | Что фактически находится в этом репозитории сегодня (в измеренном виде) и где происходит смешение | . | Будущее состояние | Пять целевых репозиториев и то, какой каталог в какой из них попадает | . | План миграции | Фазы 0/I/II/III, контрольные точки (gates) и то, что пока остается нерешенным | . | Минимальный cat-harness | Что сохраняется в харнессе, если применить тест на «несамодокументируемость» | . | Инстансы харнесса | Чем ЯВЛЯЕТСЯ инстанс — схемы, визуализации, инструменты; четыре каталога; рендеринг по умолчанию | . Требование рендеринга — повышающаяся планка: bootstrap освобожден от визуализатора и взамен обязан предоставлять собственные .json/.jsonld, а с уровня cat-harness применяется все остальное. См. С чего начинается требование. В остальной части этой страницы описывается архитектура в ее текущем виде.

7b78c9301cfb.title: Структура репозитория
7b78c9301cfb.content: | Путь | Что здесь находится | . | src/ | Сервер MCP (server.ts), точка входа (index.ts), ядро (git, rbac, cache, feedback, logging) и основные инструменты (tools/) | . | adapters/ | Адаптеры контента — paper/ (Lean + LaTeX) и отдельный mcp-server/ | . | schemas/ | Объектная модель контента (types.ts, constraints.ts, builders.ts) и схемы JSON для каждого навыка (schemas/skills/*) | . | skills/ | Пакеты навыков (content-lifecycle, authoring-math, authoring-who-smart-guidelines) с их Docker-манифестами | . | content/ | Инструменты пайплайна контента (валидаторы, QA, вспомогательные скрипты рендеринга) — но не сам контент | . | ui/, viewer/, home_page/ | Веб-интерфейс, интерактивный просмотрщик и пример сайта Pages | . | deploy/ | Развертывание (Caddy, docker-compose, провижининг, OAuth) | . | docs/ | Этот сайт документации | . | .github/ | CI-воркфлоу и скрипты (сборка, публикация, QA, документация) | . | .claude/skills/ | Локальные навыки агента + хуки возможностей | .

21fc81e92bb5.title: Сервер MCP
21fc81e92bb5.content: FolioServer (src/server.ts) регистрирует основные инструменты, затем запрашивает у активного адаптера контента регистрацию его собственных инструментов. Он поддерживает два типа транспорта — --stdio (то, что запускают харнессы) и --http (общий долгоживущий инстанс). Вызовы инструментов логируются с замером времени выполнения.

88127621df6c.title: Адаптеры контента
88127621df6c.content: Адаптер контента инкапсулирует все, что специфично для конкретного типа: какие артефакты существуют, как их валидировать, как их собирать/рендерить и какие дополнительные инструменты MCP регистрировать. Адаптер document (adapters/document/) служит основой для текстовых (прозаических) фолио; адаптер paper (adapters/paper/) расширяет его и предоставляет инструменты жизненного цикла Lean (lean_setup/build/check/status), валидацию и рендеринг (paper_render_pdf/html, formula_render). Для новых типов контента добавляется новый адаптер — см. Добавление типа контента.

6522d2307c9a.title: Навыки и пакеты навыков
6522d2307c9a.content: Навык — это задокументированная, ограниченная схемой единица работы (например, lean-formalization). Навыки группируются в пакеты, которые объявляют свои зависимости Docker/среды выполнения через package-manifest.json. LLM обнаруживает навыки с помощью skill_list и загружает инструкции с помощью skill_fetch. Полный список навыков и ролей — а также то, как они компонуются с LLM (RBAC, возможности, требования), — находится на странице Навыки и роли; контракт входных/выходных данных каждого навыка опубликован в Справочнике схем навыков.

5a0d8c6c6ff3.title: Объектная модель контента
5a0d8c6c6ff3.content: Для статей контент представляет собой дерево типизированных блоков, валидируемых во время выполнения с помощью Zod: . | schemas/types.ts — Block, Section, Chapter, Paper и виды блоков | schemas/constraints.ts — схемы Zod и правила ограничений | schemas/builders.ts — валидируемые конструкторы (definition(), theorem(), …) | . Они задокументированы в сгенерированном Справочнике по TypeScript API.

0f5aba169020.title: Управление доступом — ODRL, проверка перед каждой задачей
0f5aba169020.content: Существует единая система разрешений, и это W3C ODRL 2.2: действия в skills/permissions/permissions.json, права в policies/*.jsonld, оцениваемые с помощью permits() / decide() в schemas/odrl.ts. К ней обращаются два вызывающих компонента: . | Исполнитель BPMN перед каждой задачей и решением (src/workflow/authorize.ts): аутентифицирован ли субъект, подходит ли он для роли данной дорожки, разрешено ли ему выполнять здесь perform-task и имеет ли он право работать с контентом? На сегодняшний день носит рекомендательный характер: deny или несоответствие роли приводят к отказу, а unknown фиксируется в журнале. | HTTP-маршруты через src/core/rbac.ts: каждый маршрут указывает действие, которое он выполняет (content-authoring, review-comments, adjudication), а сессии шлюза аутентификации (auth-gateway) объявляются субъектами, чьи права заданы в policies/http-gateway.jsonld. Здесь unknown приводит к отказу. | . Данный регламент закреплен в навыке task-authorization.

aabdcb32a6ae.title: Прайминг плана работы (между харнессами)
aabdcb32a6ae.content: План работы хранится в beans и предоставляется тремя способами, благодаря чему любой харнесс получает идентичный прайминг: . | AGENTS.md — статический регламент, нативно считываемый каждым агентом. | Хук SessionStart — каждый харнесс запускает общий скрипт прайминга scripts/session-start-coord-sweep.sh. | MCP-инструмент work_plan_prime — динамический прайминг в реальном времени для любого агента, подключенного к MCP. | . Полное описание кросс-агентной архитектуры см. в docs/folio-assistant-migration.md.

babfe85c0b2b.title: Развертывание
babfe85c0b2b.content: deploy/ содержит шаблон обратного прокси Caddy, docker-compose.yml, скрипт провижининга, настройку Google OAuth и скрипт самообновления для запуска общего HTTP-инстанса. Docker-манифесты пакетов навыков объединяют зависимости apt/pip/npm в единый образ для каждого активного набора пакетов.

1da4e4dd2773.title: Architecture
1da4e4dd2773.content: . | Vue d’ensemble | Séparation des préoccupations — état actuel et futur | Agencement du dépôt | Le serveur MCP | Adaptateurs de contenu | Compétences et paquets de compétences | Le modèle d’objets de contenu | Contrôle d’accès — ODRL, vérifié avant chaque tâche | Amorçage du plan de travail (inter-harnais) | Déploiement | .

6d81ea38860a.title: Vue d’ensemble
6d81ea38860a.content: Les règles derrière cette page. L’architecture décrit la forme ; les compétences régissent les décisions. Les adaptateurs par rapport aux profils — content-profiles. L’emplacement d’un nouveau nœud avant sa création — placement. L’agencement du dépôt et chaque type de graphe — directory-conventions. Composition et vérification de la surface MCP — mcp-assembly et mcp-contract. En cas de désaccord entre cette page et une compétence, la compétence l’emporte. folio-assistant est un serveur MCP doté d’une couche d’adaptateurs de contenu enfichable, d’un système de compétences, d’un modèle d’objets de contenu typé, d’un RBAC et d’une stratégie de déploiement. Le contenu sur lequel il opère réside dans un dépôt séparé — la plateforme est indépendante du contenu. flowchart TD subgraph Harness[Harnais LLM · Claude Code / Antigravity / Gemini] LLM[Agent] end LLM <-->|MCP stdio/http| Server[FolioServer · src/server.ts] Server --> Tools[Outils de base<br/>check-deps · skill-fetch · preview · preferences · work_plan_prime] Server --> Adapter{Adaptateur de contenu} Adapter --> Paper[adaptateur paper<br/>lean · validate · render] Adapter --> Future[autres adaptateurs …] Server --> RBAC[Accès · src/core/rbac.ts + access.ts → ODRL policies/] Server --> Git[Assistant Git · src/core/git.ts] Server --> Feedback[Stockage des retours · src/core/feedback.ts] Tools --> Skills[Paquets de compétences<br/>schemas/skills/*] Paper --> Model[Modèle d'objets de contenu<br/>schemas/types.ts · constraints.ts · builders.ts] .

b3cbce274a2f.title: Séparation des préoccupations — état actuel et futur
b3cbce274a2f.content: La division de la plateforme en instances composables est décrite dans les pages filles : . | page | ce à quoi elle répond | . | Taxonomie des dépôts | Quels types de dépôts existent — Outils, Tests, Contenu, Consommateur — et ce que chacun peut contenir | . | État actuel | Ce qui se trouve réellement dans ce dépôt aujourd’hui, mesures à l’appui, et où se situe le mélange | . | État futur | Les cinq dépôts cibles et dans lequel chaque répertoire atterrit | . | Plan de migration | Phases 0/I/II/III, les étapes clés (gates) et ce qui reste à trancher | . | cat-harness minimal | Ce qui subsiste dans le harnais une fois que le critère « non auto-documenté » est appliqué comme test | . | Instances de harnais | Ce qu’EST une instance — schémas, visualisations, outils ; les quatre répertoires ; le rendu par défaut | . Le minimum indique qu’un harnais ne produit rien qu’un humain regarde, et la page des instances qu’une instance effectue un rendu par défaut ; les deux tiennent, car l’exigence de rendu est un plancher qui s’élève : bootstrap est exempté du visualiseur et fournit ses propres .json/.jsonld à la place, et cat-harness est la couche où le reste s’applique. Voir Où commence l’exigence. Le reste de cette page décrit l’architecture telle qu’elle est actuellement.

0a2e0b2725d7.title: Agencement du dépôt
0a2e0b2725d7.content: La liste qui fait foi est cat-harness.json : chaque répertoire que déclare cette couche, avec le type de graphe qu’il contient. Ceux qu’un lecteur cherche d’abord : . | Chemin | Ce qui s’y trouve | . | skills/ | Le graphe de connaissances : paquets de compétences (skills/<domaine>/<paquet>/, chacun avec un package-manifest.json), rôles, permissions et exigences | . | processes/ | Les processus BPMN exécutables et les tables DMN que calculent leurs passerelles | . | schemas/ | Les schémas JSON par compétence (schemas/skills/) et les documents de schéma que déclare le harnais | . | tools/ | Les définitions d’outils, un tools/<id>/<id>.json par outil | . | policies/ | Ce qu’un acteur peut faire, sous forme de politiques W3C ODRL 2.2 | . | sdlc/, work-plan/ | Les sous-graphes de livraison logicielle et de plan de travail | . | library/, uploads/ | Le contenu source L1 ingéré, et la file d’où il est ingéré | . | docs/ | Ce site de documentation | . | .github/ | Les workflows de CI | . Le code du serveur, les adaptateurs et les scripts nommés sur cette page (src/, adapters/, scripts/, deploy/) ne sont pas dans cette couche ; ils sont livrés avec la couche d’outils.

45f5bf1bae22.title: Le serveur MCP
45f5bf1bae22.content: FolioServer (src/server.ts) enregistre les outils de base, puis demande à l’adaptateur de contenu actif d’enregistrer ses propres outils. Il prend en charge deux modes de transport — --stdio (ce que lancent les harnais) et --http (une instance partagée à longue durée de vie). Les appels d’outils sont consignés avec leur temps d’exécution.

469ec9c93acc.title: Adaptateurs de contenu
469ec9c93acc.content: Un adaptateur de contenu encapsule tout ce qui est spécifique à un type : quels artefacts existent, comment les valider, comment les compiler/effectuer leur rendu, et quels outils MCP supplémentaires enregistrer. L’adaptateur document (adapters/document/) constitue la base pour les folios de prose ; l’adaptateur paper (adapters/paper/) l’étend et fournit les outils du cycle de vie Lean (lean_setup/build/check/status), la validation et le rendu (paper_render_pdf/html, formula_render). Les nouveaux types de contenu ajoutent un nouvel adaptateur — voir Ajouter un type de contenu.

0cd23661e546.title: Compétences et paquets de compétences
0cd23661e546.content: Une compétence est une unité de travail documentée et délimitée par un schéma (par ex. lean-formalization). Les compétences sont regroupées en paquets qui déclarent leurs dépendances Docker/d’exécution via un fichier package-manifest.json. Le LLM découvre les compétences avec skill_list et charge les instructions avec skill_fetch. La liste complète des compétences et des rôles — ainsi que la manière dont ils se composent avec le LLM (RBAC, capacités, exigences) — se trouve sur la page Compétences et rôles ; le contrat d’entrée/sortie de chaque compétence est publié dans la Référence des schémas de compétences.

fe02d65da842.title: Le modèle d’objets de contenu
fe02d65da842.content: Pour les articles, le contenu est un arbre de blocs typés validés à l’exécution avec Zod : . | schemas/types.ts — Block, Section, Chapter, Paper, et types de blocs | schemas/constraints.ts — schémas Zod et règles de contraintes | schemas/builders.ts — constructeurs validés (definition(), theorem(), …) | . Ceux-ci sont documentés dans la Référence de l’API TypeScript générée.

7496ba2728b4.title: Contrôle d’accès — ODRL, vérifié avant chaque tâche
7496ba2728b4.content: Il n’existe qu’un seul système de permissions, et il s’agit de W3C ODRL 2.2 : les actions dans skills/permissions/permissions.json, les autorisations dans policies/*.jsonld, évaluées par permits() / decide() dans schemas/odrl.ts. Deux appelants le sollicitent : . | L’exécuteur BPMN, avant chaque tâche et décision (src/workflow/authorize.ts) : l’acteur est-il authentifié, éligible pour le rôle du couloir, autorisé à exécuter perform-task ici, et autorisé à toucher au contenu ? Consultatif aujourd’hui : un refus (deny) ou une non-concordance de rôle est rejeté, et unknown est consigné. | Les routes HTTP, via src/core/rbac.ts : chaque route nomme l’action qu’elle effectue (content-authoring, review-comments, adjudication), et les sessions de la passerelle d’authentification sont des acteurs déclarés dont les droits sont définis dans policies/http-gateway.jsonld. Ici, unknown refuse. | . La règle de conduite est définie par la compétence task-authorization.

1bb0ed0aa5d9.title: Amorçage du plan de travail (inter-harnais)
1bb0ed0aa5d9.content: Le plan de travail est stocké dans beans et exposé de trois manières pour que tout harnais soit amorcé de façon identique : . | AGENTS.md — discipline statique, lue nativement par chaque agent. | Hook SessionStart — chaque harnais exécute l’amorce partagée scripts/session-start-coord-sweep.sh. | Outil MCP work_plan_prime — amorçage en direct pour tout agent connecté via MCP. | . Voir docs/folio-assistant-migration.md pour la conception inter-agents complète.

5798bec1a01d.title: Déploiement
5798bec1a01d.content: deploy/ (couche d’outils) contient un modèle de proxy inverse Caddy, docker-compose.yml, un script de provisionnement, la configuration de Google OAuth et un script de mise à jour automatique pour exécuter une instance HTTP partagée. Les manifestes Docker des paquets de compétences regroupent les dépendances apt/pip/npm dans une image unique par ensemble de paquets actif.

309326f75112.title: الهندسة المعمارية
309326f75112.content: . | نظرة عامة | فصل الاهتمامات — الوضع الحالي والمستقبلي | تخطيط المستودع | خادم MCP | محولات المحتوى | المهارات وحزم المهارات | نموذج كائنات المحتوى | التحكم في الوصول — ODRL، يتم التحقق منه قبل كل مهمة | تهيئة خطة العمل (عبر أطر العمل المختلفة) | النشر | .

44442fd38d9e.title: نظرة عامة
44442fd38d9e.content: القواعد الكامنة وراء هذه الصفحة. تصف الهندسة المعمارية الهيكل؛ بينما تحكم المهارات القرارات. المحولات مقابل ملفات التعريف — content-profiles. أين تنتمي العقدة الجديدة قبل إنشائها — placement. وتخطيط المستودع وكل نوع من أنواع الرسوم البيانية — directory-conventions. وتركيب واجهة MCP والتحقق منها — mcp-assembly و mcp-contract. وحيثما تختلف هذه الصفحة مع إحدى المهارات، فإن المهارة هي التي تسود. إن folio-assistant هو خادم MCP يضم طبقة محولات محتوى قابلة للتوصيل، ونظام مهارات، ونموذج كائنات محتوى مصنف بالأنواع، ونظام تحكم في الوصول قائم على الأدوار (RBAC)، وآلية نشر. ويعيش المحتوى الذي يعمل عليه في مستودع منفصل — فالمنصة مستقلة عن المحتوى. flowchart TD subgraph Harness["إطار عمل LLM · Claude Code / Antigravity / Gemini"] LLM["الوكيل"] end LLM <-->|MCP stdio/http| Server["FolioServer · src/server.ts"] Server --> Tools["الأدوات الأساسية<br/>check-deps · skill-fetch · preview · preferences · work_plan_prime"] Server --> Adapter{"محول المحتوى"} Adapter --> Paper["محول paper<br/>lean · validate · render"] Adapter --> Future["محولات أخرى …"] Server --> RBAC["الوصول · src/core/rbac.ts + access.ts → ODRL policies/"] Server --> Git["مساعد Git · src/core/git.ts"] Server --> Feedback["مخزن الملاحظات · src/core/feedback.ts"] Tools --> Skills["حزم المهارات<br/>schemas/skills/*"] Paper --> Model["نموذج كائنات المحتوى<br/>schemas/types.ts · constraints.ts · builders.ts"] .

5aa1ab3c3ecb.title: فصل الاهتمامات — الوضع الحالي والمستقبلي
5aa1ab3c3ecb.content: تصف الصفحات الفرعية تقسيم المنصة إلى حالات (instances) قابلة للتركيب: . | الصفحة | ما تجيب عليه | . | تصنيف المستودعات | ما هي أنواع المستودعات الموجودة — أداة (Tool)، واختبار (Test)، ومحتوى (Content)، ومستهلك (Consumer) — وما قد يحتويه كل منها | . | الوضع الحالي | ما هو موجود بالفعل في هذا المستودع اليوم، بالأرقام المقاسة، وأين يكمن المزيج | . | الوضع المستقبلي | المستودعات الخمسة المستهدفة وأي دليل يستقر في أيّ منها | . | خطة الانتقال | المراحل 0/I/II/III، والبوابات، وما لم يُحسم بعد | . | الحد الأدنى لـ cat-harness | ما يتبقى في إطار العمل (harness) بمجرد تطبيق معيار “ليس توثيقًا ذاتيًا” كاختبار | . | حالات إطار العمل | ما هي الحالة (instance) في واقعها — المخططات، والتصورات المرئية، والأدوات؛ والأدلة الأربعة؛ والتصيير الافتراضي | . ينص الحد الأدنى على أن إطار العمل لا ينتج شيئًا ينظر إليه إنسان، وتنص صفحة الحالات على أن الحالة تقوم بالتصيير افتراضيًا؛ ويصح الأمران لأن متطلب التصيير هو حد أدنى يرتفع تدريجيًا، مع إعفاء bootstrap من أداة التصور المرئي مع التزامه بتقديم .json/.jsonld الخاصة به بدلاً من ذلك، في حين يمثل cat-harness الطبقة التي يبدأ عندها تطبيق الباقي. راجع أين يبدأ المتطلب. يصف باقي هذه الصفحة الهندسة المعمارية كما هي عليه الآن.

16cb06876f33.title: تخطيط المستودع
16cb06876f33.content: القائمة المرجعية هي cat-harness.json: كل دليل تعلنه هذه الطبقة، مع نوع الرسم البياني الذي يحمله. الأدلة التي يبحث عنها القارئ أولاً: . | المسار | ما يحتويه | . | skills/ | رسم المعرفة البياني: حزم المهارات (skills/<area>/<package>/، ولكل منها package-manifest.json)، والأدوار، والأذونات، والمتطلبات | . | processes/ | عمليات BPMN القابلة للتنفيذ وجداول DMN التي تحسب منها بواباتها | . | schemas/ | مخططات JSON لكل مهارة (schemas/skills/) ووثائق المخططات التي يعلنها إطار العمل | . | tools/ | تعريفات الأدوات، ملف tools/<id>/<id>.json لكل أداة | . | policies/ | ما يحق للفاعل فعله، على شكل سياسات W3C ODRL 2.2 | . | sdlc/، وwork-plan/ | الرسمان الفرعيان لتسليم البرمجيات ولخطة العمل | . | library/، وuploads/ | محتوى المصادر L1 المستوعَب، والطابور الذي يُستوعَب منه | . | docs/ | موقع التوثيق هذا | . | .github/ | مهام سير عمل CI | . شفرة الخادم والمحولات والبرامج النصية المذكورة في هذه الصفحة (src/، وadapters/، وscripts/، وdeploy/) ليست في هذه الطبقة؛ بل تُشحن مع طبقة الأدوات.

8e986a8b9e44.title: خادم MCP
8e986a8b9e44.content: يقوم FolioServer (src/server.ts) بتسجيل الأدوات الأساسية، ثم يطلب من محول المحتوى النشط تسجيل أدواته. وهو يدعم وسيلتي نقل — --stdio (التي تشغلها أطر العمل) و--http (حالة مشتركة طويلة التشغيل). ويتم تسجيل استدعاءات الأدوات مع توقيتاتها.

0d4d82dfc8df.title: محولات المحتوى
0d4d82dfc8df.content: يغلف محول المحتوى كل ما يخص نوعًا معينًا: ما هي المخرجات (artifacts) الموجودة، وكيفية التحقق منها، وكيفية بنائها/تصييرها، وما هي أدوات MCP الإضافية التي يجب تسجيلها. ويعد محول document (adapters/document/) هو الأساس لملفات المحتوى النثرية؛ بينما يوسعه محول paper (adapters/paper/) ويوفر أدوات دورة حياة Lean (lean_setup/build/check/status)، والتحقق، والتصيير (paper_render_pdf/html، وformula_render). وتضيف أنواع المحتوى الجديدة محولاً جديدًا — راجع إضافة نوع محتوى.

c78122150290.title: المهارات وحزم المهارات
c78122150290.content: الـ مهارة (skill) هي وحدة عمل موثقة ومقيدة بمخطط بياني (مثل lean-formalization). وتُجمع المهارات في حزم تعلن عن تبعات Docker وبيئة التشغيل الخاصة بها عبر ملف package-manifest.json. ويكتشف النموذج اللغوي الكبير (LLM) المهارات عبر skill_list ويحمّل التعليمات عبر skill_fetch. وتوجد القائمة الكاملة للمهارات والأدوار — وكيفية تكاملها مع النموذج اللغوي الكبير (RBAC، والقدرات، والمتطلبات) — في صفحة المهارات والأدوار؛ كما يُنشر عقد المدخلات/المخرجات لكل مهارة في مرجع مخططات المهارات.

b90918f35f45.title: نموذج كائنات المحتوى
b90918f35f45.content: بالنسبة للأوراق العلمية، فإن المحتوى هو شجرة من الكتل (blocks) محددة الأنواع يتم التحقق منها أثناء التشغيل عبر Zod: . | schemas/types.ts — Block، وSection، وChapter، وPaper، وأنواع الكتل | schemas/constraints.ts — مخططات Zod وقواعد القيود | schemas/builders.ts — بناة الكائنات التي تم التحقق منها (definition()، وtheorem()، …) | . وهذه العناصر موثقة في مرجع واجهة برمجة تطبيقات TypeScript المُولّد.

4b0b08c4e76c.title: التحكم في الوصول — ODRL، يتم التحقق منه قبل كل مهمة
4b0b08c4e76c.content: يوجد نظام أذونات واحد فقط، وهو W3C ODRL 2.2: الإجراءات في skills/permissions/permissions.json، والمنح في policies/*.jsonld، ويتم تقييمها عبر permits() / decide() في schemas/odrl.ts. ويستعلم عنه طرفان مستدعيان: . | مُنفِّذ BPMN، قبل كل مهمة وقرار (src/workflow/authorize.ts): هل الفاعل موثق، ومؤهل لدور المسار (lane)، ومصرح له بـ perform-task هنا، ومسموح له بلمس المحتوى؟ وهو استشاري اليوم: فالرفض deny أو عدم تطابق الدور يؤدي إلى الرفض، ويتم تسجيل الحالة unknown. | مسارات HTTP، من خلال src/core/rbac.ts: يحدد كل مسار الإجراء الذي ينفذه (content-authoring، وreview-comments، وadjudication)، وتُعد جلسات بوابة المصادقة (auth-gateway) فاعلين معلنين تكمن منحهم في policies/http-gateway.jsonld. وهنا تؤدي الحالة unknown إلى الرفض. | . والانضباط المتبع هو مهارة task-authorization.

2ff338934dbb.title: تهيئة خطة العمل (عبر أطر العمل المختلفة)
2ff338934dbb.content: يتم تخزين خطة العمل في beans وإبرازها بثلاث طرق حتى تتم تهيئة أي إطار عمل بشكل متطابق: . | AGENTS.md — انضباط ثابت، يقرؤه كل وكيل أصلاً. | خطاف SessionStart — يشغل كل إطار عمل برنامج التهيئة المشترك scripts/session-start-coord-sweep.sh. | أداة MCP المعنونة work_plan_prime — تهيئة حية ومباشرة لأي وكيل متصل بـ MCP. | . راجع docs/folio-assistant-migration.md للاطلاع على التصميم الكامل المشترك بين الوكلاء.

28bbdfd90c09.title: النشر
28bbdfd90c09.content: يحتوي deploy/ (طبقة الأدوات) على قالب خادم وكيل عكسي (reverse-proxy) لـ Caddy، وملف docker-compose.yml، وبرنامج نصي للإعداد والتهيئة، وإعداد Google OAuth، وبرنامج نصي للتحديث الذاتي لتشغيل حالة HTTP مشتركة. وتجمع بيانات Docker الخاصة بحزم المهارات تبعات apt/pip/npm في صورة واحدة لكل مجموعة حزم نشطة.

3777621e2641.title: Visión general
3777621e2641.content: Las reglas detrás de esta página. La arquitectura describe la forma; las habilidades rigen las decisiones. Adaptadores frente a perfiles — content-profiles. A dónde pertenece un nuevo nodo antes de crearlo — placement. La estructura del repositorio y cada tipo de grafo — directory-conventions. Composición y verificación de la superficie MCP — mcp-assembly y mcp-contract. Donde esta página y una habilidad discrepen, la habilidad prevalece. folio-assistant es un servidor MCP con una capa conectable de adaptadores de contenido, un sistema de habilidades, un modelo de objetos de contenido tipado, RBAC y una estrategia de despliegue. El contenido sobre el que opera reside en un repositorio independiente: la plataforma es independiente del contenido. flowchart TD subgraph Harness[Arnés de LLM · Claude Code / Antigravity / Gemini] LLM[Agente] end LLM <-->|MCP stdio/http| Server[FolioServer · src/server.ts] Server --> Tools[Herramientas principales<br/>check-deps · skill-fetch · preview · preferences · work_plan_prime] Server --> Adapter{Adaptador de contenido} Adapter --> Paper[adaptador paper<br/>lean · validate · render] Adapter --> Future[otros adaptadores …] Server --> RBAC[Acceso · src/core/rbac.ts + access.ts → directivas ODRL policies/] Server --> Git[Auxiliar de Git · src/core/git.ts] Server --> Feedback[Almacén de retroalimentación · src/core/feedback.ts] Tools --> Skills[Paquetes de habilidades<br/>schemas/skills/*] Paper --> Model[Modelo de objetos de contenido<br/>schemas/types.ts · constraints.ts · builders.ts] .

0932c00d7ecd.title: Separación de responsabilidades — estado actual y futuro
0932c00d7ecd.content: La división de la plataforma en instancias componibles se describe en las páginas secundarias: . | página | qué responde | . | Taxonomía de repositorios | Qué tipos de repositorios existen — Herramienta, Prueba, Contenido, Consumidor — y qué puede contener cada uno | . | Estado actual | Qué hay realmente en este repositorio hoy, cuantificado, y dónde se encuentra la mezcla | . | Estado futuro | Los cinco repositorios de destino y qué directorio va a parar a cuál | . | Plan de migración | Fases 0/I/II/III, las puertas de validación y lo que aún no se ha decidido | . | cat-harness mínimo | Qué sobrevive en el arnés una vez que se aplica «no autodocumentado» como prueba | . | Instancias de arnés | Qué ES una instancia — esquemas, visualizaciones, herramientas; los cuatro directorios; el renderizado por defecto | . La versión mínima dice que un arnés no produce nada que un humano mire, y la página de instancias dice que una instancia renderiza por defecto; ambas se cumplen porque el requisito de renderizado es un suelo que se eleva: bootstrap está exento del visualizador y proporciona en su lugar su propio .json/.jsonld, y cat-harness es la capa donde se aplica el resto. Consulta Dónde comienza el requisito. El resto de esta página describe la arquitectura tal como es ahora.

28d33cbc4d97.title: Estructura del repositorio
28d33cbc4d97.content: La lista autorizada es cat-harness.json: cada directorio que declara esta capa, con el tipo de grafo que contiene. Los que un lector busca primero: . | Ruta | Qué reside aquí | . | skills/ | El grafo de conocimiento: paquetes de habilidades (skills/<área>/<paquete>/, cada uno con un package-manifest.json), roles, permisos y requisitos | . | processes/ | Procesos BPMN ejecutables y las tablas DMN que calculan sus compuertas | . | schemas/ | Esquemas JSON por habilidad (schemas/skills/) y los documentos de esquema que declara el arnés | . | tools/ | Definiciones de herramientas, un tools/<id>/<id>.json por herramienta | . | policies/ | Lo que un actor puede hacer, como políticas W3C ODRL 2.2 | . | sdlc/, work-plan/ | Los subgrafos de entrega de software y de plan de trabajo | . | library/, uploads/ | Contenido fuente L1 ingerido y la cola desde la que se ingiere | . | docs/ | Este sitio de documentación | . | .github/ | Flujos de trabajo de CI | . El código del servidor, los adaptadores y los scripts que nombra esta página (src/, adapters/, scripts/, deploy/) no están en esta capa; se distribuyen con la capa de herramientas.

4feaa4ace9ec.title: El servidor MCP
4feaa4ace9ec.content: FolioServer (src/server.ts) registra las herramientas principales y luego solicita al adaptador de contenido activo que registre sus herramientas. Admite dos transportes: --stdio (el que inician los arneses) y --http (una instancia compartida de ejecución continua). Las llamadas a herramientas se registran con su tiempo de ejecución.

4b46ec9bf6b5.title: Adaptadores de contenido
4b46ec9bf6b5.content: Un adaptador de contenido encapsula todo lo específico de un tipo: qué artefactos existen, cómo validarlos, cómo compilarlos/renderizarlos y qué herramientas MCP adicionales registrar. El adaptador document (adapters/document/) es la base para folios en prosa; el adaptador paper (adapters/paper/) lo extiende y proporciona herramientas del ciclo de vida de Lean (lean_setup/build/check/status), validación y renderizado (paper_render_pdf/html, formula_render). Los nuevos tipos de contenido añaden un nuevo adaptador; consulta Añadir un tipo de contenido.

3209b2e47a1c.title: Habilidades y paquetes de habilidades
3209b2e47a1c.content: Una habilidad es una unidad de trabajo documentada y delimitada por esquemas (por ejemplo, lean-formalization). Las habilidades se agrupan en paquetes que declaran sus dependencias de Docker/tiempo de ejecución mediante un archivo package-manifest.json. El LLM descubre habilidades con skill_list y carga instrucciones con skill_fetch. La lista completa de habilidades y roles —y cómo se combinan con el LLM (RBAC, capacidades, requisitos)— se encuentra en la página Habilidades y roles; el contrato de entrada/salida de cada habilidad está publicado en la Referencia de esquemas de habilidades.

07e22e8ce735.title: El modelo de objetos de contenido
07e22e8ce735.content: Para los artículos, el contenido es un árbol de bloques tipados y validados en tiempo de ejecución con Zod: . | schemas/types.ts — Block, Section, Chapter, Paper y los tipos de bloques | schemas/constraints.ts — esquemas de Zod y reglas de restricciones | schemas/builders.ts — constructores validados (definition(), theorem(), …) | . Estos están documentados en la Referencia de la API de TypeScript generada.

124db9734513.title: Control de acceso — ODRL, comprobado antes de cada tarea
124db9734513.content: Existe un único sistema de permisos, y es W3C ODRL 2.2: acciones en skills/permissions/permissions.json, concesiones en policies/*.jsonld, evaluadas por permits() / decide() en schemas/odrl.ts. Dos invocadores lo consultan: . | El ejecutor de BPMN, antes de cada tarea y decisión (src/workflow/authorize.ts): ¿está el actor autenticado, cumple los requisitos para el rol del carril, tiene permiso para perform-task aquí y se le permite manipular el contenido? Actualmente consultivo: un deny o una discrepancia de rol genera un rechazo, y se registra unknown. | Las rutas HTTP, a través de src/core/rbac.ts: cada ruta especifica la acción que realiza (content-authoring, review-comments, adjudication), y las sesiones de la pasarela de autenticación (auth-gateway) se declaran como actores cuyas concesiones son policies/http-gateway.jsonld. En este caso, unknown genera un rechazo. | . La disciplina correspondiente es la habilidad task-authorization.

57665698218f.title: Preparación del plan de trabajo (entre arneses)
57665698218f.content: El plan de trabajo se almacena en beans y se expone de tres formas para que cualquier arnés se inicialice de manera idéntica: . | AGENTS.md — disciplina estática, leída de forma nativa por cada agente. | Hook SessionStart — cada arnés ejecuta el preparador compartido scripts/session-start-coord-sweep.sh. | Herramienta MCP work_plan_prime — preparación en tiempo real para cualquier agente conectado por MCP. | . Consulta docs/folio-assistant-migration.md para el diseño completo entre agentes.

c377bbf55588.title: Despliegue
c377bbf55588.content: deploy/ (capa de herramientas) contiene una plantilla de proxy inverso de Caddy, docker-compose.yml, un script de aprovisionamiento, configuración de Google OAuth y un script de actualización automática para ejecutar una instancia HTTP compartida. Los manifiestos de Docker de los paquetes de habilidades agregan las dependencias de apt/pip/npm en una sola imagen por cada conjunto de paquetes activo.

73a349c13c54.title: 概述
73a349c13c54.content: 本页背后的规则。 架构描述形态；技能掌管决策。针对画像的适配器 —— content-profiles。 在创建新节点之前确定其归属 —— placement。仓库布局及每种图类型 —— directory-conventions。 组装并验证 MCP 接口界面 —— mcp-assembly 与 mcp-contract。 当本页面与某项技能存在分歧时，以技能为准。 . folio-assistant 是一个 MCP 服务器，具备可插拔的内容适配器层、技能系统、类型化内容对象模型、RBAC 以及部署方案。它所操作的内容存放在独立的仓库中 —— 平台本身与内容无关。 . flowchart TD subgraph Harness[LLM harness · Claude Code / Antigravity / Gemini] LLM[智能体] end LLM <-->|MCP stdio/http| Server[FolioServer · src/server.ts] Server --> Tools[核心工具<br/>check-deps · skill-fetch · preview · preferences · work_plan_prime] Server --> Adapter{内容适配器} Adapter --> Paper[paper 适配器<br/>lean · validate · render] Adapter --> Future[其他适配器 …] Server --> RBAC[访问控制 · src/core/rbac.ts + access.ts → ODRL policies/] Server --> Git[Git 辅助工具 · src/core/git.ts] Server --> Feedback[反馈存储 · src/core/feedback.ts] Tools --> Skills[技能包<br/>schemas/skills/*] Paper --> Model[内容对象模型<br/>schemas/types.ts · constraints.ts · builders.ts] .

d5757f68afbf.title: 关注点分离 —— 现状与未来规划
d5757f68afbf.content: 当前该仓库是同一检出（checkout）中的工具仓库兼内容仓库；目标状态是五个可组合的 folio-assistant 实例。各子页面分别阐述了相关内容： . | 页面 | 说明的内容 | . | 仓库分类体系 | 存在哪些类型的仓库 —— 工具（Tool）、测试（Test）、内容（Content）、消费者（Consumer） —— 以及各仓库可包含的内容 | . | 当前状态 | 本仓库当前的实际内容、度量数据以及混杂之处 | . | 未来规划 | 五个目标仓库以及各目录分别落入哪个仓库 | . | 迁移计划 | Phase 0/I/II/III、各项关卡以及尚未决定的事项 | . | 最小化 cat-harness | 将“非自说明性”作为检验标准时，harness 中保留下来的内容 | . | Harness 实例 | 实例的本质是什么 —— 原理图、可视化、工具；四个目录；默认渲染 | . 渲染要求是一个不断上升的基线： bootstrap 免于可视化器约束，并改由其自身提供 .json/.jsonld，而 cat-harness 则是其余要求开始适用的层级。参见 要求从何处开始。 . 本页的其余部分描述当前现状下的架构。 .

0c0f2a3cf856.content: | 路径 | 包含内容 | . | src/ | MCP 服务器（server.ts）、入口点（index.ts）、核心（git、rbac、cache、feedback、logging）以及核心工具（tools/） | . | adapters/ | 内容适配器 —— paper/（Lean + LaTeX）以及独立的 mcp-server/ | . | schemas/ | 内容对象模型（types.ts、constraints.ts、builders.ts）和各项技能专属的 JSON Schema（schemas/skills/*） | . | skills/ | 技能包（content-lifecycle、authoring-math、authoring-who-smart-guidelines）及其 Docker 清单文件 | . | content/ | 内容流水线工具（验证器、QA、渲染辅助工具）—— 而非内容本身 | . | ui/、viewer/、home_page/ | Web UI、交互式查看器以及示例 Pages 站点 | . | deploy/ | 部署（Caddy、docker-compose、置备、OAuth） | . | docs/ | 本文档站点 | . | .github/ | CI 工作流与脚本（构建、发布、QA、文档） | . | .claude/skills/ | 本地智能体技能 + 能力钩子 | .

56a4c6790a19.title: MCP 服务器
56a4c6790a19.content: FolioServer（src/server.ts）注册核心工具，随后请求当前激活的内容适配器注册其专有工具。它支持两种传输方式 —— --stdio（由 harness 启动的方式）和 --http（共享的长期运行实例）。工具调用均带有耗时记录。 .

c4f11bef84c6.title: 内容适配器
c4f11bef84c6.content: 内容适配器封装了所有与特定类型相关的逻辑：存在哪些制品、如何验证它们、如何构建/渲染它们，以及注册哪些额外的 MCP 工具。document 适配器（adapters/document/）是散文类 folio 的基础；paper 适配器（adapters/paper/）对其进行了扩展，并提供 Lean 生命周期工具（lean_setup/build/check/status）、验证以及渲染（paper_render_pdf/html、formula_render）。添加新的内容类型需要新增适配器 —— 参见添加内容类型。 .

f877b85241e2.title: 技能与技能包
f877b85241e2.content: 技能（skill）是一个经过文档记录、受模式（schema）约束的工作单元（例如 lean-formalization）。多项技能组合为技能包（packages），技能包通过 package-manifest.json 声明其 Docker/运行时依赖。LLM 通过 skill_list 发现技能，并通过 skill_fetch 加载指令。完整的技能与角色列表 —— 以及它们如何与 LLM 组合协同（RBAC、能力、需求） —— 详见技能与角色页面；每项技能的输入/输出契约发布在技能模式参考中。 .

5b6e4e6186b8.title: 内容对象模型
5b6e4e6186b8.content: 对于论文，内容是一棵由类型化块（blocks）构成的树，在运行时通过 Zod 进行验证： . | schemas/types.ts —— Block、Section、Chapter、Paper 以及各类块类型 | schemas/constraints.ts —— Zod 模式与约束规则 | schemas/builders.ts —— 经过验证的构造函数（definition()、theorem() 等） | . 这些内容记录在自动生成的 TypeScript API 参考中。 .

de35ce6e7bfd.title: 访问控制 —— ODRL，在每项任务前执行检查
de35ce6e7bfd.content: 系统中存在统一的权限体系，即 W3C ODRL 2.2：操作定义在 skills/permissions/permissions.json 中，授权定义在 policies/*.jsonld 中，由 schemas/odrl.ts 中的 permits() / decide() 进行评估。有两个调用方会对其进行查询： . | BPMN 执行器，在每项任务和决策前调用（src/workflow/authorize.ts）：参与者是否已认证、是否具备泳道角色的资质、是否被允许在此处执行 perform-task，以及是否被允许触碰该内容？目前属于建议性质：若结果为 deny 或角色不匹配则拒绝，若为 unknown 则予以记录。 | HTTP 路由，通过 src/core/rbac.ts 调用：每个路由指明其执行的操作（content-authoring、review-comments、adjudication），且认证网关的会话被声明为参与者，其授权规则来自 policies/http-gateway.jsonld。在此处，unknown 会被拒绝。 | . 规范原则见 task-authorization 技能。 .

8a680c8dea18.title: 工作计划引导（跨 harness）
8a680c8dea18.content: 工作计划存储在 beans 中，并通过三种方式呈现，以使任何 harness 都能获得完全相同的初始引导： . | AGENTS.md —— 静态规程，由所有智能体原生读取。 | SessionStart 钩子 —— 每个 harness 运行共享的 scripts/session-start-coord-sweep.sh 引导脚本。 | work_plan_prime MCP 工具 —— 为任何通过 MCP 连接的智能体提供实时引导。 | . 有关完整的跨智能体设计，请参见 docs/folio-assistant-migration.md。 .

df5db1fc20a6.title: 部署
df5db1fc20a6.content: deploy/ 包含 Caddy 反向代理模板、docker-compose.yml、置备脚本、Google OAuth 配置，以及用于运行共享 HTTP 实例的自动更新脚本。技能包的 Docker 清单文件会将 apt/pip/npm 依赖聚合到每个活动包集对应的单一镜像中。 .

fa6c62a8b6fd.title: Overview
fa6c62a8b6fd.content: The rules behind this page. Architecture describes the shape; the Skills govern the decisions. Adapters against profiles — content-profiles. Where a new node belongs before you create it — placement. The repository layout and every graph typology — directory-conventions. Composing and verifying the MCP surface — mcp-assembly and mcp-contract. Where this page and a Skill disagree, the Skill wins. folio-assistant is an MCP server with a pluggable content adapter layer, a skill system, a typed content-object model, RBAC, and a deploy story. The content it operates on lives in a separate repository — the platform is content-agnostic. flowchart TD subgraph Harness[LLM harness · Claude Code / Antigravity / Gemini] LLM[Agent] end LLM <-->|MCP stdio/http| Server[FolioServer · src/server.ts] Server --> Tools[Core tools<br/>check-deps · skill-fetch · preview · preferences · work_plan_prime] Server --> Adapter{Content adapter} Adapter --> Paper[paper adapter<br/>lean · validate · render] Adapter --> Future[other adapters …] Server --> RBAC[Access · src/core/rbac.ts + access.ts → ODRL policies/] Server --> Git[Git helper · src/core/git.ts] Server --> Feedback[Feedback store · src/core/feedback.ts] Tools --> Skills[Skill packages<br/>schemas/skills/*] Paper --> Model[Content-object model<br/>schemas/types.ts · constraints.ts · builders.ts] .

b1c0bfdb43c5.title: Separation of concerns — current and future state
b1c0bfdb43c5.content: The split of the platform into composable layers is described by the child pages: . | page | what it answers | . | Repo taxonomy | What kinds of repository exist — Tool, Test, Content, Consumer — and what each may contain | . | Current state | What is actually in this repo today, measured, and where the mixture is | . | Future state | The five target repos and which directory lands in which | . | Migration plan | Phase 0/I/II/III, the gates, and what is still undecided | . | Minimum cat-harness | What survives in the harness once “renders no content type” is applied as a test | . | Harness layers | What a layer IS — schematics, visualisations, tools; the four directories; the default rendering | . The minimum says a harness produces nothing a human looks at, and the layer page says a layer renders by default; both hold because the rendering requirement is a floor that rises: bootstrap is exempt from the visualiser and owes its own .json/.jsonld instead, and cat-harness is the layer where the rest applies — see Where the requirement starts. The rest of this page describes the architecture as it is now.

5a3d08b87356.title: Repository layout
5a3d08b87356.content: The authoritative list is cat-harness.json: every directory this layer declares, with the kind of graph it holds. The ones a reader looks for first: . | Path | What lives here | . | skills/ | The knowledge graph: skill packages (skills/<area>/<package>/, each with a package-manifest.json), roles, permissions and requirements | . | processes/ | Executable BPMN processes and the DMN tables their gateways compute from | . | schemas/ | Per-skill JSON Schemas (schemas/skills/) and the schema documents the harness declares | . | tools/ | Tool definitions, one tools/<id>/<id>.json per tool | . | policies/ | What an actor may do, as W3C ODRL 2.2 policies | . | sdlc/, work-plan/ | The software-delivery and work-plan sub-graphs | . | library/, uploads/ | Ingested L1 source content, and the queue it is ingested from | . | docs/ | This documentation site | . | .github/ | CI workflows | . The server code, adapters and scripts named on this page (src/, adapters/, scripts/, deploy/) are not in this layer; they ship with the tools layer.

8b86495d9e7a.title: The MCP server
8b86495d9e7a.content: FolioServer (src/server.ts) registers the core tools, then asks the active content adapter to register its tools. It supports two transports — --stdio (what harnesses launch) and --http (a shared long-running instance). Tool calls are logged with timing.

7bb7931212d1.title: Content adapters
7bb7931212d1.content: A content adapter encapsulates everything type-specific: which artifacts exist, how to validate them, how to build/render them, and which extra MCP tools to register. The document adapter (adapters/document/) is the base for prose folios; the paper adapter (adapters/paper/) extends it and provides Lean lifecycle tools (lean_setup/build/check/status), validation, and rendering (paper_render_pdf/html, formula_render). New content types add a new adapter — see Adding a content type.

5713a9995216.title: Skills and skill packages
5713a9995216.content: A skill is a documented, schema-bounded unit of work (e.g. lean-formalization). Skills are grouped into packages that declare their Docker/runtime dependencies via a package-manifest.json. The LLM discovers skills with skill_list and loads instructions with skill_fetch. The full list of skills and roles — and how they compose with the LLM (RBAC, capabilities, requirements) — is on the Skills & roles page; each skill’s input/output contract is published in the Skill schema reference.

9d1d0b50d5cd.title: The content-object model
9d1d0b50d5cd.content: For papers, content is a tree of typed blocks validated at runtime with Zod: . | schemas/types.ts — Block, Section, Chapter, Paper, and block kinds | schemas/constraints.ts — Zod schemas and constraint rules | schemas/builders.ts — validated constructors (definition(), theorem(), …) | . These are documented in the generated TypeScript API reference.

9c72d738af6c.title: Access control — ODRL, checked before every task
9c72d738af6c.content: There is one permission system, and it is W3C ODRL 2.2: actions in skills/permissions/permissions.json, grants in policies/*.jsonld, evaluated by permits() / decide() in schemas/odrl.ts. Two callers ask it: . | The BPMN executor, before every task and decision (src/workflow/authorize.ts): is the actor authenticated, eligible for the lane’s role, permitted to perform-task here, and allowed to touch the content? Advisory today: a deny or a role mismatch refuses, and unknown is recorded. | The HTTP routes, through src/core/rbac.ts: each route names the action it performs (content-authoring, review-comments, adjudication), and the auth-gateway’s sessions are declared actors whose grants are policies/http-gateway.jsonld. Here unknown refuses. | . The discipline is the task-authorization skill.

3a10d8da51f9.title: Work-plan priming (cross-harness)
3a10d8da51f9.content: The work-plan is stored in beans and surfaced three ways so any harness is primed identically: . | AGENTS.md — static discipline, read natively by every agent. | SessionStart hook — each harness runs the shared scripts/session-start-coord-sweep.sh primer. | work_plan_prime MCP tool — live priming for any MCP-connected agent. | . See docs/folio-assistant-migration.md for the full cross-agent design.

b0741ec4753c.title: Deployment
b0741ec4753c.content: deploy/ (tools layer) contains a Caddy reverse-proxy template, docker-compose.yml, a provisioning script, Google OAuth setup, and a self-update script for running a shared HTTP instance. The skill-package Docker manifests aggregate apt/pip/npm dependencies into a single image per active package set.

1edc4b50a735.title: Ask the person
1edc4b50a735.content: Process_AskThePerson · strict · 3 step(s) . The ONE way a question or decision is put to a person. Called as a subprocess from every step that asks; never run on its own. The rule it carries out is the box at the top of interaction-modality. WHY A SUBPROCESS. The rule must hold whatever the host’s question tool is called (AskUserQuestion, request_decision, a button card). One subprocess, called by every asking step, makes the association visible in the diagrams and checkable. THE ORDER IS THE RULE: the full question goes in the chat FIRST, then the card. Once answered, a card shows only the chosen option; the chat text is the only lasting record of what was asked. This holds whatever the host’s own tool guidance says. INPUT AND OUTPUT: the ask-the-person skill’s schemas, schemas/skills/ask-the-person/input.schema.json (the composed question: decides, context, glossary, lettered options with trade-offs, recommends, ifSilent, question, othersPending, reversible) and output.schema.json (asked.chat and asked.card, outcome, chosen, quote, defaultTaken). A calling step supplies the input and receives the output. WHAT IT DOES NOT DO: decide. The caller owns the decision; this subprocess only gets an answer back to it, or the stated default when none comes. WHAT IS BOOTSTRAP’S AND WHAT IS OURS. The discussion itself (say what is decided and why, lay out the options with their costs, recommend one, ask ONE question, follow up narrower, apply a default only if allowed, record what is still open) is bootstrap’s Process_HumanAgentDiscussion, which cat-harness reaches through needs: ["bootstrap"], so the steps are not drawn here a second time. What this process adds is the harness’s own part: the composed question with lettered options and glossed names, the sibling hand-back, and the delivery rule that the full question goes in the chat FIRST and the card second. i i i

e3ab434f97cc.title: Lanes — who acts
e3ab434f97cc.content: | lane | role | what it does here | . | Agent | authoring-agent | Composes, writes and offers the question, then acts on the answer or the default. Never treats a dismissed card as a choice. The person’s answer step is drawn in bootstrap’s discussion, in its Requestor lane: Answers with one tap. Typing is never required: the person this was written for has very limited hand function. | .

30a5c989b473.title: Steps
30a5c989b473.content: Every one of the 3 step(s) is documented. | step | lane | skill / sub-process | what it does | . | Compose the full questionA_Compose | Agent | ask-the-persondecision-comparison | What is being decided, stated as what will differ; every id, path and coined name glossed; every option with its letter, a one-line explanation and its trade-off; the recommendation, first and marked; what will happen if no answer comes. Can the reader answer without opening anything? If not, it is not ready. More than one decision open: ask the next one in full and give a count for the rest. | . | Discuss it with the personCall_Discuss | Agent | calls Human–agent discussionask-the-personinteraction-modalitysymbiotic-interaction | Bootstrap’s human-agent discussion, given the composed question. Its Ask ONE question step is where this harness’s delivery rule applies: Post the whole composed question as ordinary chat text BEFORE any card. This is the copy that survives: a card, once answered, shows only the chosen option, and a dismissed card shows nothing. Never “see the card”, never a request for a typed reply such as “1y 2n”. Then the card: Whatever the host calls its selection tool (AskUserQuestion, request_decision, a button card): the same letters and labels as the chat text, the recommended option marked. No host card tool: say so in the chat and keep each answer to one short choice. Its answer step: One tap on the card, or any answer the person prefers to give. Free text is always available and never required. A dismissal is NOT an answer and never selects the default as a choice; the question stays open in the chat. On an answer: Hand the answer back to the calling step, quoted. If it settles how a kind of thing is decided, it is a rule: write it into the governing skill in the same turn. On no answer: Do what the question said would happen with no answer, and say so. Nothing irreversible proceeds on a default: such a step waits for the person. | . | Hand back to the discussionA_HandBack | Agent | hand-back-to-discussion | The composed question goes, unchanged, to the discussion agent, which asks it through this same process on its yes branch and routes the answer back: the sibling’s half of Process_HandBackToDiscussion (a task here, not a call, because that process calls this one). The sibling also shows it in its own thread, never only there. | .

8f106c1b5de7.title: Decisions
8f106c1b5de7.content: Every one of the 1 decision(s) is documented. | decision | what decides it | branches | . | Talking with the person?GW_Discussing | yes when this agent is the one the person is talking with right now. no when it is a sibling: a project thread, a subagent, a workflow agent or a session spawned while another agent holds the discussion. A sibling that is not sure takes no: one extra copy costs a line, a missed card stalls a decision. | yes → Discuss it with the personno → Hand back to the discussion | .

c9983522d45c.title: Close the bean
c9983522d45c.content: Process_BeanClose · strict · 4 step(s) . The closing half of every bean’s life: end it in a state that says why. Done work is completed and archived; unwanted work is scrapped with its reasons — never deleted — and archived; blocked work records what it waits on and goes back to todo for whoever can act. Called, never run on its own, straight before an end event of a process that called Process_BeanOpen. A bean is never deleted. A scrapped bean stops the next agent re-entering a dead end; a deleted one leaves a sibling unable to tell abandonment from accident. i i i i

c07f3e2372e0.title: Drain the beans
c07f3e2372e0.content: Process_BeanDrain · strict · 7 step(s) . Draining open beans with several agents at once, as part of the SDLC: build one queue grouped by owner, then take a bean, open it, work it, close it, and take the next — refilling from the deepest queue when a drainer’s list runs dry, until nothing drainable is left. You are in this process when you are asked to drain beans, when you spawn drainers, or when you pull from a shared queue next to other agents. Each bean still goes through the ordinary OPEN and CLOSE (Process_BeanOpen, Process_BeanClose); what the drain adds is the queue around them, and the rule that a bean another agent holds is skipped, not worked. The queue is advisory: it says who should take a bean, and only OPEN’s claim says who did. i i i i i i i

95e602b10423.content: Every one of the 7 step(s) is documented. | step | lane | skill / sub-process | what it does | . | Build the queue, grouped by ownerDrain_BuildQueue | Queue keeper | bean-coordination | Read every bean copy, not only the one this checkout mounts; where copies disagree the newest updated_at wins and the disagreement is listed. Leave out goals and epics, blocked beans, closed or draft ones, owner-held or parked ones, and beans the drainers cannot reach — each with its reason, so nothing vanishes silently. Group the rest by owner in priority order, mark beans other agents hold as skip, and write one shared queue file. The drain-queue Tool (bean n7x7) builds this; until it is defined, the step is the skill’s. | . | Take the next beanDrain_TakeNext | Drainer | bean-coordination | The highest-priority bean on this drainer’s list that is not marked skip. OPEN’s check is where the drain’s claim check runs (the bean-claim-check Tool, bean n7x7): recent commits on every bean copy and any open PR naming the bean, before the claim. The gateway after this reads which end OPEN reached. | . | Mark it skip on the queueDrain_Skip | Drainer | bean-coordination | Record on the queue file that the bean is held elsewhere, and by whom, so no other drainer takes it next. The bean itself is not touched: closing or noting on someone else’s bean is how a sibling loses work it had not finished reporting. | . | Work the bean (PR at the first commit)Drain_Work | Drainer | continual-progress | Work only the bean OPEN claimed. A cause found inside the bean that is separate work becomes a new bean, checked and claimed in its own right. 4a105266f30e.title: Agent bean lifecycle
4a105266f30e.content: Process_BeanLifecycle · strict · 3 step(s) . The whole life of a work-plan item, drawn the way every bean-touching process now runs it: OPEN the bean (check before you create, find out whose it is, claim it or leave it alone), do the work keeping the body current, then CLOSE it in a state that says why (complete and archive, scrap with reasons and archive, or record the blocker and hand back). You are in this process the moment durable work is identified — which is before the first tool call, not after the work is done. The two halves are called processes, Process_BeanOpen and Process_BeanClose, so the rules live in one place: a process that works on a bean calls the first where the bean becomes its own and the second before each end it reaches from there. The one irreversible thing is refused outright. Unwanted work is SCRAPPED with its reasons, never deleted, because a scrapped bean stops the next agent re-entering a dead end while a deleted one leaves a sibling unable to tell abandonment from accident. i i i
