463794f34ef5.doc: Forced Along a BPMN vs Managing It — Harness Built, No Model Run Yet
463794f34ef5.title: 3. What the Simulated Run Does and Does Not Establish
463794f34ef5.content: It establishes properties of the engine and the runner, which are deterministic and would hold for any agent: . | The token machine refuses each scripted violation. complete() in src/workflow/instance.ts raised WorkflowError on every scripted shortcut in temptation cases 5–8 (out-of-order step, hand-asserted DMN outcome, unexpanded CallActivity, skipped Task_ResolveReach with a hand-picked route), 20 times in all, and enabled() dropped the child-only skills on leaving Process_QaReportSigning (case 10). This is a test of the engine, and it passed. | The prompt the forced arm would send is about 31× smaller per turn. The forced arm’s per-turn payload (enabled step plus its TaskContext) averages about 455 estimated tokens; the self-managed payload (the parent diagram, every called diagram, DMN tables and role closure) about 14,162. That is a static property of the two prompt shapes, measured with a byte-count estimate. It is not a cost a model incurred, and it leaves out everything a real run adds: reasoning output, retries a model chooses to make, and caching. | The two-hash recording works (§1). | . It does not establish anything about model behaviour: . | Whether a model handed the whole diagram skips steps, hand-picks gateway outcomes, bypasses subprocesses or leaks context — and how often. The 4 of 5 temptation failures in Arm 2 are the 4 violations the bank’s author wrote in. | Whether a model under the forced arm recovers after a refusal, and in how many turns. In this run the runner, not an agent, picked the recovery step. | Time or compute. The wall times are a fraction of a millisecond per runner turn. | . A gate that checks only the terminal event cannot tell cases 5, 7 and 8 apart from case 1 in Arm 2: that observation is about the gate and holds whatever produced the path. Whether a real model produces such paths is the open question.

1e44584313c9.doc: Forced Along a BPMN vs Managing It — Harness Built, No Model Run Yet
1e44584313c9.title: 4. What Is Confounded Once a Model Is Run
1e44584313c9.content: Even a run with a real model compares two orchestration harnesses on one diagram pair and one task bank; it must not be cited as a model-vs-model comparison. Three factors are structurally confounded between the arms: . | Control-flow enforcement is confounded with per-turn prompt length (Levy et al., arXiv:2402.14848). Arm 1 (forced) changes two things at once relative to Arm 2 (self-managed): . | the token machine (complete()) refuses out-of-order steps, hand-picked DMN outcomes, and unexpanded call activities; and | enabled() slices the prompt payload at each turn down to the single enabled node and its lane/subprocess TaskContext (about 455 vs 14,162 estimated prompt tokens per turn). Because reasoning performance degrades with input context length even well inside nominal context windows (Levy, Jacoby & Goldberg 2024, prior-art.md), any difference in path adherence a live run finds would combine mechanical refusal of invalid transitions with shorter per-step context. Separating the two would need a third arm (the full diagram on every turn with complete() refusals, or one step’s prose without them). | . | Turn count and refusal retries depend on the agent’s shortcut rate. In Arm 1, every attempted shortcut becomes an extra turn (refusalRetries). Against a disciplined agent refusalRetries is 0 and Arm 1 takes one fewer turn per case than Arm 2 (which spends an initial planning turn over the full diagram); against one that keeps guessing unenabled nodes, Arm 1’s turns and tokens grow with the retry cap. | Diagram, engine, and benchmark-mode specificity. Any numbers are properties of src/workflow/instance.ts, test-plan-execution.bpmn and the diagrams it calls, bpmn-forced-vs-managed-bank.json and, once run, the model. Per benchmarking-mode, benchmark outputs are assertions about the harness/runner configuration rather than facts about a folio, so eval-bpmn-forced-vs-managed.ts guards its output path with assertBenchmarkOutputPath and writes only to build/benchmarks/bpmn-forced-vs-managed/. | .

3dfa2f9f8a77.doc: Forced Along a BPMN vs Managing It — Harness Built, No Model Run Yet
3dfa2f9f8a77.title: 5. What Is Needed to Answer the Question
3dfa2f9f8a77.content: . | Replace the script with a model. At each turn, send the payload the runner already builds (turnPromptPayload in the forced arm, stepPrompt in the self-managed arm) to a model and parse its reply as the proposed step, instead of reading agentProposal.proposedSteps. In the forced arm the model, not the runner, must choose the step after a refusal. | Record what the model reports. Take prompt and completion tokens from the API’s usage fields and time the calls; add the model id and sampling settings to the process basis. | Repeat. One run per case gives no spread. Several runs per case per arm, reported with their variation, are the minimum before any rate is quoted. | . Until then the question — do behaviour outcomes change, and how much time and compute does determinism cost — is unanswered.

8f679a5df4cc.doc: The cache process: restore and save every cache a run can use
8f679a5df4cc.title: The cache process: restore and save every cache a run can use
8f679a5df4cc.content: Process_Cache · advisory · 9 step(s) . One optional process for every cache in the harness, used by render, CI, publish and every other consumer, whose components run in parallel where they are independent and in order where they are not. The rule every component follows is the skill cache-first-ci: a step is a pure function of its inputs; the key is DERIVED from them (cache:key, a lock digest, key.sh), never hand-listed; on a hit restore and skip, on a miss build and save; the full set still runs on main and nightly. OPTIONAL, AND SKIPPING IS ALWAYS CORRECT. Every consumer — the render pipeline, the code-quality gates, feature staging and the preview, publish, the docs-site publish, the merge train, and a committer’s local mount — may call it as a call activity, once with phase restore before its own work and once with phase save after that work came back green. A consumer that does not call it, or a run that cannot reach a store, simply builds: every component’s miss is the consumer doing its own work, so this process can cost a run time, never correctness. PARALLEL WHERE INDEPENDENT, IN ORDER WHERE NOT. The layers come first, because every other component reads mounted content. Then the prepared image and node_modules, the bun/pip downloads, the gate results and the generated sets restore side by side. Then the compiled Lean artefacts. Then the render seed (derive:publish’s writer records) and the FHIR IG ASTs side by side; the IG ASTs in their own lane, as the FHIR IG layer’s Process_IgAstCache, whose “valid for this commit?” is the component’s verify and whose AST refresh is its save. The Jekyll cache is last, because it caches the rendering of what the rest produce. ONLY WHAT THE TARGET NEEDS, ONLY WHAT IS STALE (owner, 2026-11-05: “not all rendering/CI/merge processes need all caches. be optimal in what needs caching” and “… be optimal in which caches need to be updated to perform a specific render”). A component runs only when the plan (cache:plan, the first gateway) marks it needed for this target; a component the target does not read is passed through untouched, neither restored nor refreshed. A needed component that is fresh is RESTORED, never rebuilt. A needed component that is stale, or whose staleness cannot be determined, is REFRESHED, incrementally where its node says so (the changed writers, the changed Lean modules over the restored .oleans, the IG AST delta, the moved layers), never wholesale when a delta is valid. A stale component no target here needs is left for the next target that needs it, or for main’s run. The plan and what actually happened are both reported (cached-step phase report), and the daily report flags a component restored and never read. EACH COMPONENT, BOTH PHASES. Restore: look up the derived key, verify the entry by its trust class — (a) against a reference derived from THIS tree, so a bad entry is only a miss; (a′) a bundle’s own manifest plus a source rule; (b) a committer’s verdict, honoured then re-verified off the critical path; (c) main-only entries, by exact key — and report hit, warm or miss with why. Save: only after the consumer’s work is green, only from main or into the run’s own ref scope, never from pull_request_target. Each component is a cache node in the knowledge graph (key recipe, derived inputs, producer, consumers, trust class, location, budget), and the cache viewer compares its current key with the key today’s pins imply, so staleness is computed, never claimed. i i i i i i i i i

A committer’s local gate record is class (b): honoured on the critical path, then re-verified off it. SAVE: main only (class c for CI’s records). Owner role: the generated-sets session (CI speed 10); the preview’s copy, the preview session (CI speed 2). cache nodes: qa-working-copy, publish-pages. 8484ff5c1297.title: What “renders no content type” constrains
8484ff5c1297.content: The harness documents itself, but it renders no content type. Its own docs/ is published as its site, so a reader can learn how the harness works. The webpage content type and every renderer of a content type belong to the content core. That yields a one-line admission test for every candidate: . If it renders a content type, it is not the harness. The webpage content type, the sticky-note Todo rendering, the QR code, the audit-sidecar iconography — all present a folio’s content to a reader, so all belong to the content core or folio-assistant-core-tools. What survives in the harness is the part with no pixels: schemas, process definitions, and skills that tell an agent how to behave. The test is falsifiable: if cat-harness ends up with dozens of skills and no crisp line against core, the test has not constrained anything.

3d4e2ba71d65.title: cat-harness — the minimum
3d4e2ba71d65.content: Schemas (.ts, minimal) . The harness owns the vocabulary of work, not of content. | schema | why the harness | . | Skill | what an actor knows how to do | . | Tool | how work actually gets done; a KG node, not a shell string | . | Task | the unit assigned to an actor in a swimlane | . | Actor / Role | who may do what — RBAC | . | Process (BPMN) / Decision (DMN) | the deterministic workflow itself | . | Todo | user/agent workflow state | . | Bean | the agent work plan; a workflow-state format with no schema cannot be validated, carry a QA sidecar, or be a KG node | . | CatHarness declaration | which directories a layer scans, and each one’s graph typology | . | Content (abstract) | the base only: identity, label, provenance. No block kinds, no profiles. | . Skills — 24: 21 from folio-core, plus 3 written for MCP projection . Classified by reading each skill’s description, not its filename. | skill | why the harness | . | bean-coordination | cross-session claim discipline | . | todo-manager | work-plan maintenance: the CLI, the STRICT create-check, coordination | . | opening-brief | brief a work item or topic before touching anything | . | turn-reporting | say which work item you are on, every turn | . | pending-show | read-only view of session pending work | . | session-intent | session-start intent, session-end results | . | continual-progress | PR from the first commit; visibility of in-flight work | . | coordinate | multi-PR coordination toward a shared goal | . | pickup | resume an existing open PR | . | watch | background-watch a branch or PR | . | prepare-merge-auto | the merge pipeline as a process | . | idle-backlog | what an agent does while blocked | . | dispatch-agent | background sub-agents — the swarm entry point | . | interaction-modality | how to talk to the person before deciding what to say | . | symbiotic-interaction | the three epistemic registers of author input | . | crdm-detect | feature-request detection | . | crdm-requirements-workflow | the six-phase process | . | getting-started | folio-creation triage | . | repo-conversion | laying the harness over an existing repo — bootstrap | . | integration-watcher (abstract parent only) | the shared watcher mechanics; the concrete watchers are downstream | . | directory-conventions | the declaration and its graph typologies | . | process-state | reading a BPMN swimlane as process state for the role you are playing, and recovering when you find yourself outside it | . | skills-and-tools | the skill/Tool separation — the SOP every other skill follows | . | mcp-projection (new) | mapping a Tool node onto the MCP standard — how an agent stands a service up from a CLI tool | . | mcp-assembly (new) | composing many Tools into one service: naming, collisions, prefixes, versioning | . | mcp-contract (new) | verifying a served tool still matches the node it was projected from | . The three mcp-* skills are new writing, not moves — nothing in folio-core covered projection. Where they live now is in Skill groups. Documentation — the smallest set . Prose an agent reads, not pages a reader browses: . | the data models above, described as one deterministic workflow: Actors with Skills work Tasks in a Business Process, assigned by swimlane role; | context-handling expectations, and work item info/workflow/management; | a minimal coding policy; | how Tools are made available in shell/CLI and optionally as MCP, and how a Task’s I/O corresponds to a Tool’s inputs and outputs. | . Tools — what the harness itself depends on . The harness holds work items and nothing else as a dependency — a statement about what must be installed, not about how many Tool nodes exist. Its own work needs these nodes: . | Tool node | satisfies | invocation | . | beans-cli | the six work-plan skills | shell — installed by scripts/install-beans.sh | . | beans-manual | the same six | shell — scripts/beans-fallback.ts, or a hand edit of the front matter | . | github | the four PR-choreography skills | shell — gh, or the REST call it wraps | . | pages-publish | kg-export | shell — push a directory to the gh-pages branch | . Two work items nodes, not one. The CLI is absent from a fresh container, and an agent that knows only the CLI reads the plan and touches nothing. The fallback is a Tool of equal standing, which forces the skill to say when to reach for it. The harness documents itself, and pages-publish also publishes its graph as data. Its docs/ is rendered as its own site; no content type’s renderer is in the harness. Its knowledge graph is published as data as well: kg-export serializes it to one JSON document and this Tool puts the document somewhere. A GitLab Pages or object-store node can satisfy the same skill. The Tool KG stays in the harness: that is what makes the harness bootstrappable — it describes its own tools in its own vocabulary, without a content layer’s renderer or a server.

023a75f6ea1e.title: The Tools schema — built, and where the strawperson bent
023a75f6ea1e.content: The shipped schema is schemas/tools/harness-tools.ts in the tools layer, the Tool nodes are tools/<id>/<id>.json, and bun run cat check:tools gates them in CI. It differs from the strawperson below in five ways: . | invoke.manual exists: editing a work item’s front matter by hand is a real mechanism with equal standing to the CLI, and must not look like an unfinished record. | install.none exists for the same reason: “nothing to install” and “not filled in” must not render identically. | invoke must carry an arm the harness can run. A Tool whose only invocation is invoke.mcp is rejected at parse time, because it is unusable by the layer that defines it and would make a projector emit a server that proxies itself. | io.*.schema is an absolute IRI into a published $defs document, because an unresolvable reference is the failure the io block exists to prevent. | satisfies must be non-empty, and check:tools resolves the names — a schema cannot, because it does not read the tree, and an unchecked list is a declared-but-absent edge that lets a consumer scan nothing and report a clean run. | .

a5275ee5e55b.title: Strawperson: the Tools-repo schema
a5275ee5e55b.content: The shape, written in Zod — the authoritative form, with the TypeScript type inferred from it so there is one definition and not two that can drift: . // schemas/tool.ts export const ToolDefinitionSchema = z.object({ id: z.string(), // stable KG node id title: z.string(), summary: z.string(), /** How to obtain it. */ install: z.object({ cli: z.string().optional(), container: z.string().optional(), service: z.string().optional(), }), /** How to run it, per environment. */ invoke: z.object({ shell: z.string().optional(), mcp: z.object({ tool: z.string() }).optional(), container: z.string().optional(), }), /** The contract a Task binds against — the 16:28 requirement. */ io: z.object({ inputs: z.array(z.object({ name: z.string(), schema: z.string(), required: z.boolean(), })), outputs: z.array(z.object({ name: z.string(), schema: z.string(), })), }), /** Skills this tool can satisfy. One skill may have several tools. */ satisfies: z.array(z.string()), requires: z.object({ os: z.array(z.string()).optional(), runtime: z.array(z.string()).optional(), network: z.boolean().optional(), }).optional(), }); export type ToolDefinition = z.infer<typeof ToolDefinitionSchema>; . The io block is the part that earns its keep: it lets a Task’s inputs and outputs be checked against the Tool that will execute it. Carrying it — authored once in Zod, rendered downstream . The .ts Zod schema is authoritative, and downstream renderings are generated from it — JSON-LD and JSON Schema to begin with. Every schema in the harness is defined this way. schemas/tool.ts ← AUTHORITATIVE. Zod + the inferred TS type. │ ├─→ schemas/generated/Tool.schema.json JSON Schema (validation, editors) └─→ kg/tools/<id>.jsonld JSON-LD (KG node, queryable) . Both renderings are derived artefacts: regenerate, never hand-edit, as docs/reference/skills/ and docs/reference/skill-instructions/ are treated. The options . |   | Zod .ts, rendered down | JSON-LD authored | TS, no renderings | Skill front-matter | . | shape | one Zod schema; per-tool instances validated against it | one hand-written .jsonld per tool | one .ts per tool, and nothing else | YAML block in the skill .md | . | author-time checking | yes | no — a typo is a runtime discovery | yes | no | . | KG node | yes, generated | yes, natively | no — needs a projection nobody wrote | no — unqueryable without parsing Markdown | . | readable without a TS toolchain | yes, via the renderings | yes | no | no | . | number of truths | one | one | one | one | . | verdict | decided | superseded | insufficient | do not | . | A hand-authored JSON-LD node is unchecked until CI runs. With Zod as the type, a malformed tool definition fails at tsc, in the editor, before it is committed; validation after the fact catches the same error later, and only if CI runs. | Authoring the rendering and validating backwards would be a fourth pattern. Zod → JSON Schema, Zod → docs and Zod → JSON-LD all run the other way. | Nothing language-agnostic is lost. A shell or Python consumer reads the generated JSON-LD and JSON Schema as well as a hand-authored one. | Front-matter in the skill is rejected: it contradicts the rule that code belongs in tools rather than skills, and it caps the model at one tool per skill. | . What “as many renderings as make sense” means in practice . A rendering earns its place when a real consumer cannot read the ones that exist: JSON Schema because editors and validators speak it, JSON-LD because the KG query path does. A third — SHACL, an OpenAPI fragment, Turtle — is added when something needs it, not in anticipation, because each one is another file to regenerate and another chance for a stale artefact to be read as current. A rendering is never the place a fix lands. If a generated Tool.schema.json is wrong, the Zod schema is wrong; edit that and regenerate. A --check mode in CI (as gen-skill-docs.ts --check uses) enforces it.

6a91ea500fc4.title: User todo management — proposals
6a91ea500fc4.content: . | Todo and Work item are the same object at different audiences. A work item is agent work-plan state; a Todo note is a user-authored sticky. Proposal: one schema with an audience discriminator (agent | human), and the work item store a serialisation of it — two schemas give two answers to “what is outstanding”. | Hierarchy: child Todos and sub-beans for parallel work need parent?: string plus an ordering key. | Timed blocking: blockedOn?: { what, since, expires, handoff }, so an expired block becomes a signal and a second agent knows what it inherits. | The rendering is core’s, the state is the harness’s. Sticky-note styling, drag/resize and position metadata belong in folio-assistant-core-tools; the Todo schema stays in the harness, so a headless agent can read and write Todos with no renderer present. | .

1c4bb13a34a7.title: The forge is isolated at the Tool layer, not in a repository
1c4bb13a34a7.content: All the PR-choreography skills — prepare-merge-auto, pickup, watch, coordinate — stay in cat-harness. There is no cat-harness-github repository. The skills are forge-neutral prose; only their invocations (mcp__github__*, gh pr, gh api) are not, and those are a few dozen lines. A repository boundary is the most expensive cut available, and it would separate things that are not separable at that grain. Isolate at the Tool layer instead. A skill states the capability generically; Tool nodes, one per forge operation, carry the invocations and name the skills they satisfy. Adding GitLab is more Tool nodes against the same skills — not a repository, not a fork, not a rewrite. The SOP is skills-and-tools; the Tool schema’s satisfies field is exactly this edge. repo-conversion is not merged into getting-started, nor symbiotic-interaction into interaction-modality: both pairs overlap, but the merge has no architectural consequence. No MCP in the harness — but the harness knows how to emit one . cat-harness assumes no MCP server. Everything it needs is files in declared directories, readable with a filesystem and <name>.json alone. ToolDefinition.invoke carries mcp as one optional arm beside shell and container, and the harness relies on shell. MCP is an output of this harness, not an input to it. The three mcp-* skills are how an agent takes a Tool node describing a CLI and produces a working MCP service from it. An MCP tool declaration is a name, a description and a JSON Schema for its input; io.inputs/io.outputs are already the I/O contract and invoke.shell the mechanism, so the projection is a rename, not a translation. A layer with no server loses a transport, not a capability — which is what keeps sovereign-compute and air-gapped operation reachable.

2a0141df6252.title: Skill groups
2a0141df6252.content: A flat directory of skills gives a reader no way to tell which one governs the task in front of them, so the kg graph is grouped, and the group is part of the address: skills/<area>/<package>/ (for example skills/kg/kg-core/, skills/conduct/conduct-core/), sdlc/skills/<package>/ for software delivery, and work-plan/skills/work-plan/ for the work plan. cat-harness.json is the list; directory-conventions says what each graph typology holds.

9ad792c1fcf2.doc: Is CI actually working on the default branch?
9ad792c1fcf2.title: Is CI actually working on the default branch?
9ad792c1fcf2.content: Process_CiHealth · strict · 2 step(s) . Is CI actually working on the default branch: record each workflow’s state on one tracking issue, and fail the job only when the state could not be determined. A WORKFLOW’S OUTCOME IS INVISIBLE FROM A CHECKOUT. Bean xom7: one workflow here fired on every push to main and FAILED ALL 30 TIMES OVER TWO MONTHS with nothing in the repository saying so. This is the backstop. WEEKLY, NOT DAILY, and the cadence is an argument rather than a default: the defect is “nobody noticed for two months”, not “nobody noticed for a day”, and the session-start sweep already covers every day somebody is working. A weekly run bounds the blind spot to seven days without turning the tracking issue into a feed. Could we tell? IS NOT SIMPLY THE EXIT CODE, and that is the subtlety worth drawing. bun exits 1 on an uncaught exception as well as on a live failure, so exit 1 alone does not separate “found something red” from “crashed”. The REPORT FILE separates them: --out writes it before any exit path, so a genuine red always has one and a crash before that point does not. Exit 1 with no report is reclassified as unknown. Without that, a crash would open a tracking issue quoting a stale file. THE THIRD STATE IS THE WHOLE POINT, AND IT IS THE ONLY ONE THAT FAILS THE JOB. Verified 2026-09-20 by reading the if: guards: unknown runs exit 1; a finding does NOT. A repository in trouble leaves this workflow GREEN and speaks through the tracking issue, while a sweep that could not look turns the job red. That inversion is deliberate and is invisible from the run list, which is the argument for drawing it. ONE TRACKING ISSUE, EDITED IN PLACE, never a comment and never a second issue — a feed nobody reads is the failure mode a watchdog invites. On unknown the issue is left UNTOUCHED: not closed, not opened, not edited. Closing it would assert the thing the sweep just failed to establish. Ensure the tracking label exists sits AFTER Could we tell? and before the split, because both issue paths need the label — the clean path filters on it too, and on a repository where nothing has ever gone wrong it would not otherwise exist. It is skipped on unknown, where neither path runs and a label hiccup must not be what fails the job. The verdict is reported through the shared tracked-watch process (Process_TrackedWatch), with the label ci-health. Its three ends say what happened: unknown (job red, issue untouched), clean (issue closed), or found (issue opened or edited, job green). i i

0d6ed7669f20.content: Every one of the 2 step(s) is documented. | step | lane | skill / sub-process | what it does | . | Run check:ci-health, WRITING the report fileTask_Check | Scheduled log sweep | ci-health | Run check:ci-health –out, writing the report file before any exit path. Exit 0 clean, 1 live failures, 2 could not check. bun also exits 1 on an uncaught exception, so an exit 1 with no report file is a crash and is treated as could-not-check.Where its verdict comes from: Asked of the verdict output that the check step of .github/workflows/ci-health.yml writes, not of the raw exit code. check:ci-health exits 0 clean, 1 live failure(s), 2 could not check; an exit 1 with no report file is a crash and is reclassified as could-not-check, as is any other code. no is verdict == ‘unknown’: the last step runs exit 1 and no issue step runs, so the tracking issue is left untouched. yes is verdict != ‘unknown’, the guard on the label step and so on both issue paths. | . | Report the verdict on the tracking issueCall_Watch | Scheduled log sweep | calls Report a verdict on one tracking issue | Runs the shared tracking watch with the label ci-health. 2c36ff1cd059.title: Classify and code content
2c36ff1cd059.content: Process_ClassifyAndCodeContent · advisory · 5 step(s) . Classifies and codes L1 extracted statements (recommendations, implementation practices, remarks, proposed coverage exclusions) and L2 DAK slots (personas, business processes, guideline domains, conditions, interventions, medicines, GRADE ratings), following the terminology-coding methodology and the classify-and-code-content skill. The authoring agent runs terminology-lookup down the four-rung reuse-first ladder, records provenance (declared, context, inferred) and candidate status, and stages the result. A person in the l1-extraction-reviewer lane signs or rejects each exclusion proposed in exclusions.proposed.json against the printed page (sections/page-NNN.md). A person in the terminologist / ontologist lane then adjudicates the candidate codings, SKOS match precision (exactMatch vs closeMatch) and any Rung 4 local glossary candidates. i i i i i

78a2713c81fa.title: The gates a change must pass before it can merge
78a2713c81fa.content: Process_CodeQualityGates · strict · 9 step(s) . The gates a change must pass before it can merge: the jobs of the code-quality workflow, each marked hard, warn-only or not a gate, joined by one question — did every hard one pass. EVERY GATE IS INDEPENDENT, AND NOTHING IN THE YAML SAYS SO IN ONE PLACE. Bean 7yvd. The file reads as a long sequence; it is not one. NO gate declares needs: on another GATE, so they all start together and the wall-clock cost of the gates is the SLOWEST job, not the sum. The needs: in the file are on jobs that are not gates: qa-publish (arc 3fva) waits for the corpus parts of gates whatever they concluded and stores the run’s QA results on the qa-reports branch, and nothing waits for it; and every job that READS the QA working copy waits for qa-working-copy (bean jtfk), which builds it once for the run instead of once per reader. That is the single most useful thing to know before adding a gate, and it is recoverable today only by checking for needs: keys that are not there. COUNT THE # bpmn-node: DECLARATIONS rather than trusting a number here: this paragraph said SIX until 2026-09-26, by which point there were eight — typescript had been split into typescript + gates and skill-registration-chain added — and the count was wrong in the one place a reader checks the shape. THE ASYMMETRY IS THE OTHER HALF, AND IT IS THE PART THAT DOES NOT GO STALE. Exactly TWO gates report without blocking — the Rust wildcard report and the dependency advisories, both STEPS of the hygiene job since bean 7fu5 — and every other gate is HARD. (qa-publish blocks nothing either, but it is not a gate at all, so it is drawn off the join rather than counted here.) Stated that way round on purpose: the warn-only set is named and closed, so it stays true as jobs are added, whereas “four are hard” needed editing the moment a ninth gate existed. Drawing them as equal boxes would be a lie a reader would act on, so the warn-only gates are labelled as such and the gateway after the join asks specifically about the HARD ones. THE TWO WARN-ONLY GATES ARE WARN-ONLY BY DIFFERENT MECHANISMS, AND THE DIFFERENCE IS THE POINT. The Rust step carries continue-on-error: true — the RUNNER discards its result. The advisories step carries no such flag: its script exits 0 in every state and keeps the three states apart in its OUTPUT instead. That is deliberate, because a warn-only step whose exit code says nothing has only its output left to distinguish found nothing from could not find out, and continue-on-error would have thrown away the one signal that still worked. continue-on-error IS NOT A DEFAULT HERE, it is a decision that has been REVERSED once already: the Python import check carried it, and the flag swallowed a failure on a missing path, so the job reported success over a check that never ran. It was removed and a new unused import now fails. The flag STILL survives on exactly one step — adding a second warn-only gate did not add a second continue-on-error, which is the history being honoured rather than an oversight. Anyone reaching for the flag should read that paragraph first. TypeScript IS ONE BOX STANDING FOR ROUGHLY THIRTY REPOSITORY GATES — workflow policy, AGENTS.md cross-references and claims, declared assets, workflow skill refs and BPMN coverage, the knowledge-graph audit, generated-docs currency, agent memory, and the ratchet that fails a check script no workflow runs. They are sequential only because one job runs them; each is independent, and bun run cat gates is the local runner derived from this job so a contributor can run the same set before pushing. Mechanical throughout. Nothing here waits on a person, which is what makes build-pipeline the right lane rather than a convenient one. i i i i i i i i i

76366c142557.doc: The gates a change must pass before it can merge
76366c142557.title: Steps
76366c142557.content: Every one of the 9 step(s) is documented. | step | lane | skill / sub-process | what it does | . | Verdict reuse: tree already green? (NOT A GATE)Task_VerdictReuse | CI/CD Pipeline | platform-gates | Bean qbco, issue #2456 (owner, 2026-10-07: “1y, 2y, 3y, 4y”). On a PUSH to main only; on any other event it is skipped and nothing waits for it. A merge-button merge of an up-to-date PR carries a tree CI has already tested. verdict-reuse.sh looks up the runs of this workflow on the merged head (the merge commit’s second parent) and answers reuse=true only when one concluded success, ran every job a reuse would skip, and tested exactly this tree: for a pull_request run, the tested-tree: its Task_QaWorkingCopy job wrote into its check run’s summary; for a dispatch, the head’s own tree. Then the four bun test shards (part of Task_TypeScript), the three e2e shards (Task_E2E) and the standalone ratchet (part of Task_RepositoryGates) are skipped on this push, and the summary names the run whose verdict stands. Everything that judges the tree against main or reads qa-reports still runs. A squash, an API error, a missing record or a mismatch is reuse=false and every job runs: could-not-determine is never green. Drawn before the fork because the jobs it can skip wait for it; the others do not. Since the same ruling, a newer push to main also cancels an older main run still in progress (the workflow’s concurrency), so main’s verdict history is thinned by decision. | . | QA working copy, built once (NOT A GATE)Task_QaWorkingCopy | CI/CD Pipeline | qa-reports | Bean jtfk, issue #2456. bun run qa:working-copy (bean 72a8) — the bootstrap kg-export, then every declared QA writer — used to run INSIDE each job that reads the QA tree, and qa-publish ran the same writers again: nine builds of one tree from one commit, measured at 2,284 of 4,714 runner-seconds (48 %) on run 37659324493. Now the qa-working-copy job builds it once and uploads everything the build changed as an artifact with a sha256 manifest; each reader downloads it, checks the manifest against the hash this job reported and every restored file against the manifest, and only then judges. An artifact rather than a cache, because a cache key built from less than the real inputs serves stale data; an artifact is per run and exact. It judges nothing, so it is not a gate and does not reach GW_Join; a failed build fails every reader at its first step (they run if: !cancelled()), never a skip. Drawn feeding GW_Readers, the four tasks that wait for it; within them typescript-static and gates-standalone read no QA tree and do not wait, and qa-publish waits for it as well as for Task_RepositoryGates. | . | Import hygiene (HARD) and advisories (WARN-ONLY)Task_Hygiene | CI/CD Pipeline | platform-gates | FOUR QUESTIONS, ONE RUNNER — bean 7fu5. They were four jobs (lean-bare-import, python-imports, rust-wildcard, dependency-advisories), each about a second of work behind a ~13 s checkout and a runner request; measured on main run 37133247484 (2026-10-03), the run took 21.7 min while its longest job executed for 174 s, the rest waiting for runners. Now they are steps of the hygiene job, and every step after the first gate runs if: !cancelled(), so a red one masks none of the others — the om30 rule kept inside one job rather than by splitting it. (1) Lean, HARD: fail on any bare import Mathlib in content/*/.lean; in this platform repo there is no content/, so the step prints SKIP and states that nothing was scanned. (2) Python, HARD: ruff F401 (unused) and F403 (wildcard) over the Python trees that exist, then the Python tests; an absent tree is dropped rather than passed to ruff, and an empty set says SKIP. (3) Dependency advisories, WARN-ONLY by the owner’s ruling on bean j41m: is anything in the resolved tree KNOWN-VULNERABLE? The script exits 0 in every state and keeps them apart in its output; .github/dependabot.yml is the other half of that ruling and is not drawn here. (4) Rust wildcard imports, WARN-ONLY: report non-test use …::*; in tools/*/.rs; continue-on-error, and therefore the job’s LAST step, where it masks nothing. | . | TypeScript: lint, types and tests (HARD)Task_TypeScript | CI/CD Pipeline | platform-gates | Three checks: bun run cat lint, tsc --noEmit and bun test. The repository gates it used to carry are Task_RepositoryGates now (bean om30). Since bean dlqu it is split across jobs: typescript-static (lint, then typecheck), typescript-test (bun test as four SEQUENTIAL shards on separate machines — Bun’s in-process --parallel worker pool hung at both 4 and 2 workers, measured — the shard passed in BUN_OPTIONS so the command stays the one bun run cat gates runs locally) each shard and typescript-static its own required check. A fourth job, typescript, carried one check name for all of them and was green only when the others succeeded; bean 5p4m (issue #2456) removed it — a runner request for ~1 s of work that waited minutes for a runner — so branch protection names the five checks directly. The step-order rule the single job needed — bun test LAST, because Actions stops at the first failing step and a red-by-decision test would otherwise mask lint and typecheck — no longer has anything to order: separate jobs cannot mask each other. Measured on three main runs before the change: bun test alone was 7m30s-7m45s of an 8m14s-8m33s job. | . | End-to-end + accessibility (HARD)Task_E2E | CI/CD Pipeline | platform-gates | Install Chromium, check the rendered BPMN SVGs are current, then run the Playwright suite, which includes the accessibility checks. Hard: a failure blocks the PR. SHARDED since bean dlqu (drawn as one task, deliberately: a multi-instance marker would add a BPMN term to every instance’s UML overview, about 75 generated files, for a picture this sentence already gives): the suite runs as three e2e-shard jobs (E2E_SHARD=i/3, one Playwright worker per core in each), and each shard is its own required check, so a shard that failed, was cancelled or never ran is a red check of its own. Until bean 5p4m (issue #2456) an e2e job carried one check name for the three and completed the task only when every instance succeeded; it was ~1 s of work behind a runner request that waited minutes, and was removed. Measured before the split: playwright test alone was 4m33s of a 5m16s job, the workflow’s slowest once bun test ran in parallel. The BPMN-render and .bat-wrapper checks run in shard 1 only, so they are asked once. | . | Repository gates (HARD)Task_RepositoryGates | CI/CD Pipeline | platform-gates | The 43 repository-gate steps — workflow refs, lane and process documentation, kg:audit:check, detangle, skills, published packages — 150 bun run invocations in all. A SEPARATE job from Task_TypeScript since bean om30: they were one job in which bun test came second of 47 steps, and because Actions stops a job at its first failing step and no step was continue-on-error, a deliberate test failure on main meant none of these ran. A gate never asked and a gate that passed are indistinguishable from outside, which is xom7 at the step rather than the workflow. No sequence dependency on Task_TypeScript is drawn because there is none: a red test must not stop these being asked. bun run cat gates derives its list from BOTH jobs, so the local set still cannot drift from CI’s. | . | Registered gates that never run (HARD)Task_UnrunGates | CI/CD Pipeline | platform-gates | check:gates-registered, split out of Task_RepositoryGates by bean dlqu: one step of that job measured 1m46s-2m28s across four runs, the longest step in it by a factor of four, and a sequential job is as slow as the sum of its steps. In its own job it runs beside the rest rather than after them. It still asks the same question — is every gate a script registers actually run somewhere — and is still hard. It also carries bun run cat security:gate (bean ieum, owner 2026-10-07: “security check before release”): the security checks by name, plus third-party action SHA pinning outside staging-only workflows, as one step that merge-train’s gate call reaches. A blocking fail OR could-not-check fails the job. | . | Skill-registration chain (UNMASKED)Task_SkillChain | CI/CD Pipeline | platform-gates | Runs the five --check commands that adding a skill stales, each on its own: gen-skill-docs, check:glossary, auto:docs:check, kg:audit:check, kg:detangle:check. CORRECTED 2026-09-26, after main split this workflow: the original justification is GONE. It read “the only place those five are read against the tree as checked out”, because at the time all six lived in one job behind bun test, which runs the kg-audit and detangle WRITERS and repaired two artefacts before their checks read them (bean ymsu). Task_RepositoryGates is now a separate job that runs all six and never runs bun test, so they are unmasked THERE. What survives is narrower and is the reason this is kept: one command a skill author runs (bun run cat skill:register) that regenerates and verifies the chain together, a committed QA sidecar saying which steps ran, and ONE named failure instead of six unrelated generated files — which is bean v625’s actual complaint. The unmasking argument belongs to Task_RepositoryGates now. Its first CI run earned the place: it went red on kg:detangle:check and the cause was kg-detangle.ts counting 1214 files of a gitignored node_modules/ as graph nodes — 1441 where a clean checkout computes 227, pinned in a committed sidecar. Not a step in front of bun test either: measured on main’s run 36234052354, a failing step SKIPS every step behind it, so a red there would turn one named failure into forty-five unevaluated ones. 13s, in parallel. Beans v625, fjwi. | . | Publish QA results (not a gate)Task_QaPublish | CI/CD Pipeline | calls Publish and keep QA results on qa-reportsqa-reports | Bean 16ei, arc 3fva. After Task_RepositoryGates, WHATEVER it concluded (needs: its two corpus parts, with always()), and after Task_QaWorkingCopy, whose copy it restores and publishes rather than building a second time (bean jtfk), qa:publish --github writes this run’s test/results trees to the orphan qa-reports branch: main/<sha>/ on a push to main, pr/<n>/<head-sha>/ on a same-repository PR (owner rulings D1, D3). A fork PR’s token is read-only, so it is skipped with a ::notice naming why. It does NOT reach GW_Join: a red publish is its own red and never decides mergeability, and the hard gates never wait on it. The only job here holding contents: write, which is also how bun run cat gates knows not to run it locally. A CALL ACTIVITY: the key derivation, the fork skip and the never--f retry loop are qa-publish.bpmn, which also draws the retention run that takes entries off the branch again. | .

98a660c2a288.title: Complete initialization
98a660c2a288.content: Process_CompleteInitialization · strict (defaulted) · 9 step(s) . A SUB-PROCESS of initialize-harness, called after a harness is installed and also when the location turns out to be a layer instantiating the chosen harness already. It is how an agent — the one that installed the harness, or one dispatched for exactly this with nothing but this diagram and the declaration — makes sure EVERY initialization step is done. THE STEPS ARE NOT LISTED HERE. They are named by the declarations: the layer’s <name>.json and every declaration it needs, read from the sibling checkouts. A declared directory is a step (it exists); a declared asset is a step (the file is there); a dependency’s <name>/docs/bootstrap/initialization.md is a step (it was followed); the root README and the sections it opts into are steps; the repository a declaration names makes the site steps — a Pages workflow, a gh-pages branch, Pages switched on, the address answering. A harness above bootstrap names more in the same way — a work-plan store it declares as a directory is a directory step — and bootstrap does not need to know which. The skill initialization-steps has the table. IDEMPOTENT BY CONSTRUCTION. Every step is CHECKED before anything is done, and a done step is left alone, so running this twice changes nothing the second time. Nothing is replaced: a step that would overwrite what somebody wrote is a step for a person, not for the agent. FOUR STATES, NOT TWO. done; not done; could not determine — the check could not run (no forge CLI, no network), which is NEVER reported as done; and stated — the declarations name it but nothing can observe it (reading and following instructions), exactly as a stated precondition is never reported as satisfied. THE PRIMARY STEP IS DRAWN, not left in the list: A_CheckDocuments, the harness’s JSON Schemas and JSON-LD at the IRIs they name, checked first after the declarations are read. Everything after it — directories, README, the site — is either how those documents are reached or how a person reads about them. 8ad1ac5e76eb.title: Which harness, and where
8ad1ac5e76eb.content: Skill confirm-harness: Narrow the harnesses and locations this could be, then have the Requestor settle it. Takes a list; returns at most ONE harness. It needs a person: the Requestor settles it, never the agent. Named by: Complete initialization, Determine the harness and repositories, Initialize a harness . You are the Bootstrapping Agent. You may narrow; only the Requestor may decide.

ff8dae515b6b.title: The contract
ff8dae515b6b.content: |   |   | . | in, from the Bootstrapping Agent | 0 or more harnesses · 0 or more locations | . | out, from the Requestor | 0 or 1 harness · 0 or more locations | . At most one. A list of two harnesses is not an answer, and you may not break the tie yourself. Zero is a real outcome, not a failure to try again: it ends the process, logged.

7df4f37c9dc6.title: Building the list you go in with
7df4f37c9dc6.content: Harnesses. The default is bootstrap itself. Add any the context already names: “please set up <owner>/<repo> here” in a discussion names one, and so does any Harness built on bootstrap that the Requestor mentions. Locations. Is this already a git repository? Were one or more URLs to repositories supplied? Both are Knowledge Graph Data Stores and the difference is only how you reach them — the git CLI, or a forge’s API. Assume a remote repository is read-only (read-from). Having push access to a remote git repository is never evidence that you are meant to modify it, and never makes it written-to. When a remote Knowledge Graph is supplied, two modes are open — and the Requestor chooses which: . | keep it here (read-from) — build and render from the remote Knowledge Graph in this repository, with whether to materialize its content locally or reference it in place asked as its own question; or | put a harness on the remote repository (written-to) — instantiate the harness in that remote repository itself. Nothing is written to a remote repository without the Requestor’s explicit permission for that repository. | .

f1a0c620a468.title: Asking
f1a0c620a468.content: Before you ask, say where you are — Initialize a harness, determining the harness and repositories, as the Bootstrapping Agent, asking the Requestor — and if you cannot tell that the person in front of you is the Requestor, ask that first (human-agent-discussion). Ask through human-agent-discussion: context, the candidates as options, your recommendation, and, said before the question, that there is no default: with no answer, the process stops. Ask once, with what you found, and make it answerable by picking: . What should this become? I can see (list). If it is none of those, name the repository — owner/name. If they answer with a kind — “a paper”, “a guideline” — that is not an answer yet: tell them which harnesses you know of and ask them to pick one. A kind is a property of the harness they name, and you read it from that harness rather than asking for it separately.

2309e4648935.title: Do not guess
2309e4648935.content: A wrong harness does not fail. It succeeds at being the wrong thing, and every consumer that reads the declaration believes it. So when you cannot get an answer: say the process needs one harness, log the failure, and stop.

fbe9204c74bf.content: Every one of the 6 step(s) is documented. | step | lane | skill / sub-process | what it does | . | Ask for a link or a descriptionA_Ask | Agent | calls Ask the personcontent-acquisition | Both forms, named together. On failure, fall back to the conversation. | . | Drop the file in the queueP_Upload | Contributor | — | Through the forge’s upload form, a commit, or any other route that lands the file in the declared queue. The agent watches rather than chases: an arrival may be minutes or days away. | . | Accept it, and record where it came fromA_Accept | Agent | content-acquisition | Both branches land here. An unprompted offer is accepted as it stands — do not make somebody follow a process to hand over what they already have. Provenance is recorded whichever channel it arrived through: a description given in chat has a source and can be wrong, exactly as a PDF does. | . | Route it, and watch the queueA_Route | Agent | uploads-watchlibrary-ingestion | A file goes to ingestion; a link or a description goes to whatever will resolve it. ecbb5f35127c.title: Committee review of a content change
ecbb5f35127c.content: Process_ContentChangeReviewCommittee · strict (defaulted) · 10 step(s) . The review committee’s review of one staged content change, ending in an approval or a request for changes: compare staged against main, slice the change and review each slice, settle withdrawn comments and disputed findings, gate on coverage, review the editorial dependencies and the impact, and decide. Called from content-change-review when the author submits. Which end it reaches is what the caller’s GW_CommitteeApproved reads. Organising the review is the review coordinator’s lane and deciding it is the committee’s. Merging is not here: it is a separate, confirmed act in content-change-review-publish. i i i i i i i i i i

ae91ae1166f3.title: Lanes — who acts
ae91ae1166f3.content: | lane | role | what it does here | . | Review Committee | reviewer | Compares staged against main, reviews the slices it is assigned (review-task.bpmn, one call per slice), takes a disputed finding to adjudication, judges the impact assessment, and decides. Task_Approve records the approval; merging is a separate, confirmed act in the publish phase. A rejection ends this phase with changes requested, and the caller routes it to Task_Iterate in the agent’s lane rather than to the author. | . | Review Coordinator | review-coordinator | Organises a review large enough to need organising, and decides nothing about the content: ingests the reviewers’ tagged comments, slices the change into pieces a reviewer can hold, assigns each slice to a review lane, and watches coverage until every changed block has a verdict or a reasoned waiver. A separate role from the editor: organising a review and deciding its outcome are different accountabilities. | .

b1e28a79a054.doc: Committee review of a content change
b1e28a79a054.title: Steps
b1e28a79a054.content: Every one of the 10 step(s) is documented. | step | lane | skill / sub-process | what it does | . | Compare main vs stagingTask_CompareBeforeAfter | Review Committee | staging-reviewvisual-diffrendered-impact | The review starts from the Change Set’s RENDERED list (skillrendered-impact): every rendered file the change alters, predictedfrom each renderer’s dependency cone and checked against the build.The reviewer opens every content page on it, not only the pages theauthor mentions; index files are listed but not reviewed. An inputthe renderer could not place is shown as not known, never as nochange.Review committee opens both URLs side by side:- Main site: <pages-url>/ (current published state)- Staging: <pages-url>/branches/<branch-slug>/The staging banner shows the commit SHA so they can verifywhat they are reviewing matches the PR. A changed figure, diagramor table is also pictured before and after on the review page,with the share of changed pixels in words (skill visual-diff,Tool folio-block-screenshots). Anything the staging job cannotpicture (page chrome, scroll behaviour, a PDF page, an IG page) isin the agent’s before/after preview (skill before-after-preview). | . | Ingest tagged review commentsTask_IngestComments | Review Coordinator | review-comments | Every PR conversation comment that starts with block: <label> becomes a review-comment/1.0.0 todo (open), idempotently, and is published with the preview as review-comments.json. The staging workflow runs this on every push and on every tagged comment; the coordinator owns that it has run before slicing, because the slices are cut around what reviewers have already said. This is the ingest transition of REVIEW_TRANSITIONS. Uses folio-review-comments. | . | Slice the change and assign reviewersTask_SliceAndAssign | Review Coordinator | review-heatmapstaging-reviewrendered-impact | From the ChangeSet, its rendered list (skill rendered-impact: each changed rendered page is assigned like a changed block) and the heat map on the review page: cut the change into slices a reviewer can hold (usually a section, or a run of sections where the heat map clusters), and assign each slice to a review lane by what it contains — clinical content to a clinical SME, a decision table to a QC reviewer, prose to a narrative reviewer. A block that needs no review (a pure rename, say) is WAIVED here with a written reason, which is what the coverage gate counts. Re-entered from GW_Covered when coverage is incomplete: the uncovered blocks become new slices. | . | Review each sliceCall_ReviewSlices | Review Committee | calls Review taskcontent-reviewreview-comments | review-task.bpmn, once per slice, in parallel lanes by role. What kind of thing changed decides which review the slice descends into; the reviewer takes on that inner lane’s role for the call only. Each reviewer gives the slice’s blocks a verdict, and comments on the pull request with the block: tag where something needs saying. | . | Withdraw a review commentTask_WithdrawComment | Review Committee | review-comments | The reviewer who made a comment takes it back (it was a misreading, or a later slice answered it). Recorded with folio-review-comment-move --to withdrawn, committed to the edit-set’s feature branch like every status change. This is the withdraw transition of REVIEW_TRANSITIONS. | . | Adjudicate the disagreementCall_Adjudication | Review Committee | calls Adjudicationadjudication | adjudication.bpmn. When the editor and a reviewer, or two reviewers, disagree about a finding, an adjudicator settles it and records why; the review comment moves to adjudicated with the Decision that closed it.Permitted answers: stands — the finding is right and the author addresses it; withdrawn — the finding is wrong and the comment closes. Recorded on the comment, not branched: either way the flow goes on to the coverage check. | . | Review the editorial dependenciesTask_ReviewUses | Review Committee | uses-editorial-review | uses[] is what a READER must have read to follow the block — neverpopulated from the formal dependency graph. Once every changed blockis covered, the committee checks the editorial dependencies of thechange as a whole before judging its impact. Reading order is aproperty of folio content, so the step belongs to the contentprocess, which reaches the harness’s review by calling DOWN intoreview-task. | . | Review impact assessmentTask_ReviewImpact | Review Committee | content-review | Committee reviews the agent’s impact assessment:- Were all downstream effects identified?- Are the indicator changes acceptable?- Does the logic change match the narrative intent? | . | Request changesTask_RequestChanges | Review Committee | content-reviewcontent-review | Committee provides feedback. PR stays open.Author and agent iterate further. | . | ApproveTask_Approve | Review Committee | decision-audit | The committee approves the change: the judgement, recorded with theevidence it rests on. Approving is not merging: a self-authoredchange cannot be approved through GitHub’s own review (the approvermay not be the PR’s author), and a merge needs the owner’s explicitconfirmation whoever approved. | .

46b38bc7aefc.title: Content Change and Review
46b38bc7aefc.content: Process_ContentChangeReview · strict (defaulted) · 11 step(s) . Getting a change to a folio’s CONTENT from a request into a published rendering: the author says what they want, an agent works out its scope and makes it, a review committee accepts or refuses it, and the pipeline deploys. You are in this process when what is changing is a folio — a chapter, a block, a piece of deterministic logic — rather than the platform that renders it. code-change-review is the same shape for the platform: a content change is accepted by a REVIEW COMMITTEE on editorial grounds, a platform change by a code reviewer on engineering ones. Two things this is not. It is not the feedback workflow: todo-review triages what readers said about content that already exists. And the rendering the author reviews is a STAGED one, because a person cannot assess a rendered artefact from a description of it. The diagram shows the phases and the hand-offs between them; each phase is its own process. Making the change is content-change-review-make, staging it is content-change-review-stage, the committee’s review is content-change-review-committee, and merging and deploying is content-change-review-publish. This follows bpmn-authoring’s rule of one phase per call activity. i i i i i i i i i i i

5e1ec758ee43.title: Типы контента
5e1ec758ee43.content: TR . На этой странице . | Научные статьи и книги | Другие — расширение folio-assistant | . Эта страница сгенерирована из content/docs/content-types/ — каждый раздел ниже ссылается на собственный исходный файл. ✎ Edit QA… TR . folio-assistant не зависит от контента: платформе ничего не известно о какой-либо конкретной статье или руководстве. Каждый вид контента поддерживается адаптером контента (код, который умеет валидировать, собирать и отображать этот вид) и пакетом навыков (формализм создания — то, что делают автор и LLM). На этой странице описан формализм каждого типа контента. Он намеренно отделен от какого-либо конкретного контента; конкретные артефакты располагаются в собственном репозитории контента.

5554bed98f55.title: Научные статьи и книги
5554bed98f55.content: ✎ Edit QA… TR . Пакет навыков: authoring-math · Адаптер: paper · Руководство: Написание статьи . Строгие научные статьи и книги, где текст и математические выкладки подкреплены формализацией в Lean 4, проверенной машиной, и сверстаны с помощью LaTeX. Статья — это документ плюс блоки с поддержкой Lean. Всё из предыдущего раздела применимо и здесь: то же дерево блоков, тот же редакторский граф uses[], те же сайдкары QA, тот же жизненный цикл — а также путь рендеринга в Markdown, который работает при подготовке черновика на компьютере без установленного TeX. Адаптер paper расширяет адаптер document в коде именно по этой причине. Статья добавляет семь приведенных ниже видов блоков, утверждения которых представляют собой формальные утверждения, и две инструментальные цепочки, которые проверяют их и выполняют верстку. | Исходная модель — контент представляет собой дерево типизированных блоков (definition, theorem, lemma, proof, equation, prose, …). См. справочник по API TypeScript для Block, Chapter и Paper. | Формализация — навыки lean-formalization и proof-verification управляют Lean; каждый блок типа теоремы можно сопоставить с его аналогом в Lean, при этом каждый sorry подлежит аудиту. | Рендеринг — latex-authoring плюс инструменты адаптера paper paper_render_pdf / paper_render_html. | . Семь видов, которые фолио документов не получает, и восемь общих видов: . | Вид блока | Префикс метки | Lean? | Профиль | . | definition | def: | обязательно | только paper | . | theorem / lemma / proposition / corollary | thm: / lem: / … | ожидается | только paper | . | conjecture | conj: | опционально | только paper | . | proof | prf: | опционально | только paper | . | example / remark | ex: / rem: | опционально | общий | . | algorithm / simulator | alg: / sim: | опционально | общий | . | prose / equation / diagram / table | prose: / eq: / fig: / tbl: | не применимо | общий | . Четыре строки со значением только paper соответствуют MATH_BLOCK_KINDS в schemas/block-kinds.ts; строки общий соответствуют DOCUMENT_BLOCK_KINDS, полученным как дополнение, чтобы вид, добавленный позже, не остался без классификации. На две из этих строк стоит обратить особое внимание. definition — это самая четкая граница разделения: это единственный вид, чье поле lean является обязательным, а не опциональным, поэтому фолио документа не могло бы содержать его, даже если бы это разрешал профиль. При этом общие виды по-прежнему декларируют опциональное поле lean: система типов разрешает то, что запрещает профиль, поэтому у content_profile_check есть второе правило помимо «разрешен ли этот вид». Соответствующие схемы навыков: latex-authoring, lean-formalization, proof-verification.

42912efb599b.title: Types de contenu
42912efb599b.content: TR . Sur cette page . | Articles scientifiques et livres | Autres — étendre folio-assistant | . Cette page est générée à partir de content/docs/content-types/ — chaque section ci-dessous renvoie vers sa propre source. ✎ Edit QA… TR . folio-assistant est indépendant du contenu : la plateforme ne sait rien d’un article ou d’une directive en particulier. Chaque genre de contenu est pris en charge par un adaptateur de contenu (du code qui sait comment valider/construire/restituer ce genre) et un ensemble de compétences (le formalisme de rédaction — ce qu’un auteur et le LLM font). Cette page décrit le formalisme de chaque type de contenu. Elle est intentionnellement gardée séparée de tout contenu concret ; les artefacts concrets résident dans leur propre dépôt de contenu.

e341c304c6b6.title: Articles scientifiques et livres
e341c304c6b6.content: ✎ Edit QA… TR . Ensemble de compétences : authoring-math · Adaptateur : paper · Guide : Rédiger un article . Articles scientifiques et livres rigoureux où la prose et les mathématiques sont appuyées par une formalisation Lean 4 vérifiée par machine et restituées via LaTeX. Un article est un document auquel s’ajoutent des blocs porteurs de Lean. Tout ce qui figure dans la section précédente s’applique ici : le même arbre de blocs, le même graphe éditorial uses[], les mêmes sidecars de QA, le même cycle de vie — ainsi que la voie de rendu Markdown, qui fonctionne lors de la rédaction sur une machine sans TeX. L’adaptateur paper étend l’adaptateur document dans le code, précisément pour cette raison. Ce qu’un article ajoute, ce sont les sept genres ci-dessous dont l’assertion est une affirmation formelle, ainsi que les deux chaînes d’outils qui les vérifient et les composent. | Modèle source — le contenu est un arbre de blocs typés (definition, theorem, lemma, proof, equation, prose, …). Voir la référence de l’API TypeScript pour Block, Chapter et Paper. | Formalisation — les compétences lean-formalization et proof-verification pilotent Lean ; chaque bloc de type théorème peut être suivi par rapport à son équivalent Lean, et chaque sorry est vérifiable. | Rendu — latex-authoring ainsi que les outils paper_render_pdf / paper_render_html de l’adaptateur paper. | . Les sept genres qu’un folio de type document ne reçoit pas, et les huit qu’il partage : . | Genre de bloc | Préfixe d’étiquette | Lean ? | Profil | . | definition | def: | obligatoire | paper uniquement | . | theorem / lemma / proposition / corollary | thm: / lem: / … | attendu | paper uniquement | . | conjecture | conj: | optionnel | paper uniquement | . | proof | prf: | optionnel | paper uniquement | . | example / remark | ex: / rem: | optionnel | partagé | . | algorithm / simulator | alg: / sim: | optionnel | partagé | . | prose / equation / diagram / table | prose: / eq: / fig: / tbl: | s. o. | partagé | . Les quatre lignes « paper uniquement » correspondent à MATH_BLOCK_KINDS dans schemas/block-kinds.ts ; les lignes « partagé » correspondent à DOCUMENT_BLOCK_KINDS, obtenu par complémentarité pour qu’un genre ajouté ultérieurement ne puisse rester non classé. Deux de ces lignes méritent un second regard. definition constitue le point de démarcation le plus net de toute la séparation — c’est le seul genre dont le champ lean est obligatoire plutôt qu’optionnel, si bien qu’un folio de type document ne pourrait pas en contenir un même si le profil l’autorisait. Et les genres « partagé » continuent de déclarer un lean optionnel : le type autorise ce que le profil interdit, raison pour laquelle content_profile_check comporte une seconde règle au-delà de « ce genre est-il autorisé ? ». Schémas de compétences pertinents : latex-authoring, lean-formalization, proof-verification.

30b94f0d72e8.title: أنواع المحتوى
30b94f0d72e8.content: TR . في هذه الصفحة . | الأوراق والكتب العلمية | أنواع أخرى — توسيع folio-assistant | . تم توليد هذه الصفحة من content/docs/content-types/ — يرتبط كل قسم أدناه بمصدره الخاص. ✎ Edit QA… TR . إن folio-assistant مستقل عن المحتوى: فالمنصة لا تعرف شيئًا عن أي ورقة بحثية أو دليل إرشادي بعينه. ويتم دعم كل نوع من أنواع المحتوى عبر محول محتوى (شفرة برمجية تعرف كيفية التحقق من ذلك النوع وبنائه وعرضه) و حزمة مهارات (الصياغة الرسمية للتأليف — ما يقوم به المؤلف والنموذج اللغوي الكبير). تصف هذه الصفحة الصياغة الرسمية لكل نوع محتوى. وقد تم فصلها عمدًا عن أي محتوى ملموس؛ حيث تعيش المخرجات الملموسة في مستودع المحتوى الخاص بها.

ab2c539afc20.title: الأوراق والكتب العلمية
ab2c539afc20.content: ✎ Edit QA… TR . حزمة المهارات: authoring-math · المحول: paper · الدليل الإرشادي: كتابة ورقة بحثية . الأوراق والكتب العلمية الدقيقة حيث يُدعم النثر والرياضيات بصياغة رسمية يتم التحقق منها آليًا عبر Lean 4 وتُصيَّر باستخدام LaTeX. الورقة البحثية هي مستند بالإضافة إلى كتل تدعم Lean. ينطبق كل ما ورد في القسم أعلاه هنا: شجرة الكتل نفسها، ومخطط uses[] التحريري نفسه، وملفات ضمان الجودة المرافقة (QA sidecars) نفسها، ودورة الحياة نفسها — ومسار تصيير Markdown، الذي يعمل أثناء الصياغة الأولية على جهاز لا يحتوي على TeX. يوسع محول paper محول document برمجياً لهذا السبب تحديدًا. وما تضيفه الورقة هو الأنواع السبعة الموضحة أدناه والتي يشكل توكيدها ادعاءً رسميًا، بالإضافة إلى سلسلتي الأدوات اللتين تتحققان منها وتنضدانها. | نموذج المصدر — المحتوى عبارة عن شجرة من الكتل المصنفة (definition، وtheorem، وlemma، وproof، وequation، وprose، …). راجع مرجع واجهة برمجة تطبيقات TypeScript للاطلاع على Block وChapter وPaper. | الصياغة الرسمية — تقود مهارتا lean-formalization وproof-verification نظام Lean؛ حيث يمكن تتبع كل كتلة شبيهة بالمبرهنة مقابل نظيرتها في Lean، ويكون كل تعبير sorry قابلاً للتدقيق. | التصيير — مهارة latex-authoring بالإضافة إلى أداتي paper_render_pdf وpaper_render_html التابعتين لمحول الورقة. | . الأنواع السبعة التي لا يحصل عليها الـ folio الخاص بالمستند، والأنواع الثمانية التي يشترك فيها: . | نوع الكتلة | بادئة التسمية | هل يدعم Lean؟ | ملف التعريف | . | definition | def: | إلزامي | paper فقط | . | theorem / lemma / proposition / corollary | thm: / lem: / … | متوقع | paper فقط | . | conjecture | conj: | اختياري | paper فقط | . | proof | prf: | اختياري | paper فقط | . | example / remark | ex: / rem: | اختياري | مشترك | . | algorithm / simulator | alg: / sim: | اختياري | مشترك | . | prose / equation / diagram / table | prose: / eq: / fig: / tbl: | لا ينطبق | مشترك | . الصفوف الأربعة الخاصة بـ paper فقط هي MATH_BLOCK_KINDS في schemas/block-kinds.ts؛ أما الصفوف المشتركة فهي DOCUMENT_BLOCK_KINDS، المشتقة كمتممة حتى لا يبقى أي نوع يُضاف لاحقًا دون تصنيف. يستحق اثنان من تلك الصفوف نظرة فاحصة. فالنوع definition هو النقطة الأوضح في هذا التقسيم بأكمله — فهو النوع الوحيد الذي يكون حقل lean فيه إلزاميًا وليس اختياريًا، ولذا لا يمكن لـ folio المستند أن يحتوي عليه حتى لو سمح ملف التعريف بذلك. وما زالت الأنواع المشتركة تعلن عن حقل lean اختياري: فالنوع البرمجي يسمح بما يحظره ملف التعريف، ولهذا السبب تحتوي أداة content_profile_check على قاعدة ثانية تتجاوز مجرد السؤال “هل هذا النوع مسموح به”. مخططات المهارات ذات الصلة: latex-authoring، lean-formalization، proof-verification.

c80570cfca73.title: Artículos científicos y libros
c80570cfca73.content: ✎ Edit QA… TR . Paquete de habilidades: authoring-math · Adaptador: paper · Guía: Redacción de un artículo . Artículos científicos y libros rigurosos donde la prosa y las matemáticas están respaldadas por una formalización en Lean 4 verificada por máquina y renderizadas mediante LaTeX. Un artículo es un documento más bloques con Lean. Todo lo explicado en la sección anterior aplica aquí: el mismo árbol de bloques, el mismo grafo editorial de uses[], los mismos sidecars de QA, el mismo ciclo de vida —y la ruta de renderizado a Markdown, que funciona mientras se redacta en una máquina sin TeX. El adaptador paper extiende el adaptador document en el código, exactamente por esa razón. Lo que añade un artículo son los siete tipos siguientes cuya aseveración es una afirmación formal, y las dos cadenas de herramientas que los verifican y componen tipográficamente. | Modelo fuente — el contenido es un árbol de bloques tipados (definition, theorem, lemma, proof, equation, prose, …). Consulta la referencia de la API de TypeScript para Block, Chapter y Paper. | Formalización — las habilidades lean-formalization y proof-verification controlan Lean; cada bloque de tipo teorema puede rastrearse frente a su contraparte en Lean, y cada sorry es auditable. | Renderizado — latex-authoring más las herramientas paper_render_pdf / paper_render_html del adaptador paper. | . Los siete tipos que un folio de documento no recibe, y los ocho que comparte: . | Tipo de bloque | Prefijo de etiqueta | ¿Lean? | Perfil | . | definition | def: | obligatorio | solo paper | . | theorem / lemma / proposition / corollary | thm: / lem: / … | esperado | solo paper | . | conjecture | conj: | opcional | solo paper | . | proof | prf: | opcional | solo paper | . | example / remark | ex: / rem: | opcional | compartido | . | algorithm / simulator | alg: / sim: | opcional | compartido | . | prose / equation / diagram / table | prose: / eq: / fig: / tbl: | n/a | compartido | . Las cuatro filas «solo paper» son MATH_BLOCK_KINDS en schemas/block-kinds.ts; las filas «compartido» son DOCUMENT_BLOCK_KINDS, derivadas como el complemento de modo que un tipo añadido posteriormente no pueda quedar sin clasificar. Dos de esas filas merecen una segunda mirada. definition es el punto más estricto de toda la división: es el único tipo cuyo campo lean es obligatorio en lugar de opcional, por lo que un folio de documento no podría contener uno incluso si el perfil lo permitiera. Y los tipos «compartidos» aún declaran un lean opcional: el tipo permite lo que el perfil prohíbe, razón por la cual content_profile_check tiene una segunda regla más allá de «¿está permitido este tipo?». Esquemas de habilidades pertinentes: latex-authoring, lean-formalization, proof-verification.

79b9341b7f2a.title: 科学论文与专著
79b9341b7f2a.content: ✎ Edit QA… TR . 技能包： authoring-math · 适配器： paper · 指南： 编写论文 . 严谨的科学论文与专著，其中的散文和数学内容均有机器校验的 Lean 4 形式化作为后盾，并通过 LaTeX 进行排版渲染。 . 论文就是文档加上包含 Lean 的块。 上一节中的所有内容在此同样适用：相同的块树、相同的编辑 uses[] 图、相同的 QA sidecar、相同的生命周期——以及 Markdown 渲染路径（在未安装 TeX 的机器上起草时即可工作）。正因如此，paper 适配器在代码上继承扩展了 document 适配器。论文所增加的是下方的七种断言为形式化主张的块类型，以及用于检查和排版它们的两个工具链。 . | 源模型（Source model）——内容是由类型化块（definition、theorem、lemma、proof、equation、prose 等）构成的树。有关 Block、Chapter 和 Paper，请参阅 TypeScript API 参考。 | 形式化（Formalization）——lean-formalization 和 proof-verification 技能驱动 Lean；每个类定理（theorem-like）块都可以对照其 Lean 对应项进行追踪，且每一个 sorry 均可审计。 | 渲染（Rendering）——latex-authoring 加上论文适配器的 paper_render_pdf / paper_render_html 工具。 | . 文档 folio 无法获得的七种类型，以及它共享的八种类型： . | 块类型 | 标签前缀 | 是否包含 Lean？ | 配置文件 | . | definition | def: | 必需 | 仅限论文 (paper only) | . | theorem / lemma / proposition / corollary | thm: / lem: / … | 预期包含 | 仅限论文 (paper only) | . | conjecture | conj: | 可选 | 仅限论文 (paper only) | . | proof | prf: | 可选 | 仅限论文 (paper only) | . | example / remark | ex: / rem: | 可选 | 共享 (shared) | . | algorithm / simulator | alg: / sim: | 可选 | 共享 (shared) | . | prose / equation / diagram / table | prose: / eq: / fig: / tbl: | 不适用 | 共享 (shared) | . 四个“仅限论文”（paper only）行是 schemas/block-kinds.ts 中的 MATH_BLOCK_KINDS；而“共享”（shared）行则是 DOCUMENT_BLOCK_KINDS，作为补集推导得出，以便后续添加的类型不会未经分类。 . 其中有两行值得进一步审视。definition 是整个划分中最明确的分水岭——它是唯一一个其 lean 字段为必需而非可选的类型，因此即便配置文件允许，文档 folio 也无法容纳它。而“共享”（shared）类型仍然声明了一个可选的 lean：类型系统允许了配置文件所禁止的内容，这正是为什么 content_profile_check 在“该类型是否被允许”之外还有第二条规则。 . 相关的技能模式： latex-authoring、 lean-formalization、 proof-verification。 .

0ebc41a49292.title: Content types
0ebc41a49292.content: TR… . On this page . | Scientific papers & books | Others — extending folio-assistant | . This page is generated from docs/source/concepts-content-types/ — each section below links to its own source. ✎ Edit QA… TR… . folio-assistant is content-agnostic: the platform knows nothing about any particular paper or guideline. Each kind of content is supported by a content adapter (code that knows how to validate/build/render that kind) and a skill package (the authoring formalism — what an author and the LLM do). This page describes the formalism of each content type. It is intentionally kept separate from any concrete content; concrete artifacts live in their own content repository.

09926f8d96a0.title: Scientific papers & books
09926f8d96a0.content: ✎ Edit QA… TR… . Skill package: authoring-math · Adapter: paper · Guide: Writing a paper . Rigorous scientific papers and books where prose and mathematics are backed by a machine-checked Lean 4 formalization and rendered through LaTeX. A paper is a document plus Lean-bearing blocks. Everything in the section above applies here: the same block tree, the same editorial uses[] graph, the same QA sidecars, the same lifecycle — and the Markdown render path, which works while drafting on a machine with no TeX. The paper adapter extends the document adapter in code, for exactly that reason. What a paper adds is the seven kinds below whose assertion is a formal claim, and the two toolchains that check and typeset them. | Source model — content is a tree of typed blocks (definition, theorem, lemma, proof, equation, prose, …). See the TypeScript API reference for Block, Chapter, and Paper. | Formalization — lean-formalization and proof-verification skills drive Lean; each theorem-like block can be tracked against its Lean counterpart, and every sorry is auditable. | Rendering — latex-authoring plus the paper adapter’s paper_render_pdf / paper_render_html tools. | . The seven kinds a document folio does not get, and the eight it shares: . | Block kind | Label prefix | Lean? | Profile | . | definition | def: | required | paper only | . | theorem / lemma / proposition / corollary | thm: / lem: / … | expected | paper only | . | conjecture | conj: | optional | paper only | . | proof | prf: | optional | paper only | . | example / remark | ex: / rem: | optional | shared | . | algorithm / simulator | alg: / sim: | optional | shared | . | prose / equation / diagram / table | prose: / eq: / fig: / tbl: | n/a | shared | . The four paper only rows are MATH_BLOCK_KINDS in schemas/block-kinds.ts; the shared rows are DOCUMENT_BLOCK_KINDS, derived as the complement so a kind added later cannot go unclassified. definition is the one kind whose lean field is required rather than optional, so a document folio could not hold one even if the profile allowed it. The shared kinds still declare an optional lean: the type permits what the profile forbids, so content_profile_check has a second rule beyond “is this kind allowed”. Relevant skill schemas: latex-authoring, lean-formalization, proof-verification.

db5e1a0127ee.doc: Contributor feedback on a working draft
db5e1a0127ee.title: Contributor feedback on a working draft
db5e1a0127ee.content: Process_ContributorFeedback · strict (defaulted) · 9 step(s) . A document is still being written, and the Authoring Committee gives feedback on it in a shared Contributor Feedback sheet. This is what happens to ONE change set, one row of that sheet: a member starts it with a title, the sections it is about and their feedback; the agent proposes a direction; an Editor lets the agent edit; the agent makes the edit in the row’s one pull request, whose staging preview shows what changed; the committee answers on the row; and an Editor lets the agent merge. If the row’s feedback changes after the agent wrote its proposal, the proposal is marked stale and the row’s Ready for agent goes back to No, so the agent proposes again and an Editor decides again. The sheet’s colours follow the lanes: Blue for the committee, Green for the agent, Orange for the Editor. Skill: review-sheet-script. i i i i i i i i i
