c4d72b542de0.content: | lane | role | what it does here | . | FHIR modeller / PR author (person + authoring agent) | fhir-modeller | Starts the run with a source change, and owns every failure branch before the process ends rather than just stopping: Gateway_Valid’s no, Gateway_QcPass’s no and Gateway_Restore’s environment error each write to the work plan here, in Task_LogFindings, Task_QcBeans and Task_LogEnvError, before EndEvent_Findings, EndEvent_FindingsQc or EndEvent_EnvError. A run that stops short always leaves a record of why. The work plan is a data store these tasks write to, not a lane of its own. | . | Incremental build (system) | build-pipeline | Owns everything that stays inside the cone: restore the cache, compute the cone, check it out, compile and re-render only that slice, then merge and rebuild the aggregates — Task_Index never re-derives an artefact on its own, so a missing record is a miss rather than a silent rebuild. What needs the JVM’s warm state, it hands to Lane_Services rather than running itself. | . | Publisher + validator services (JVM) | ig-publisher-service | Two duties. Task_FullBuild is the fallback when Gateway_Restore finds the cache unusable: it bypasses the cone machinery and reaches Task_Qa on its own. Task_ContextLoad and Task_Validate hold the loaded dependency packages and expansions warm across runs, which makes validating a handful of cone files cheap; losing that warm state is a cache miss and routes to the fallback. | . | PR reviewer / QC reviewer | qc-reviewer | Sees the change’s shape before the build finishes — Task_ConeReport names what will rebuild and whether a shared hub is touched, posted while the checkout is still running — then gates on Task_Qa by reading the cone’s own rows in the aggregate first. On a PR branch it also deploys the preview itself, but never seeds the shared cache: that stays Lane_PubMgr’s, reached only past Gateway_Path on main or a release. | . | Publication manager — deploy and seed | publication-manager | Reached only past Gateway_Path’s main-or-release branch, never for a PR preview; the one lane allowed to touch the shared cache. Task_Seed writes to a -test branch and verifies a restore from a clean clone before promoting: the verified restore, not the deploy, licenses the shared cache. | .

5348b01fddad.title: Steps
5348b01fddad.content: Every one of the 19 step(s) is documented. | step | lane | skill / sub-process | what it does | . | Restore derived stateTask_Restore | Incremental build (system) | ig-publication | ig-cache restore: the IG’s AST and the Publisher’s terminology cache (input-cache/txcache/). Exit 0 usable, 1 miss, 2 environment error, 3 present but unusable (corrupt or mismatched, such as a moved toolchain). The cache restored is the declared fhir-ast cache (caches/fhir-ast.cache.json), whose component process is ig-ast-cache.bpmn: this task is that component’s verify, run inside the incremental build. | . | Log the environment error on the beanTask_LogEnvError | FHIR modeller / PR author (person + authoring agent) | todo-manager | Exit 2 from restore: the cache store or the toolchain could not be reached. Record that on the change’s bean, with the restore output, so the work plan says the build did not run and why. Check before creating — beans create is not idempotent. | . | Full publisher buildTask_FullBuild | Publisher + validator services (JVM) | ig-publication | Exit 1 or 3 from restore: the whole IG is built. Its outputs become the records the next seed writes. | . | Compute the cone of the changeTask_Cone | Incremental build (system) | ig-publicationig-publicationig-publication | fsh-cone --changed (scripts/fsh-cone.ts) over the changed files: the forward cone is what to rebuild, the backward cone is what to check out. | . | Post the cone report on the PRTask_ConeReport | PR reviewer / QC reviewer | quality-controlquality-controlquality-control | Review path: the reviewer sees what this change rebuilds — how many artefacts, and whether a hub (a shared RuleSet, CQL library or value set) is touched — before the build finishes. On main it is a log line. | . | Restricted checkout of the backward coneTask_Checkout | Incremental build (system) | ig-publicationig-publicationig-publication | git sparse-checkout of the cone’s files plus sushi-config.yaml, ig.ini and the alias files — a median of three files, p90 eleven, measured on the SMART Immunizations IG. | . | SUSHI on the restricted tankTask_Sushi | Incremental build (system) | l3-fhir-authoring | Compile the restricted checkout with SUSHI — the cone’s FSH, not the whole IG. A build optimisation, not a validation shortcut: SUSHI compiling is not conformance, so a green compile goes on to validation rather than standing in for it. | . | Load or reuse the warm contextTask_ContextLoad | Publisher + validator services (JVM) | ig-publicationig-publicationig-publication | The validator’s server mode holds the loaded dependency packages, snapshots and expansions in its session cache. Cold start loads the restored derived FHIR rather than regenerating it. | . | Validate the cone (fhir_validate)Task_Validate | Publisher + validator services (JVM) | fhir-validation | Validate the cone’s resources against the warm validator and report the cone that was checked. A validator that could not start is could-not-determine, never a pass with no findings. A green cone is not a green IG: a profile the change did not touch can still be broken by it. | . | Log findings on the beanTask_LogFindings | FHIR modeller / PR author (person + authoring agent) | todo-manager | Validation failed: record the findings on the change’s bean, so the work plan says what blocks it. Check before creating — beans create is not idempotent. | . | Re-render the cone’s records (fhir_narrative · skip lists)Task_Render | Incremental build (system) | ig-publicationig-publicationig-publication | Narrative and fragments for the cone only: the publisher’s -no-validate / -no-narrative complements today, Rapido’s differential build once its tracker is persisted. | . | Merge restored and rebuilt recordsTask_Merge | Incremental build (system) | ig-publication | Combine the restored per-artefact records with the cone’s freshly rendered ones into one complete set, so the meta-index rebuild that follows has every artefact’s record and never re-derives one. | . | Rebuild the meta-index (ig_metaindex_rebuild)Task_Index | Incremental build (system) | ig-publicationig-publicationig-publication | The whole-IG aggregates only — artifacts, TOC, canonicals, expansions, package, QA aggregate. Never re-derives an artefact: a missing record is a miss (exit 1), not a silent rebuild. | . | Assemble the siteTask_Site | Incremental build (system) | ig-publication | Assemble the site from the merged records: the IG template and a Jekyll build over output/. Only site assembly happens here — every artefact record already exists. | . | Run QC gates on the aggregate QATask_Qa | PR reviewer / QC reviewer | quality-control | qa.json is the aggregate of per-artefact outcomes; the reviewer reads the cone’s rows first. | . | File QC findings as beansTask_QcBeans | FHIR modeller / PR author (person + authoring agent) | todo-manager | QC failed on the aggregate: file each finding as a bean, so it is tracked on the work plan rather than lost in qa.json. Check for an existing bean before creating one. | . | Deploy the preview siteTask_DeployPreview | PR reviewer / QC reviewer | content-publish | A preview never seeds the shared cache. | . | Deploy the siteTask_Deploy | Publication manager — deploy and seed | content-publishig-publication | Deploy the site built from main or a release. Deploying is release-management, after a human authorised the release — an agent never records that authorisation. A release’s files are not deployed to the site: a v* tag makes a GitHub draft release carrying them (ig-release.yml; skill ig-binary-artefacts §”Releasing”), which the owner publishes. Report the published URL only once it answers: a returned deploy is not a serving site. | . | Seed the cache from the green buildTask_Seed | Publication manager — deploy and seed | ig-publicationig-publicationig-publication | Only a green build of main or a release seeds. Seed writes to the -test branch, verifies a restore from a clean clone, then promotes. This is the save of the declared fhir-ast cache (caches/fhir-ast.cache.json), under its save policy: the default branch only. | .

13ba1039e5b3.title: Decisions
13ba1039e5b3.content: Every one of the 4 decision(s) is documented. | decision | what decides it | branches | . | Cache usable?Gateway_Restore | Answered by the exit code of ig-cache restore (Task_Restore): 0 is a usable cache and takes yes, into the cone machinery. 1 (a miss) or 3 (present but unusable) takes no, to the full publisher build, whose outputs become the records the next seed writes. Exit 2 (an environment error — the cache could not be read, which says nothing about whether it is usable) takes environment error: the run stops and the error is logged, so a broken cache store is not hidden behind a slow full build. | yes → Compute the cone of the changeno → Full publisher buildenvironment error → Log the environment error on the bean | . | Valid?Gateway_Valid | Answered by Task_Validate — the cone’s resources checked against the warm validator. yes goes on to re-render the cone’s records. no logs the findings on the change’s bean and returns them to the author. A validator that could not start is could-not-determine and does not take yes. | no → Log findings on the beanyes → Re-render the cone’s records (fhir_narrative · skip lists) | . | QC clean?Gateway_QcPass | Decided in the reviewer’s QC gate (Task_Qa, quality-control) over qa.json, the aggregate of per-artefact outcomes, reading the cone’s rows first. no files each QC finding as a bean, checking for an existing one first, and returns the findings to the author. yes goes on to deploy. | no → File QC findings as beansyes → PR branch, or main / release? | . | PR branch, or main / release?Gateway_Path | Answered by the push that started the process. PR branch is the review path: deploy the preview, which never seeds the shared cache. main / release is the publish path: deploy the site after a human has authorised the release, then seed the cache (Task_Seed). Only this branch reaches the lane allowed to touch the shared cache. | PR branch → Deploy the preview sitemain / release → Deploy the site | .

892d9cc8f16d.doc: An IG release: the owner tags, a draft is built, the owner publishes
892d9cc8f16d.title: An IG release: the owner tags, a draft is built, the owner publishes
892d9cc8f16d.content: Process_IgRelease · advisory · 5 step(s) . How an IG repository’s release is cut, and how a missed one is caught up (skill ig-binary-artefacts §”Releasing”). (Owner, 2026-11-10: “need to add this to process (and how to catchup if not tagged) of build”.) . THE RULE. A release is a governance decision. The owner tags the IG’s CURRENT version from sushi-config.yaml, v<version>, on the default branch. The tag starts the IG’s ig-release.yml caller, which builds the tag in full and makes a GitHub DRAFT release carrying package.tgz (and its R4/R4B variants), ast-data.zip and SHA256SUMS. The owner publishes the draft. An agent never chooses a version, never pushes a tag and never publishes a release. THE CATCH-UP. Every AST refresh of the default branch runs ig-release.ts check (advisory, never failing the run): an untagged current version is reported with the commit that set it, for the owner to tag; a tag with no release is reported with the by-hand run of the release workflow; a draft is reported as waiting for the owner. The site is not the release: it is published from the AST cache (ig-ast-cache.bpmn) and carries none of these files. i i i i i

4d5929265715.content: Derived: every term this instance's swimlanes define — the role's title and description, the lane names that bind it, and whether the term has been retired. This is an index, not the documentation. It says what exists and what each artefact declares about itself. What a process is for, when you would be in it, and what it is not, is authored beside it and reuses these entries rather than restating them — see the auto-docs skill. Filter this table | Artefact | What it declares about itself | . | Activity logglossary-ledger.json | The agent activity log. A MECHANICAL role: it is written to at task start and task end, and emptied by an actor — one entry, all of them, or on a periodic sweep — and it decides nothing. Modelled on work-plan and corpus, the two existing stores; its skill is the contract it is held to. Its entries are held in the layer's unpublished store and never reach a published graph; the activity-log skill names the location, which is deliberately not repeated here because a role description IS published.notation role/logfirst seen 2026-09-21status current | . | Actorbootstrap/glossary-ledger.json | no description in the artefactnotation process/Process_LogMessage/lane/Lane_Actorfirst seen 2026-09-21status current | . | Adjudicatorglossary-ledger.json | Settles a criterion whose reviewer entries disagree, and records WHY. Inherits reviewer because an adjudicator is a reviewer with one added entitlement — the adjudication permission — and the separation is the point: a reviewer reports, an adjudicator settles, and a process where every reviewer could settle has no way to say who decided. The KNOWLEDGE spreads (several roles carry the adjudication skill, because each has to tell an adjudicable disagreement from a complaint); the ENTITLEMENT does not, and lives on the actor as a permission.notation role/adjudicatorfirst seen 2026-09-22status current | . | Administratorglossary-ledger.json | Administers the role graph itself: who exists, what they may act as, and what they may do. The ONE lane whose activities change the substrate every other diagram's lanes bind to — which is why it is drawn rather than left as a filesystem edit. Declared 2026-09-20 on the owner's answer that administration is a swimlane; role-model.md's rule is that a role is never invented to make a diagram drawable, so it waited for that.notation role/administratorfirst seen 2026-09-21status current | . | Agentbootstrap/glossary-ledger.json | no description in the artefactnotation process/Process_HumanAgentDiscussion/lane/Lane_Agentfirst seen 2026-10-01status current | . | Archimateglossary-ledger.json | no description in the artefactnotation kind/archimatefirst seen 2026-11-04status current | . | Attestation serviceglossary-ledger.json | Signs a QA report's run hashes over an API. 960a011395ad.content: $schemabean/1.0.0 titleFOLIO WORKFLOWS live in the PLATFORM repo — do they belong here? them `AGENTS.md` already states the shape for two of them — 'qa-sweep and witness-refresh fail by design in this repo: the first preflights on content/package.json, the second needs computations/, and the platform carries no folio' — and adds 'do not fix a dispatch-only workflow by dispatching it'. So at least some are deliberate: the platform ships the workflow a folio will use. If that is the intent for all twelve, the question is whether a workflow a repository cannot run should live in it at all, or be part of what `folio_init` writes into a folio. If it is NOT the intent, some of these are dead files whose paths broke at the #223 split and nothing noticed — `check:ci-health` cannot see them because a path-filtered workflow that never fires has no runs to be red. They are now declared `no-folio` in `STEP_EXEMPTIONS` with reasons, so a machine can read what prose asserted. **That records what they are and does not decide where they go.** ## Done when - [x] decide: shipped-for-a-folio, or dead since the split, per workflow - [x] the shipped ones have a home that makes their non-running visible rather than silent - [x] the dead ones go to `fsh-guts/`, never `rm` statuscompleted typetask prioritynormal created_at2026-09-20T07:44:35Z updated_at2026-09-20T09:12:10Z parentfolio-assistant-1xhc

1de3b6ec6504.content: cat-harness's work plan · beans by process · every instance . BPMN workflow instances recorded in cat-harness's work plan, joined with the beans they name. Ages are measured on 2026-11-13 (UTC, the day this page was built); an instance is stalled when it is running and has not moved for more than 7 days. A finished instance is marked where it ended. Beans that no instance names are listed under "Beans in no process"; the store page has every bean. A running subprocess is followed on each instance's own page.

Beans that no instance names are listed under "Beans in no process"; the store page has every bean. A running subprocess is followed on each instance's own page. 8443f206ef0b.content: cat-harness-tools's work plan · beans by process · every instance . BPMN workflow instances recorded in cat-harness-tools's work plan, joined with the beans they name. Ages are measured on 2026-11-13 (UTC, the day this page was built); an instance is stalled when it is running and has not moved for more than 7 days. A finished instance is marked where it ended. Beans that no instance names are listed under "Beans in no process"; the store page has every bean. A running subprocess is followed on each instance's own page.

The harness's own minimal folio renderer (bean ohx6, owner ruling 2026-10-10): `file-list.ts`, which renders the folio as the list of files it holds into `folio/index.md`, and the skill that says when to run it. Code and a skill, not folio content: the folio reader reads only `folio/*.json`, and the renderer skips this directory. 4 files . | README.md | file-list.test.ts | file-list.ts | folio-file-list.md | . upstream/ cat-harness-upstream . The pinned-upstream registry, `upstream-pins.json` (`"$schema": "folio-upstream-pins/v1"`): one row per upstream dependency the build pins — such as the just-the-docs theme and the Bun runtime — naming the file the pin is READ from (`pinnedIn`, resolved against this layer's root), the pattern that reads it, what of ours binds to the dependency and the MVP that must pass before it moves. It deliberately holds no version: that lives in the file the build reads. Read by `bun run cat check:upstream-pins` (weekly, `.github/workflows/upstream-pins.yml`) and worked by the `upstream-pin-watch` / `upstream-version-adoption` processes and skill this layer owns. Moved here from the repository root on 2026-10-06 (bean `ar1s`, phase 3: tooling leaves the root before the repo split). HERE rather than in the tool layer because this layer's processes, skills and scripts name it, and a harness file naming a file in the layer above is a wrong-direction reference (`check:reference-direction`). `code`: the checker's input table, authored beside the processes that read it, not content any reader renders. 2 files . | README.md | upstream-pins.json | .

4430a5ebedaa.content: folio-assistant-sci · 5 declared code directories · Files open on GitHub at the commit this site was built from. templates/ folio-templates . The PAPER profile of the files `folio_init` writes into a new folio: `paper/` holds the Lean build, lake-cache restore and blueprint workflows and the `.github/scripts` they call, written into a paper folio after the `document/` profile the tools layer keeps. Only a paper folio is given them, and the paper profile is this layer's. The id is the tools layer's `folio-templates`, so this directory is a member of that subgraph and `init-folio` finds it by id across the checkout, never by a path naming this layer. `{{assistant}}`, `{{folio}}`, `{{platform_git}}` and `{{platform_repo}}` are substituted at write time. b3a88f8b40d3.title: Fields
b3a88f8b40d3.content: $schemacat-harness-declaration/1.0.0 _commentTHE AGENTIC HARNESS layer. Owner, 2026-09-20 (paraphrased): the harness, the content core above it and the composed checkout are distinct layers with distinct schemas — so this declares itself `cat-harness` rather than `folio-assistant`. It carried the latter until the repository root gained a harness.json of its own, at which point TWO layers declared one name and `instanceRoots` — keyed on the declared name — could only hold one of them. The one it held was the root, so `folio-assistant` resolved to the checkout and the harness layer became unreachable by name. `stub` was RENAMED to `cat-harness` on 2026-09-21 (owner ruling, PR #685), resolving the collision where both resolved to `<base>/folio-assistant.jsonld`. The CatHarness declaration for THIS layer — what directories it scans and what kind of graph each holds. See skills/kg/kg-core/directory-conventions.md. This repo is PRE-SPLIT (issue #223), so it declares what is true today, not the target layout: `tools/` and `folio/` do not exist here yet and are deliberately not declared. A directory that is declared but absent is worse than one that is missing, because every consumer then scans nothing and reports a clean run over it. NOTE: `schemas/` declares TWO graphs — the first real use of the array. A directory is a place to look and may hold more than one part of the graph; it does not say how to tell them apart, because the files declare what they are (see bean xxxb: schemas/*.ts does not yet do this well). `beans/` is declared ONCE, as a single `beans` graph. Its internal split — `defs` for work items, `workflows` for running BPMN state — is declared by `beans/beans.json`, not here. #263 declared the two as separate directories, one nested inside the other, which left a consumer unable to tell which owned what beneath it; the nodes now carry that. _titleNo `title`, deliberately: `displayTitle` is title || name || id, so the sidebar and the landing page fall back to `name` — which the schema already requires to be the layer's identifier, the one artefacts are stub-named after. A title here said `c@t-harness` and overrode that, labelling THIS repository with the brand of the harness layer that is still to be split out of it. Setting the title to `folio-assistant` instead would be the same fact in two fields, free to drift. The c@t-harness derivation stays in the description, where it is a tagline rather than an identity. namecat-harness repositorylitlfred/cat-harness version0.1.0 iriBasehttps://litlfred.github.io/cat-harness/ _title_commentThe HUMAN display name, for the LHS navbar's harness tabs. Owner, 2026-09-21: "harnesses should list the names (they should be named in schmeas, e.g. cat-boostrap should be named 'Boostrap', f-a => Folio Assistant, cat-harness => C@T Harness)". `name` stays the machine identifier that filenames, `needs` edges and `declaredBy` resolve against; `title` is what a reader sees and nothing resolves against. Bean t3n8. THIS ONE WAS WRONG RATHER THAN ABSENT: it declared `title: "folio-assistant"`, the ROOT layer's name, so two layers carried one title and `disambiguate()` correctly qualified this tab to "folio-assistant (cat-harness)" — the label the owner reported. The disambiguator behaved as designed; the declaration was the defect. titleC@T Harness skillPrefixcat descriptioncomputable adjudication and agentic test harness caaat-harness ca&at-harness .c&at-harness  c@t-harness summaryComputable adjudication and agentic test harness. alsoWritten[ "caaat-harness", "ca&at-harness", ".c&at-harness", "c@t-harness" ] . iconmark navbarIcons[ "close", "todos", "beans", "fsh-guts", "qr", "launcher" ] . glassStrip[ { "chrome": "todos" }, { "chrome": "settings" }, { "kind": "library" }, { "kind": "processes" }, { "kind": "tools" }, { "kind": "skills" } ] . images[ { "id": "mark-small", "src": "docs/assets/img/icons/cat-mark-small.svg", "role": "browser-icon", "title": "c@t mark, small", "description": "The same at-sign, with the whiskers dropped. Below about 32 px a 2.4-unit whisker is under a pixel and reads as dirt on the glyph rather than as a cat, so the small mark leaves them out instead of drawing them badly." }, { "id": "mark", "src": "docs/assets/img/icons/cat-mark.svg", "role": "mark", "title": "c@t", "description": "An at-sign whose inner a is a cat: the a's bowl is the head, its counter is the face, the ears grow out of the top of the bowl and cross the ring, and the whiskers are cut in white across the sage. The ring keeps its gap and its tail, so it still reads as an @." }, { "_comment": "THE MASK FORM, and it REPLACES the light/dark pair above rather than joining it. Owner, 2026-09-22: \"I want theme like in avaatars\". An avatar is a mask plus a background-colour derived from one declared hue, so both schemes come from one number and neither can be authored legible while the other is invisible — which is exactly what `gen-avatars-css` says about not shipping 64 assets: \"as files they would drift, and the one that fell behind would be invisible until somebody opened the site in the other mode\". The mark had already shipped that risk as two files that must agree. It also ends a second disagreement: `cat-harness` declares tone 268 and its mark was sage, two colour vocabularies for one layer. The cost, accepted by the owner over two hand-derived tones: the pale-sage EAR step flattens into the body.", "id": "mark-mask", "src": "docs/assets/img/icons/cat-mark-mask.svg", "role": "mark-mask", "title": "c@t mark, as a mask", "description": "The same at-sign expressed as ALPHA rather than as colour: opaque where the mark takes the layer's declared tone, transparent where it cuts out — the face and the whiskers, both of which are already cut-outs in the coloured mark." }, { "_comment": "THE DARK-SCHEME MARK, and it exists for a MEASUREMENT rather than for taste. The text region was found by rendering candidate boxes over the image and looking at them — the first attempt spilled past the cloud edge, which no amount of arithmetic on the aspect ratio would have caught." }, { "id": "landing-mobile", "src": "docs/assets/img/harness/landing-mobile.webp", "role": "landing", "layout": "mobile", "width": 941, "height": 1670, "textRegion": { "x": 0.13, "y": 0.225, "w": 0.72, "h": 0.225 }, "title": "Thinking about it — tall", "description": "A grumpy cat in a sage hoodie stands in the rain under a thought-cloud carrying the c@t mark; the layer's description is drawn inside the cloud. Owner, 2026-09-20: "So bootsteap, cat harness, fa-core, f-a, from bottom to top." Declared rather than hardcoded in the navbar, so the ordering is a fact of the repository and not of whichever consumer needed it first. `bootstrap-tools` added 2026-09-30 (bean `0lj4`, owner's ruling): bean `xsqm` moved that code OUT of this layer into its own, and this list was not updated with it, so 20 imports under `cat-harness/` reached a layer this file did not name. `allowedFromNeeds` gives a layer `{layer} U ancestors(layer)`, and `bootstrap-tools` is a SIBLING of `cat-harness` rather than an ancestor, so every one of those 20 was `wrong-direction` by the declared rule while four separate checks reported clean. The reverse arrow stays forbidden and is guarded by `check:tools-closure`. REMOVED again 2026-10-30 (bean `8lcl`, owner card "A. One coordinated move"): the code those imports sat in moved to cat-harness-tools, which names `bootstrap-tools` in its own `needs`. Measured after the move, no file under `cat-harness/` imports `bootstrap-tools`, so the edge named nothing. needs[ "bootstrap" ] . _jsonldPrefixes_commentThe external vocabularies this layer's JSON-LD speaks (schemas/kg/jsonld-prefixes.ts; bean folio-assistant-63q4, owner 2026-10-14). Measured 2026-10-14: these are emitted (doco, prov, dcterms by the block/library/site generators; skos by the glossary export; cito by block siblings; rdfs by the named-subgraph documents, through ns/subgraph/v1.jsonld's aliases). deo, oa, csvw and fhir are bound in CONTENT_CONTEXT but emitted by no code and no document, so they are not declared: the generated context will not carry them. jsonldPrefixes{ "doco": "http://purl.org/spar/doco/", "cito": "http://purl.org/spar/cito/", "prov": "http://www.w3.org/ns/prov#", "skos": "http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#", "dcterms": "http://purl.org/dc/terms/", "rdfs": "http://www.w3.org/2000/01/rdf-schema#" } . mountApprovers[ "litlfred" ] . _cat_bootstrap_commentNO `bootstrap` DIRECTORY IS DECLARED HERE, and that is the owner's ruling of 2026-09-21 ("neither") on bean `pve3`, not an omission. This file used to declare `bootstrap/skills/` with `scope: "repository"`, which resolves against the REPOSITORY root rather than this instance — so bootstrap's skills and roles landed in folio-assistant's graph while the entry lived here. It did NOT declare `bootstrap/workflows/`, deliberately, because #432 measured bootstrap's process leaking into the root graph 88 times. The root therefore carried HALF of bootstrap, and the two symptoms were one asymmetry: a `lanes` entry on a bootstrap role minted `bindsLane -> role/<Lane>` pointing at a lane node only bootstrap's own export mints (four dangling links, measured 2026-09-21 by restoring `lanes` and watching `kg-export.test.ts` refuse it), and bootstrap's `kg-navigation` collided by name with `skills/folio-core/kg-navigation` in the published docs (bean `v3se`). `pve3` put the choice as BOTH halves or NEITHER; both would undo #432's isolation and put a process the root does not own into its published graph. Under NEITHER, bootstrap's skills are published through `bootstrap.jsonld` and its own instance page, which is where an instance's own graph belongs. The old entry's rationale is preserved in the bean rather than here, because a rationale for a declaration that no longer exists reads as a declaration to a skimming reader. knownSubstrates[ { "name": "who-world-health-data-hub", "title": "WHO World Health Data Hub", "status": "proposed", "note": "Proposed by the owner 2026-09-30 as a repository per large KG asset type; no layer or repository yet." } ] . contentTranslations[ { "contentType": "docs", "name": "Docs site (Markdown)", "formats": [ { "id": "markdown", "name": "Markdown", "extensions": [ ".md" ], "extractModule": "pipeline/pot-extract.ts", "injectModule": "pipeline/po-inject.ts" } ], "rtlSupported": true, "notes": "The harness's own just-the-docs site, and the profile of any layer that declares no content type: every site this platform publishes is Markdown, translated through the generic pipeline (bean 0r7u)." } ] . _subscriptions_commentIssue #1719, bean `tmo5`: the first real subscription. iHRIS was an `associatedHarnesses` entry (issue #1146) until it became a subscription; the schema allows one relation per remote thing, so the association was dropped when the subscription was added. It stays in the known-substrates registry as `exists`, now derived from this entry. No harness is chosen, and that is deliberate. Owner, 2026-09-23: "i dont want to publish at /folio-assistant/ihris/; that's a platform change, certainly not a materialized publish". Instantiating `ihris` would put it in this site's navbar, so it stays referenced and is published from its own repository at https://litlfred.github.io/ihris/. Only the `skills` subgraph is chosen, and assets are on demand. Each copy still passes the five gates of `Process_MaterializeRemote`, and the upstream has no root licence, so the copyright gate is the person's to answer. The snapshot is under `subscriptions/` and is written by `bun run cat kg:subscribe`. subscriptions[ { "id": "ihris", "repository": "litlfred/ihris", "ref": "7a89f67282f53c1ace2e1cfe4d913ebfad466783", "subgraphs": [ "skills" ], "assets": { "policy": "on-demand" }, "harnesses": [], "note": "The iHRIS folio, published from its own repository: its skills are chosen for materialisation, and its harness stays referenced." } ] .

Step 3a moves the standalone MCP server (adapters/mcp-server/) in and nothing else, so this declaration names only what exists (bean dh4f). The layout MIRRORS cat-harness's (adapters/, src/, test/) so that, as step 3b moves src/ here, the relative imports between modules that move together come out unchanged. namecat-harness-tools repositorylitlfred/cat-harness-tools version0.1.0 _title_commentThe HUMAN display name, for the LHS navbar's harness tabs (bean `t3n8`). `name` stays the machine identifier that filenames and `needs` edges resolve against. titleC@T Harness Tools descriptionWhat implements the harness's Tool definitions: the MCP servers, their tool registrars and routes. Two questions, not one. catalogues / templates asks whether a .po exists at all for each extractable .pot; the string columns ask how much of the catalogues that DO exist is done. A locale can be near 100% translated across a handful of catalogues while most of its templates have none — which is why the first column is not folded into the rest. “no basis” is not zero. A share over an empty denominator is undefined, and rendering it as 0% would report a measurement this run did not make. One directory per table, each named. translation-sources is a graph KIND, and more than one instance may declare it; the first table measures the directory named in the subtitle, and each instance below it gets its own table for its own declared directory. They are never summed: two instances' catalogues answer two questions. A catalogue sitting in an instance that has not declared the directory is invisible here — which is a gap in that declaration rather than a locale with no work done, and the two must not read the same. Fuzzy is counted apart from translated. A fuzzy entry has a translation and needs review; adding it to translated would flatter exactly the entries a reviewer must look at.

21932897144e-2.title: Digital Transformation Handbook (DTH) dth
21932897144e-2.content: A WHO guidance publication on digitalising one area of a health system — an L1 publication whose body is a planning method rather than recommendations. It sits within the DIIG process and should use the DPI-H Reference Architecture (owner, 2026-10-01). Its domain sections map onto smart-kg L2 (DAK) classes: a DTH states for a health-system area what a DAK states for a guideline. Structure read from the three DTHs ingested in smart-base/library; a section is required only where all three have it. The Reference Architecture for DPI-H calls itself "A Digital Transformation Handbook for DPI-H" and is cited here as the architecture the others should reference. semi-fixed structure · 22 section(s) · extends l1 · declared by smart-base in smart-base/document-kinds/dth.json . | # | Section | | What it holds | Source | . | 1 | Audience and how to use this handbookaudience-and-how-to-use | required | Target users/roles per chapter and the stepwise reading path through the handbook.computed from: library | who-iris/library/9789240093362-eng, 2. The seven phases have ONE source, DIIG §1.1 Fig. 1.1.1 (owner, 2026-10-03, #1984: "use one DIIG seven phase figure as source"); a DTH cites that figure for them, and the copies the handbooks print (PHC Fig. 6, SC Fig 5, PC Fig. 4) are reproductions of it, not further sources. The primary health care DTH places itself in Phase 5, determining health content requirements; the Reference Architecture's Figure 1, which adapts the DIIG figure, places the supply chain and product catalogue handbooks in Phase 7, and the Reference Architecture itself across Phases 1-4. To inform DAK scope. | the kind's sources | . | 2 | Generic Personasgeneric-personas | required | Roles, responsibilities, and essential interventions performed by targeted personas. Example for human centered design. | the kind's sources | . | 3 | User Scenariosuser-scenarios | required | Brief narrative description of how the targeted personas may engage with the digital system. Example for human centered design. | the kind's sources | . | 4 | Business Processes & Workflowsgeneric-business-processes-and-workflows | required | Generic workflows representing clinical and non-clinical processes. To inform when data is collected and used & required features. | the kind's sources | . | 5 | Core Data Elementscore-data-elements | required | Data elements, used for clinical decision-making, indicators, and other data needs. To inform data collection forms and L3 interoperability requirements. | the kind's sources | . | 6 | Decision Support Logicdecision-support-logic | required | Decision tables representing counselling and treatment algorithms, and any other logic used to determine workflow paths or clinical actions. | the kind's sources | . | 7 | Scheduling Logicscheduling-logic | required | Decision tables representing scheduling logic according to care plans. Previously combined with decision support logic. Not yet a field of its own in WHO's DAK logical model. | the kind's sources | . | 8 | Indicators & Monitoringprogramme-indicators | required | Indicators for reporting & monitoring with numerator, denominator of data elements. Linking person centered data to aggregate. | the kind's sources | . | 9 | Functional & Non-functional Requirementsfunctional-and-non-functional-requirements | required | A non-exhaustive list of key functions and non-functional requirements for a digital tracking and decision support system. To inform system features. | the kind's sources | . | 10 | Test Scenariostest-scenarios | required | Test data and scenarios to check a system against the other nine components. A test harness to run them. | the kind's sources | . To inform DAK scope. | the kind's sources | . | 2 | Generic Personasgeneric-personas | required | Roles, responsibilities, and essential interventions performed by targeted personas. Example for human centered design. | the kind's sources | . | 3 | User Scenariosuser-scenarios | required | Brief narrative description of how the targeted personas may engage with the digital system. To inform system features. | the kind's sources | . | 10 | Test Scenariostest-scenarios | required | Test data and scenarios to check a system against the other nine components. e64064f93b5e-2.title: Digital Transformation Handbook (DTH) dth
e64064f93b5e-2.content: A WHO guidance publication on digitalising one area of a health system — an L1 publication whose body is a planning method rather than recommendations. It sits within the DIIG process and should use the DPI-H Reference Architecture (owner, 2026-10-01). Its domain sections map onto smart-kg L2 (DAK) classes: a DTH states for a health-system area what a DAK states for a guideline. Structure read from the three DTHs ingested in smart-base/library; a section is required only where all three have it. The Reference Architecture for DPI-H calls itself "A Digital Transformation Handbook for DPI-H" and is cited here as the architecture the others should reference. semi-fixed structure · 22 section(s) · extends l1 · declared by smart-base in smart-base/document-kinds/dth.json . | # | Section | | What it holds | Source | . | 1 | Audience and how to use this handbookaudience-and-how-to-use | required | Target users/roles per chapter and the stepwise reading path through the handbook.computed from: library | who-iris/library/9789240093362-eng, 2. e64064f93b5e-5.title: L2 Digital Transformation Handbook (DTH) l2-dth
e64064f93b5e-5.content: An L2 Digital Transformation Handbook folio authored on top of an L1 WHO Digital Transformation Handbook and the DPI-H Reference Architecture (smart-ra). It extends the L1 DTH structure with computable L2 linkage and DAK-kind components: every domain term links via SKOS to the shared DPI-H Reference Architecture glossary or an upstream DTH glossary, narrative and structured blocks link to ArchiMate 3.1 elements and views in smart-ra, roles are authored as DAK persona or actor-definition blocks bound to BPMN 2.0 swimlanes, business processes carry BPMN 2.0 companions and structured step tables, decision logic is extracted into DMN 1.3 decision tables citing their source passages, and L1 normative coverage accounts for every normative sentence in the source handbook. semi-fixed structure · 6 section(s) · extends dth · declared by smart-base in smart-base/document-kinds/l2-dth.json . | # | Section | | What it holds | Source | . | 1 | Cross-instance SKOS glossary alignmentskos-glossary-alignment | required | Domain terms and abbreviations in the handbook's SKOS glossary, linked via SKOS match relations (exactMatch, closeMatch, broadMatch, narrowMatch, broader, related) to the shared DPI-H Reference Architecture (smart-ra) glossary or mounted upstream DTH glossaries (such as dth-sc, dth-pc, dth-hrh), and referenced from narrative and DAK blocks.computed from: glossary, librarymodelled by: sgkg-l1#terminology-code | who-iris/library/9789240093362-eng, Abbreviations p.v; 27c116ac03d6.title: Research and analysis
27c116ac03d6.content: Findings gathered to inform a decision, not a proposal of what to build. The sibling Proposals section sets out options and what each costs; this one records what was found out — about other projects, about tools a skill could be satisfied by, about the repository itself. Every page here follows the design-record rules in the placement skill: it is dated, it says what it was true of and where each fact came from, and it names what it could not establish. A survey of other projects goes stale faster than anything else in docs/, so read its date before its conclusions. A finding that changes how agents work does not stay here: its rule moves into the skill it governs, and this page keeps the evidence. | page | question | . | Prior art | Are other open-source projects taking a similar approach? Eighteen projects across skills, work plans, roles and processes, agent frameworks, and documents with and without formal backing, each checked against its own repository on 2026-09-23. None combines all of it; the nearest per axis are Superpowers, Beads, BMAD-METHOD, Camunda and leanblueprint. Includes a work items ↔ Beads health comparison (rechecked 2026-10-24) | . | Table-of-contents extraction | Which way of inferring a PDF’s table of contents works when the PDF has no outline? Five methods scored on 2026-10-06 against the 13 corpus PDFs that carry one, outline hidden as the answer key. Layout — a printed contents page, else heading styles from font metrics — reaches title F1 0.88, the consensus of all methods 0.92 — 0.83 on 20 held-out PDFs — against 0.30 for the text patterns it replaced; Grobid measured at 0.59 (CRF models); Nougat handed to an agent with network access | . | Forced along a BPMN vs managing it | When the same BPMN diagram (test-plan-execution.bpmn + qa-report-signing.bpmn) is run over the same 10-case task bank under token-machine step enforcement (forced) vs handing the full diagram in context (self-managed), do outcomes change, and at what compute?. Not yet answered: the two-arm runner exists, but so far (2026-10-26) it has been run only with a simulated agent (a hand-written step script), not a model. That run shows the token machine refuses every scripted shortcut, the forced arm’s per-turn prompt is about 31× smaller (byte-count estimate), and the folio-test-run/v1 two-hash split works; its outcome rates hold by construction and are not evidence about models | .

462faf32fe10.title: Processes — cat-harness

588eb9d40acf.content: Every one of the 92 diagrams has a rendered SVG. Activities carrying no <bootstrap.processes:skill ref> — a census, not a gap list . 59 across 34 diagram(s). This section reported them as defects in its first version, and that was wrong: beans luke and uuhu worked this corpus from 90 down to this remainder and settled what is left. luke: “coverage is deliberately NOT gated — a human sign-off step has no skill”. uuhu added the call-activity exemption and recorded that its own remainder “are not gaps”. 25 are call activities, which delegate to a subprocess — the skill is named there, and naming it twice would be one fact in two places. 0068a61ea39d.title: Findings
0068a61ea39d.content: Every one of the 3 diagrams has a rendered SVG. Activities carrying no <bootstrap.processes:skill ref> — a census, not a gap list . 1 across 1 diagram(s). This section reported them as defects in its first version, and that was wrong: beans luke and uuhu worked this corpus from 90 down to this remainder and settled what is left. luke: “coverage is deliberately NOT gated — a human sign-off step has no skill”. uuhu added the call-activity exemption and recorded that its own remainder “are not gaps”. 1 are call activities, which delegate to a subprocess — the skill is named there, and naming it twice would be one fact in two places. The other 0 are listed by lane, because the lane is what says whether a person, a pipeline or an agent performs the step, and only the last of those has a skill to run. | lane | steps |—|—| . No verdict is offered on which of these is a gap, and that is the honest state rather than a hedge: distinguishing a person’s judgement step from an agent step somebody forgot needs the lane’s actor KIND, which a free-text lane name does not give — process-model.ts notes sixty lanes spell two dozen positions. The lane’s partitionElementRef is the join that would answer it, and it is present on 0 of these 0 steps — which is the measurement, not an impression. An earlier draft of this sentence said few of these and was counting whether the lane had a NAME, a different question with a different answer.

1fcef6b32258.title: Indexing evidence
1fcef6b32258.content: Indexing is adding an index to a document or a graph: keywords for each section, glossary terms, subject terms from a controlled vocabulary, a search that finds what is said in other words, and near-duplicate proposals. Each indexing method rests on papers held in the library. A skill applies the method (uses-methodology), Tools carry the skill out (satisfies), and processes call the skill from an activity. Read a row left to right and you have the evidence for that piece of indexing work. A skill with no method has no held evidence yet, and is listed at the end. The keywords these methods extract from every library entry are on the Keywords page, with the extraction variants side by side. 4indexing methods 10papers cited as their evidence 4skills applying them 3indexing skills with no evidence yet

7eb96ad8adfd.doc: WireGen: wireframing from a written design intent
7eb96ad8adfd.title: WireGen: from a written intent to a reviewed, mid-fidelity wireframe
7eb96ad8adfd.content: Adopted in part, 2026-09-23, by the owner’s direction. In the owner’s words: “make methodology/utilize/integrate into existing processes. need both web and mobile layouts in usability reviews. wireframe is part of design process for adjudication”. Integrated into CRDM, 2026-10-14. crdm-requirements-definition.bpmn calls Process_WireframeDesignReview (Call_Wireframe) whenever a requirement changes a rendered surface, before anything is built; the candidates become assets of the request’s proposal, and the requester or BA chooses one at BA_ReviewReqs. See wireframe-design-review. Placed in cat-harness (owner, 2026-09-23: “put wireframe in cat-harness, not folio-assist(-core)”). The method is domain-neutral, and methodology-adoption §4 puts a domain-neutral method in the harness. It was first drafted in litlfred/ihris, and its first use was that folio’s data-model site. Issue #1023.

bd4eda7a0ad7.doc: WireGen: wireframing from a written design intent
bd4eda7a0ad7.title: What the method says (rendered faithfully)
bd4eda7a0ad7.content: Section numbers below are the paper’s. | Design intent comes first, as language (§3, §5.2). A short natural-language description of what the screen is for and what it holds. | Mid-fidelity is the target (§3.1.1). The wireframe is monochrome and simplified, but it carries real content, semantic icons and interactive elements, not boxes and placeholder text. | HTML is the carrier (§3.1.2, §3.3). The screen is expressed as a UI-specific HTML-like language. Raw output is post-processed against UI guidance: icons chosen by meaning, typography, and layout guidelines (§3.3). | Evaluation is blind and comparative (§4.3). Independent raters with design background see the description and a shuffled grid of candidates, without knowing which generator produced which. They mark candidates significantly better or significantly worse. | Usefulness is asked separately (§5.2): whether a wireframe is effective for inspiration, whether it relates to the description, and whether the candidates are diverse. These are rated on a 5-point scale. | Refinement is iterative (§6). Intent, then wireframe, then a revised intent, then a revised wireframe. | .

16ab6bd69f2b.doc: WireGen: wireframing from a written design intent
16ab6bd69f2b.title: What this platform adopts, and what it refuses
16ab6bd69f2b.content: |   | adopted | refused, with the reason | . | intent statement | yes: every candidate set starts from one, and it is the criterion candidates are judged against | none | . | mid-fidelity with real content | yes: real content from the folio (for iHRIS: real form classes, fields, lists) | none | . | HTML carrier + guideline post-processing | yes: wireframes are HTML, and the mechanical checks are the post-processing gate | none | . | fine-tuning an LLM on Rico / Screen2Words (§3.1, §3.2) | no | That is how the authors generate; it is not a review method. Candidates here may come from a person, an agent or any tool. The method applies to what they produce. | . | blind, shuffled comparison | yes: reviewers are not told a candidate’s author | none | . | better/worse marks and Likert ratings | the structure, not the arithmetic | methodology-adoption refuses scoring and summing. A mean of Likert ratings reads as a measurement of a judgement. Reviewers record per-criterion pass / warn / fail with a reason. | . | mobile only (the paper’s data is Android, §3.1.1) | extended: both web and mobile layouts are required in every usability review (owner, 2026-09-23) | The source’s scope is narrower than our need. We state the extension rather than claim the paper supports it. | . | the reported numbers (77.5%, the user study) | no | They describe the authors’ model and datasets. Nothing here depends on them. | .

a05688021463.doc: WireGen: wireframing from a written design intent
a05688021463.title: How it plugs into existing processes
a05688021463.content: . | Review record: each criterion gets entries from a script (the mechanical checks), an agent and a human, in block-qa/v1 sidecars. This is folio-assistant’s existing multi-reviewer primitive. | Disagreement: when entries for one criterion disagree, the candidate set enters Process_Adjudication (processes/process/adjudication.bpmn). The adjudication leads, the checker’s entry is kept, and the dispensation carries its reason. | Choice between surviving candidates: a one-off choice, so it uses the decision-analysis methodology. Rejected candidates are kept with the reason they lost. | After build: the rendered result does not go through theme-ui-review.bpmn any more. Theme and UI review moved to ingestion only, by owner ruling (work item 9fdi, 2026-09-24): it runs when the graphical assets arrive, from ingest-theme.bpmn, and still requires both web and mobile layouts (#1023). A post-build visual look for a wiregen output is therefore not provided by that process — recorded so it is not assumed. | . The executable form is processes/ui/wireframe-design-review.bpmn. The operating skill is wireframe-design-review. The mechanical checks are the Tool wireframe-check.

f70f18797a5f.doc: WireGen: wireframing from a written design intent
f70f18797a5f.title: Refusals
f70f18797a5f.content: . | Never review a single candidate as if it were a choice. The method is comparative; at least two candidates, or say why only one exists. | Never accept a wireframe reviewed at one viewport. A web-only or mobile-only review is incomplete, not passed. | Never show a reviewer who made a candidate. Blindness is the method’s evidence of fairness. | Never let placeholder text through. Lorem ipsum makes it a low-fidelity wireframe, and the method is about mid-fidelity. | Never average the ratings into a score. | .

62d48837c4a4.doc: WireGen: wireframing from a written design intent
62d48837c4a4.title: WireGen: wireframing from a written design intent
62d48837c4a4.content: ← All methodologies . wiregen — declared by cat-harness — source held . Applies when. Designing a USER INTERFACE, for example a page layout, a navigation scheme or a visualiser, where the choice between candidate designs has to be reviewed and, when reviewers disagree, adjudicated. It is a design-generation and design-evaluation method. It does not choose between non-UI options (use the decision-analysis methodology) or grade evidence. It does not by itself settle a disagreement: that is adjudication. Origin. Sidong Feng, Mingyue Yuan, Jieshan Chen, Zhenchang Xing and Chunyang Chen, “Designing with Language: Wireframing UI Design Intent with Generative Large Language Models”, arXiv:2312.07755v1 [cs.HC], 12 Dec 2023. Ingested in full at cat-harness/library/corpus/ui/arxiv-2312.07755v1/. The source states no licence, and its licence could not be established (see check:source-licence). 544f4b7bd67b.doc: ODRL 2.2 — what a party may do, as permission and prohibition rules over actions
544f4b7bd67b.title: Its sources: what is held, what is not
544f4b7bd67b.content: | source | held | what this node takes from it | . | ODRL Information Model 2.2 (W3C REC, 2018) | ✅ library/w3c-2018-odrl-model-2-2 | the model, its classes and every MUST quoted below | . | ODRL Vocabulary & Expression 2.2 | ❌ not held | the Common Vocabulary actions (display, modify, …) and their includedIn; the JSON-LD context. The includedIn values in ODRL_ACTIONS are not verified against it here | . | post-REC errata | ❌ not held | none | . A caution on section references. f8ed30094530.doc: ODRL 2.2 — what a party may do, as permission and prohibition rules over actions
f8ed30094530.title: The load-bearing idea, in the standard’s words
f8ed30094530.content: “The ODRL Information Model represents Policies that express Permissions, Prohibitions and Duties related to the usage of Asset resources. The Information Model explicitly expresses what is allowed and what is not allowed by the Policy” — §2. Its terms (§1.3): a Policy is “A group of one or more Rules”; an Action “An operation on an Asset”; a Permission “The ability to exercise an Action over an Asset”; a Prohibition “The inability to exercise an Action over an Asset”; a Duty “The obligation to exercise an agreed Action”; a Party “An entity or a collection of entities that undertake Roles in a Rule”; a Constraint “A boolean/logical expression that refines an Action and Party/Asset collection or the conditions applicable to a Rule”. Three mechanisms carry the method, and the platform uses all three: . | Actions inherit through includedIn. “a Permission or Prohibition of an encompassing Action is inherited by all Actions with an includedIn relationship”, and every action other than use and transfer “MUST have one includedIn property value” (§2.4). | Constraints conjoin. “When multiple Constraints apply to the same Rule … they are interpreted as conjunction and all MUST be satisfied” (§2.5). | Conflicts are resolved by a declared strategy: “perm: the Permissions MUST override the Prohibitions; prohibit: the Prohibitions MUST override the Permissions; invalid: the entire Policy MUST be void” (§2.10). | . And one that makes extension legitimate: a policy may “Use an ODRL Profile that declares the supported vocabulary” (§2.1), and new actions are made by creating “an instance of an Action and define its includedIn parent Action” (§3.3).

c51ebe0e18ce.doc: ODRL 2.2 — what a party may do, as permission and prohibition rules over actions
c51ebe0e18ce.title: What this platform adopts — class by class
c51ebe0e18ce.content: | ODRL | here | where | . | Policy (Set, Offer, Agreement), uid, profile, inheritFrom, conflict | adopted; both live policies are Sets with conflict: odrl:prohibit | OdrlPolicySchema, policies/*.jsonld | . | Permission | adopted: one rule per (actor, action), migrated from the old per-actor lists | policies/folio-defaults.jsonld, policies/http-gateway.jsonld | . | Prohibition | adopted in the schema and the evaluator; no live policy states one — both files’ prohibition is [] or absent | permits() in schemas/content/odrl.ts | . | Action + includedIn | adopted: the folio profile’s actions each name a broader action, ending at ODRL’s odrl:display/modify/annotate/derive/translate/execute under odrl:use | skills/permissions/permissions.json, ODRL_ACTIONS, broaderOrSelf() | . | Party — assignee, assigner | adopted as the assignee of each rule, an actor id from scenarios/actors/, plus the profile party cat-harness:anyone for an unauthenticated reader | OdrlRuleSchema, ANYONE | . | Asset — target | adopted as an optional target string | ruleApplies() | . | Constraint | adopted for three profile leftOperands — cat-harness:process, cat-harness:task, cat-harness:role — and four operators eq, neq, isAnyOf, isNoneOf, conjoined | OdrlConstraintSchema, constraintHolds() | . | Profile | profile is required; the action half of the profile is permissions.json | OdrlPolicySchema | . The evaluator is the question every caller asks — the BPMN task gate (src/workflow/authorize.ts, action perform-task), the HTTP routes (src/core/rbac.ts), and the auth_whoami tool (src/tools/auth.ts) — all through decide(), over policies loaded by src/core/access.ts.

2f5d11c6b8e1.doc: ODRL 2.2 — what a party may do, as permission and prohibition rules over actions
2f5d11c6b8e1.title: What it refuses or departs from, with reasons
2f5d11c6b8e1.content: Each item is a place where the code differs from the held text. They are stated so nobody reads @conformsTo w3c-odrl as full conformance. | Duty, obligation, consequence, remedy — refused. No reader exists, and .strict() rejects the keys “because a rule that silently means less than it says is exactly the failure a permission file must not have” (schemas/content/odrl.ts). A Permission carrying an unfulfilled duty would be read as unconditional, which is worse than refusing it. | Refinements, AssetCollection, PartyCollection, LogicalConstraint, rightOperandReference, dataType, unit, status, implies, partOf, hasPolicy, transfer — refused, for the same reason: no reader. | target is optional; ODRL requires it. §2.6.1: “A Permission MUST have one target property value of type Asset” (Prohibition likewise, §2.6.2). Here an absent target means the layer’s whole graph. Every live rule omits it. | The default conflict strategy is prohibit; ODRL’s is invalid. §2.10: “If the conflict property is not explicitly set, the default of invalid will be used.” The code names this as “OUR rule rather than claimed as ODRL’s”; both live policies set odrl:prohibit explicitly, so the difference does not fire today. Kept by owner ruling, 2026-10-01 (work item jcet): an unstated clash denies rather than voiding the policy — a deliberate profile departure, not an oversight; odrl.test.ts pins it. | Across policies, any deny wins. decide() evaluates each policy and lets a prohibition in one beat a permission in another. ODRL’s merge rule is different — inherited conflict values are replicated and “If a Policy has multiple conflict property values … then the entire Policy MUST be void” (§2.10). Only the child’s conflict is read by permits(). | A circular inheritFrom is tolerated, not refused. §2.9: “Inheritance MUST NOT be circular.” effectiveRules() walks with a visited set, so a cycle terminates silently instead of failing. (Cycles are deliberately allowed in the action graph — the owner’s “doensnt necc need to be rooted acyclic graph”. That sits uneasily with §2.4, which calls includedIn transitive, says “the Actions form ancestor relationships”, and requires every action to reach use or transfer; a cycle among profile actions is a departure, not a reading.) | No-match answers unknown, a third value. This node found no held text that defines the outcome when no rule matches; unknown — never permit, never deny — is the platform’s rule (Decision in schemas/content/odrl.ts), so task-authorization can report it as a finding. | Role eligibility is added on top. permits() denies a permitted request whose cat-harness:role the actor is not eligible for. That is role-model’s separation of what a lane needs from what an actor may do; it is not ODRL. | Cardinalities not enforced: an empty policy validates (§2.1: “MUST have at least one permission, prohibition, or obligation”); an Offer needs no assigner and an Agreement needs no policy-level assignee (§2.1.2, §2.1.3); and the profile IRI is never checked, although §3.2 says a processor that “does not recognise the ODRL Profile identifier(s) … MUST stop processing”. | The profile is not published as RDF. §3.3 asks that new terms “must also be defined as a skos:Concept”; permissions.json is plain JSON with id, title, description, includedIn, and the profile IRI https://litlfred.github.io/folio-assistant/ns/folio-odrl is not shown to resolve. | .

ce0061cb8805.doc: ODRL 2.2 — what a party may do, as permission and prohibition rules over actions

ce0061cb8805.content: . | Not for source licences. ODRL’s own subject is content usage, and the natural reading would be a library entry’s licence as an ODRL Offer. That is not what happens: licence.json records a status and an SPDX id, checked by bun run cat check:source-licence (scripts/check-source-licence.ts). | Not for identity. Which login is which actor is GitHub’s answer (src/core/github-auth.ts), never a policy’s — policies/README.md. | Not for logging. That is PROV-O (schemas/content/prov.ts), chosen alongside it. | .

6d0a1c686056.doc: ODRL 2.2 — what a party may do, as permission and prohibition rules over actions
6d0a1c686056.title: ODRL 2.2 — what a party may do, as permission and prohibition rules over actions
6d0a1c686056.content: ← All methodologies . odrl-policies — declared by cat-harness — source held . Applies when. What an actor may DO — may this party perform this action, here? Use it when a grant or a refusal has to be written down so a machine can evaluate it: who holds an action, scoped to a process, a task or a role, and which broader action it falls under. It answers permit, deny or nobody has said. It does NOT answer who is involved in an activity (raci), which lane an actor may act in (role-model), or how a decision is reached (kepner-tregoe, dmn). It is not used here for source licences, which are recorded as SPDX ids in each library entry’s licence.json. Origin. W3C, “ODRL Information Model 2.2”, W3C Recommendation 15 February 2018, edited by Renato Iannella and Serena Villata, produced by the W3C Permissions and Obligations Expression Working Group. The held copy is the Working Group’s own staged REC snapshot (github.com/w3c/poe), not compared byte for byte with the w3.org copy and without later errata — see the entry’s licence.json. The companion “ODRL Vocabulary & Expression 2.2”, which the model defers to for normative serialisation and the Common Vocabulary, is NOT held. 24bb51c6187e.doc: RACI — who is involved in an activity, and in which of four ways
24bb51c6187e.title: RACI — involvement, in four kinds
24bb51c6187e.content: Adopted on the owner’s ruling, 2026-09-22 (work item 2xfl): RACI is a methodology, not a house practice, so it has a node here. Until that ruling it existed only as a skill, and the methodology graph reported five nodes where a reader might reasonably expect it to report this one too.

de8af9899bd8.doc: RACI — who is involved in an activity, and in which of four ways
de8af9899bd8.title: ⚠ The cited source backs ONE sentence of this node, and nothing else
de8af9899bd8.content: evidence points at Dusengumuremyi (2026), ingested 2026-09-23. It earns its place only as a secondary rendering of the four roles — its §2.1, verbatim from sections/page-002.md: . a classic project management instrument delineating four roles: Responsible (doer), Accountable (owner), Consulted (input provider), and Informed (notified). Everything else in that paper is rejected, and the rejection is load-bearing rather than fastidious. Its own Data Availability statement reads “No new datasets were generated or analyzed during this study” while its abstract claims 1,247 decision events and its §4.1 reports t(1245)=47.3, p<.001; its abstract’s headline 92.4 % detection rate appears nowhere in its findings, which say 78.4 %; and its running head claims Journal of International Business Studies “Vol. 1, 2026” while its own reference list cites that journal at vol. 53 in 2022. Work item thb1 holds the full assessment with every item checkable against the ingested pages. So: cite this source for the four letters. Never cite it for a claim about what RACI achieves. No efficacy, latency, error-rate or risk-detection statement anywhere in this repository may rest on it. That split is why evidence here is not the same kind of backing swot has. swot rests on two sources that survive reading whole; this rests on one paragraph of one paper that does not. check:methodology-evidence counts nodes with a resolvable source and will now count this one — the axis measures whether a citation resolves, not whether a reader would accept it, and conflating those is what this box exists to prevent.

09d4d8499523.doc: RACI — who is involved in an activity, and in which of four ways
09d4d8499523.title: The four letters
09d4d8499523.content: | letter | means | direction | . | Responsible | does the work | may be several | . | Accountable | carries the decision; answers for the outcome | exactly one | . | Consulted | asked for input before | two-way | . | Informed | told after | one-way | . The axis that makes it a method rather than a list is time and direction: C happens before and is a conversation; I happens after and is a broadcast. Collapsing them turns consultation into notification, which is the failure the letters exist to keep apart.

4f4b63219fb5.doc: RACI — who is involved in an activity, and in which of four ways
4f4b63219fb5.title: Exactly one Accountable
4f4b63219fb5.content: The method’s central constraint, and the one most often broken in practice. A chart with two A’s does not record a shared decision — it records that nobody established who answers for the outcome, and it reads as complete while doing so. Zero is also a breach, once a row claims anything at all. A half-filled row is worse than an empty one for the same reason: the chart looks answered. A row where the same party is both Accountable and Consulted is not a row with two facts in it. Asking yourself is not consultation, and that pairing is how consulted becomes a formality while the chart still reads complete.

f899328cbd28.doc: RACI — who is involved in an activity, and in which of four ways
f899328cbd28.title: What RACI is not
f899328cbd28.content: . | Not a decision method. A is who answers for a decision, not how it is reached. Reaching it is kepner-tregoe or dmn; recording it is madr. | Not an approval gate. Answering for an outcome and signing off on one are different acts, and a method that conflated them would let a chart stand in for a gate. | Not a permission model. What a party may do in general is a different question from who is involved in this activity, and the two cross-cut. | Not a party registry. RACI names roles in rows; it does not establish who exists. Something else has to say that first. | .

9b71c4d9884d.doc: RACI — who is involved in an activity, and in which of four ways
9b71c4d9884d.title: The primary is still not held
9b71c4d9884d.content: A secondary rendering is cited above; the primary is not, and the gap has narrowed rather than closed. literature-search’s outcome 3, recorded so the next agent does not repeat the search: nothing was found because nothing could be fetched. Measured 2026-09-22 — doi.org, pmi.org and every open-access aggregator fail through this container’s proxy; only raw.githubusercontent.com answers. Candidates worth fetching, unverified and listed as leads rather than as provenance: . | candidate | why it is a candidate | access | . | PMI, PMBOK Guide — the responsibility assignment matrix (RAM) | the most commonly cited formal treatment | not open access | . | The Linear Responsibility Chart literature (Cleland & King and successors) | commonly named as the earlier form RACI descends from | books, not open access | . RACI and kepner-tregoe were in the same bucket, and RACI has left it. For both, the commonly cited sources are books and paid standards, so no open-access primary exists to fetch, and closing the gap needed either a copy or a decision to render from an open secondary — the route swot took. The owner made that decision for RACI on 2026-09-23. kepner-tregoe is still in the bucket, and the same two exits are still open to it.

400040ca9841.doc: RACI — who is involved in an activity, and in which of four ways
400040ca9841.title: RACI — who is involved in an activity, and in which of four ways
400040ca9841.content: ← All methodologies . raci — declared by cat-harness — source held . Applies when. Who is involved in an activity, and how. Use it when a process or a breakdown exists and the question is participation — who answers for this, who must be asked first, who is told afterwards. Not a decision method: a one-off choice among options is kepner-tregoe, a recurring rule is dmn, certainty of evidence is grade, the record of a decision is madr, and situation analysis before any of them is swot. RACI answers who, never what or whether. Origin. NO PRIMARY SOURCE IS HELD HERE, and the ingested one is SECONDARY. RACI is a responsibility assignment matrix from project-management practice. The text this node cites renders the four roles but does not originate them — it attributes them onward to PMI’s PMBOK Guide (2021), which is a paid standard nobody here has opened. The earlier Linear Responsibility Chart literature is the other commonly named ancestor. Both stay in §”The primary is still not held” as CANDIDATES TO FETCH, unverified, rather than asserted here as provenance. Rendering from an open secondary was the owner’s ruling of 2026-09-23 — the route swot took. See literature-search. 144b74a20453.doc: SDLC agentic landscape — mapping LLM multi-agent systems to the software development lifecycle
144b74a20453.title: SDLC Agentic Landscape — Mapping LLM Multi-Agent Systems to the Software Lifecycle
144b74a20453.content: Adopted from arXiv:2404.04834v4 (He, Treude, and Lo, 2025). The comprehensive survey maps the state of LLM-based multi-agent (LMA) systems across every phase of the software development lifecycle (SDLC), contrasting team architectures, collaboration topologies, and benchmark results. This node establishes the systematic cross-cutting comparison between the survey’s SDLC taxonomy and the 69 executable BPMN/DMN processes in this platform.

3ea5a021a18e.doc: SDLC agentic landscape — mapping LLM multi-agent systems to the software development lifecycle
3ea5a021a18e.title: 1. The Survey’s SDLC Phase Taxonomy
3ea5a021a18e.content: He et al. synthesize empirical literature into six foundational SDLC phases: . | SDLC Phase | Focus & Key Activities | Representative LMA Systems | . | 1. Requirements Engineering | Elicitation of user needs, domain modeling, requirement formalization/specification, consistency analysis, validation | Elicitron, MARE, AgileGen (Gherkin-based) | . | 2. Software Design | Architecture design, system decomposition, API contracts, interface specifications, role delegation | MetaGPT (Architect agent), ChatDev, DevLoops | . | 3. Code Generation & Implementation | Multi-agent pair programming, role-specialized coding, teacher-student self-repair, retrieval-augmented coding | INTERVENOR, Self-repair, TGen, FlowGen | . | 4. Software Quality Assurance | Test case generation, fault localization, vulnerability detection, cross-validation, static analysis pruning | ICAA, RCAgent, AgentFL, ChatDev (Tester agent) | . | 5. Software Maintenance | Automated program repair (APR), debugging, code review, test case maintenance, dependency migration | MASAI, MarsCode, AutoCodeRover, Lemner et al. | . | 6. Software Management & Collaboration | Process modeling (Waterfall vs. Agile sprints), agent coordination, resource allocation, human-agent collaboration | ChatDev, MetaGPT, AgileCoder, Think-on-Process (ToP) | .

Post-Deployment Monitoring │ Cloud root-cause analysis (e.g., RCAgent), │ │ & Live Incident Diagnosis │ runtime log anomaly detection, and active │ │ │ fault mitigation in production. │ ├────────────────────────────────┼────────────────────────────────────────────┤ │ 2. Production telemetry does not feed back into the beans graph. | Survey benchmark: Automated incident-to-bug-report translation with automated regression test generation. | Recommendation: Connect external issue alerts and crash-reporters into automated triage work items (stalled-agent-triage / issue-working). | . | Legacy Software Reverse Engineering: . | Current state: Folio-assistant excels in forward-engineering from formal specifications, guidelines, and schemas. | Survey benchmark: Agents that ingest 100k-LOC legacy C/Java codebases with no tests and reverse-engineer requirements and architecture. | Recommendation: Develop an extraction adapter to reconstruct BPMN/DMN diagrams and CRDM requirement models from existing code repositories. | . | .

8c106c8c187d.doc: SDLC agentic landscape — mapping LLM multi-agent systems to the software development lifecycle
8c106c8c187d.title: 4. Key Takeaways for Agentic Platform Design
8c106c8c187d.content: . | Process Rigor Trumps Unconstrained Multi-Agent Chat: As He et al. demonstrate in their Tetris case study, unconstrained agent conversation (e.g. ChatDev) fails repeatedly (9 out of 10 attempts failed, with the final attempt still missing core line-clearing logic) when tasks require deep stateful logic. Folio-assistant’s deterministic process boundaries, DMN rules, and compiler shims prevent these catastrophic failures. | Hybrid Deterministic/LLM Architecture is Essential: Pure generative coding degrades with complexity. Inverting the model’s responsibility from generating whole output to generating validated rules (methodologies/hybrid-llm-deterministic.md) matches the survey’s research agenda for Phase 1 (specialized agent capability enhancement). | Multi-Agent Coordination Requires Serialized Governance: Uncoordinated agent swarms produce merge chaos and duplicated work. Folio-assistant’s work item claims and merge steward fulfill the survey’s Phase 2 vision for optimizing agent synergy and leveraging industry software engineering principles. | .

07bf6224343a.doc: SDLC agentic landscape — mapping LLM multi-agent systems to the software development lifecycle
07bf6224343a.title: SDLC agentic landscape — mapping LLM multi-agent systems to the software development lifecycle
07bf6224343a.content: ← All methodologies . sdlc-agentic-landscape — declared by cat-harness — source held . Applies when. Assessing, designing, or auditing multi-agent systems and automated workflows across the software development lifecycle (SDLC). Use this framework to evaluate which SDLC phases an agentic platform covers, identify architectural gaps, and benchmark agent collaboration models (e.g., Waterfall sequential vs. Agile sprint cycles vs. dynamic workflows). Not applicable for selecting single-prompt generation techniques or isolated bug-fix heuristics. Origin. Junda He, Christoph Treude, and David Lo, “LLM-Based Multi-Agent Systems for Software Engineering: Literature Review, Vision and the Road Ahead” (arXiv:2404.04834v4, 2025), Singapore Management University. Systematic review (30pp) covering multi-agent architectures, SDLC stage taxonomies, empirical case studies, and research agendas for agentic software engineering.
