da46939b4843.title: Skills it satisfies
da46939b4843.content: A skill states the capability; this Tool is one way to exercise it. Each skill’s declared input and output contract follows, where it has one. sub-kg-lifecycle . A sub-KG is a knowledge graph staged as a directory inside a harnessed repository, declared as its own layer, that may later leave for a repository of its own. The lifecycle: declare it in place, grow it, stage it for separation (one import seam, the separation guard, a self-contained rehearsal), and then, each behind an explicit owner confirmation, create the repository, copy the staged contents in with history, re-point the declaration, verify on a fresh clone and delete the in-repo copy. The light sibling of kg-separation: use this for a DATA layer that leaves whole, and kg-separation when a graph must split into a content repository and a tools repository. Source: cat-harness/skills/kg/graph-management/sub-kg-lifecycle.md. The skill declares no I/O contract (schemas/skills/sub-kg-lifecycle/{input,output}.schema.json).

36ab5b48cf77.title: Skills it satisfies
36ab5b48cf77.content: A skill states the capability; this Tool is one way to exercise it. Each skill’s declared input and output contract follows, where it has one. translation-manager . Translation lifecycle management for folio content. Covers gettext PO/POT extraction and injection, TranslationNode manifests as KG nodes, official vs unofficial translations, staleness tracking, sign-off workflow, automatic badge rendering, the poSources fallback resolution chain, and translating into several locales as a team: one extraction, a PR per locale to main, FHIR terms as CodeSystem supplements, the untainted round trip as run, and the per-locale QA report. Source: cat-harness/library/skills/library-core/translation-manager.md. Also satisfied by: translation-extract, translation-inject, translation-roundtrip-record, translation-status, translation-validate. The skill declares no I/O contract (schemas/skills/translation-manager/{input,output}.schema.json). decision-audit . Record why a decision was made, or why a finding in it was left. Required of whoever adjudicates a gate, and of the agent that assembles the citations for them. Every overrule of a mechanical finding carries a note, and every note cites corpus evidence. Source: cat-harness/skills/process/process-core/decision-audit.md. The skill declares no I/O contract (schemas/skills/decision-audit/{input,output}.schema.json).

e526f802803b.content: Re-run a computation witness’s producer and say whether it reproduces the committed witness. Reads the command from invocation.reproduce (else python3 <scriptFile>) and the recorded package versions from environment; on a version mismatch it stops at unknown, since a different environment is not a reproduction test. 9a12a4464567.title: Screen a hand-over for injected instructions, field by field
9a12a4464567.content: Before a model reads a sub-agent’s report, a delegated prompt, a tool result or a comment from someone who is not the principal, screen it against a declared schema whose top-level fields are control (steers what the receiver does) or data (content it reads). A finding in a control field, or any field the strict schema does not declare, is REFUSED, so a report cannot extend the delegator’s plan. A finding in a data field is QUARANTINED: the original is kept and marked, never stripped. The patterns are a deterministic tripwire (instruction overrides, role and turn spoofs, fence breaks, tool-call syntax, hidden Unicode, exfiltration links, pipe-to-shell), a mitigation and not a guarantee. Exit 0 clean, 1 refused, 3 quarantined, 2 could not determine. |   |   | . | Tool | handover-screen | . | IRI | https://litlfred.github.io/folio-assistant/cat-harness/tools/handover-screen.jsonld | . | part of | https://litlfred.github.io/folio-assistant/cat-harness/cat-harness.jsonld | . | type | https://litlfred.github.io/cat-harness/v0/ns/Tool | . | declared by | cat-harness | . | source | cat-harness/tools/handover-screen/handover-screen.json | . | invoked | shell | . | qa | pass | .

199c0d97d60b.title: Where to drop a file — the queue’s upload URL
199c0d97d60b.content: Compose the forge URL a person can drop a file at, from the layer’s own declaration: the uploads graph’s directory, resolved against the ROOT its scope names, expressed relative to the repository, and appended to the origin remote as GitHub’s /upload/<branch>/<path>. Every failure is NAMED and no URL is guessed — no declaration, no declared uploads graph, a declared queue absent from disk, no origin remote, and a non-github.com remote each return a reason and a remedy instead. The declared path is relative to the LAYER and a forge URL needs it relative to the REPOSITORY, so pasting the declared path can mint a 404. |   |   | . | Tool | upload-url | . | IRI | https://litlfred.github.io/folio-assistant/cat-harness/tools/upload-url.jsonld | . | part of | https://litlfred.github.io/folio-assistant/cat-harness/cat-harness.jsonld | . | type | https://litlfred.github.io/cat-harness/v0/ns/Tool | . | declared by | cat-harness | . | source | cat-harness/tools/upload-url/upload-url.json | . | invoked | shell | . | qa | pass | .

4eba9dfea21d.content: . | Command line. No workflow in this checkout runs its command. | . As an API: its operation in the OpenAPI document and the MCP tool list of its layer. |   |   | . | install | none | . | runtime | bun | . | network | no | . | when to choose it |   | . | when | You are about to tell somebody where to put a file, in any channel. Reach for it every time, not only when unsure: a hand-written path breaks silently when a directory moves. It also answers “which queue” when a checkout declares more than one (one per layer): the answer is whichever layer root you pass, never a literal. | . | limits | It answers WHERE, and nothing else. It does not upload, does not check whether the person has write access, and cannot tell you which of several declared queues should own a given file — that is undecided and upload-routes says so rather than picking. The /upload/<branch>/<path> form is GitHub’s, so another forge gets a named refusal rather than a guess. And the URL it hands back opens the route with the FEWEST guarantees: the web form has no working tree, so no pre-commit hook and no generator run happen on it, and everything upload-routes lists has to be discharged afterwards from a checkout. | . | cost | One read of the declaration and one of the git remote; no network at run time and nothing installed. | .

60070079f31f.title: Merge train
60070079f31f.content: Build a train branch from a base SHA: merge each member (a PR number or branch) with merge-base.ts --no-regen, refusing — never hand-resolving — a member whose conflicts no declared pattern covers; then one bun run cat regen, check:l1-complete --write, every check a layer declares afterMerge (its declared writer run when red), and kg:audit:all:check; then merge origin/main, taking main’s side of generated conflicts and regenerating once more. Emits a merge-train-report/v1 JSON report. b66a8703bfee.content: A skill states the capability; this Tool is one way to exercise it. Each skill’s declared input and output contract follows, where it has one. merge-conflict-patterns . Merge the base branch in and resolve, without a person, only the conflicts a DECLARED pattern covers — generated files, generated README regions, QA sidecars — then prove the result with the gate set. Refuses the whole merge when any conflict is authored or undeclared. Use for “merge main”, “resolve the conflicts”, “the PR is conflicted again”, “auto-resolve”, and when adding a pattern for a new kind of churn. Also governs what a merge steward does with a merge-train member it had to refuse: one deduplicated work item under the PR’s own epic, a hand-back to the owning session with a fail condition, one dispatched agent when nobody owns it, one PR comment, and the close. Source: cat-harness/sdlc/skills/sdlc-core/merge-conflict-patterns.md. Also satisfied by: merge-leftover, merge-overlap. Take a feature branch to a clean, conflict-free, green, pushed state so it can be merged with no surprises: base merged in, generated files regenerated, the folio’s content-type gates run, then pushed. It does NOT merge and does NOT push to the default branch. Use for “prepare-merge”, “make it mergeable”, “ship it”. Source: cat-harness/sdlc/skills/sdlc-core/prepare-merge.md. db3a08400cfb.title: Skills it satisfies
db3a08400cfb.content: A skill states the capability; this Tool is one way to exercise it. Each skill’s declared input and output contract follows, where it has one. kg-separation . Separate a Knowledge Graph into its own repository — as a CONTENT repository (files to read, no code) and a TOOLS repository (the code that writes and checks it) — once it is too large, or its consumers or cadence differ. The end-to-end method: the signals that trigger it, the preconditions, eleven stages each with the command that gates it, the owner’s decision points, how identifiers, QA and publication move, how the parent consumes the result, rollback, and the post-move sweep that a move between the pair owes before the parent re-pins. graph-detanglement owns stages 1–3; this skill owns the rest. Bootstrap + bootstrap-tools and cat-harness + the tools layer are the worked examples. Source: cat-harness/skills/kg/graph-management/kg-separation.md. Also satisfied by: mount-from-lock, package-exports, rewrite-moved-paths, separation-cutover-check. The skill declares no I/O contract (schemas/skills/kg-separation/{input,output}.schema.json). kg-affordances . The four affordances of a conformant knowledge graph — browse, materialise, instantiate and copy-into-folio — which capabilities each requires, how each writing verb degrades cleanly when no write capability is available, and how copying an asset stamps KgAsset.source provenance. Source: cat-harness/skills/kg/kg-core/kg-affordances.md. The skill declares no I/O contract (schemas/skills/kg-affordances/{input,output}.schema.json).

60d2d8131c8e.content: A skill states the capability; this Tool is one way to exercise it. Each skill’s declared input and output contract follows, where it has one. corpus-grep . Pre-declaration corpus check. Before declaring any item “open”, “gap”, “TODO”, “open problem”, “pending derivation” — or asserting in chat that something is unresolved in the corpus — run the four-path grep checklist. 7b3ec24fd549.title: Instantiate a harness over a repository that has none: pin, mount, open the setup-only PR, render the preview
7b3ec24fd549.content: The scripted step of the initiation process (getting-started.bpmn, the repo-conversion skill §4). Reads the harness’s declaration at its pin and every needs, transitively (a need beside the layer that needs it unless –repo-of says otherwise, at its default branch’s tip unless –pin says otherwise, its declaration’s name checked), seeds them all into the repository’s index.config.json with the consent given (remote-mount --seed --whole), sets site.landing to the harness, site.agentRun and mountApprovers, mounts the closure (remote-mount: index.lock.json and the .gitignore mounts block), installs it as root workspaces with the hoisted linker, writes the root bootstrap (.github/cat.ts and .github/mount-from-lock.sh from cat-harness-tools templates/root-bootstrap/) and sets the root’s cat script to bun .github/cat.ts, so bun run cat … mounts the layers itself on a later fresh clone, re-renders the agent surface from the mounted generators, runs the harness’s instantiate:<harness> checkout script when a mounted layer declares it, and commits on a branch (default harness/). Then, unless --local, pushes the branch, provisions gh-pages when absent (`pages-bootstrap --provision`), opens the setup-only PR, runs `prepare:` when declared (what the site is built from and nobody commits, such as an IG's AST) and renders the branch's preview at gh-pages branches// (`stage-local`); with --local the site is built and composed and nothing is pushed. It imports only node:*, so it runs from a fresh clone of cat-harness-tools before anything is mounted: it lays the platform's own closure, at the pins the repository will mount, into a temporary root to run the mount from. On a repository with nothing mounted yet, run the same file from a fresh clone: `git clone --depth 1 https://github.com/litlfred/cat-harness-tools /tmp/cht && bun run /tmp/cht/scripts/instantiate-harness.ts …`. Two more flags, not declared as ports because no constrained type carries them yet: `--pin =` pins one layer of the closure, `--repo-of =<owner/repo>` says where a need lives. |   |   | . | Tool | instantiate-harness | . | IRI | https://litlfred.github.io/folio-assistant/cat-harness/tools/instantiate-harness.jsonld | . | part of | https://litlfred.github.io/folio-assistant/cat-harness/cat-harness.jsonld | . | type | https://litlfred.github.io/cat-harness/v0/ns/Tool | . | declared by | cat-harness | . | source | cat-harness/tools/instantiate-harness/instantiate-harness.json | . | invoked | shell | . | qa | pass | .

14a66ba369e1.content: A skill states the capability; this Tool is one way to exercise it. Each skill’s declared input and output contract follows, where it has one. repo-conversion . Lay folio-assistant over a repository that already exists, without losing or silently moving what is in it. Scans the tree read-only, classifies candidate files into library (external source) and content (authored here) with an explicit third bucket for what it cannot classify, scans outside the content tree for mathematical evidence and refutations, lists the content markers (an IG, a DAK, processes, work items, library, Lean, folio manifests) the harness could declare and declares only the ones the person picks, puts the three questions the scan cannot answer to the author as selections, and hands ingestion to one agent or a small swarm. Use when a user wants an existing repo converted to a folio, asks to import what is already there, asks whether their PDFs/notes/drafts can come along, or asks what else in a repository an existing harness could declare. Covers when to mount and when to subscribe instead, why there are no submodules and no .deps/, the transitive closure through needs and gitlinks, overrides by id, the lock, and the three states. dfdfe705d4d0.title: Skills it satisfies
dfdfe705d4d0.content: A skill states the capability; this Tool is one way to exercise it. Each skill’s declared input and output contract follows, where it has one. repo-conversion . Lay folio-assistant over a repository that already exists, without losing or silently moving what is in it. Scans the tree read-only, classifies candidate files into library (external source) and content (authored here) with an explicit third bucket for what it cannot classify, scans outside the content tree for mathematical evidence and refutations, lists the content markers (an IG, a DAK, processes, work items, library, Lean, folio manifests) the harness could declare and declares only the ones the person picks, puts the three questions the scan cannot answer to the author as selections, and hands ingestion to one agent or a small swarm. Use when a user wants an existing repo converted to a folio, asks to import what is already there, asks whether their PDFs/notes/drafts can come along, or asks what else in a repository an existing harness could declare. Source: cat-harness/skills/conduct/conduct-core/repo-conversion.md. Also satisfied by: instantiate-harness. The skill declares no I/O contract (schemas/skills/repo-conversion/{input,output}.schema.json). getting-started . Triage what a person means when they ask to create a folio, and route them. Five requests share one sentence — a folio in a new repo, folio-assistant overlaid on an existing repo, a second folio in a layer that already has one, a content object they called a folio, or something the filesystem cannot tell apart. Reads the repository facts, runs them through the folio-intent decision table, asks a selectable question for what facts cannot settle, scaffolds, and reports the published URL. Use whenever a user asks to create, start, set up, or initialise a folio, a paper, a DAK, an IG, or “folio-assistant” itself. Source: cat-harness/skills/conduct/conduct-core/getting-started.md. The skill declares no I/O contract (schemas/skills/getting-started/{input,output}.schema.json). folio-init . Scaffold a new folio layer from the harness — the instantiate affordance of the knowledge graph. Covers when to run folio-init vs remote-mount, what the scaffold writes, the builder shim, state branch seeding, write capability requirements, and –dry-run degradation. Source: cat-harness/skills/kg/kg-core/folio-init.md. The skill declares no I/O contract (schemas/skills/folio-init/{input,output}.schema.json).

ac3e46bd9e2f.title: Run every existing security check as one named release step
ac3e46bd9e2f.content: Run the repository’s security checks — workflow injection, secret leaks, lockfile pinning, the toolchain pin, QA reviewer permission, materialised-asset fixity — plus two advisories (dependency advisories, third-party action SHA pinning), each by name as argv. Every check is reported as pass, fail or unknown; a blocking check that fails OR could not be run refuses the release, because could-not-check is never clean. Advisories are reported and never block. 8dd23d620dfb.content: A skill states the capability; this Tool is one way to exercise it. Each skill’s declared input and output contract follows, where it has one. merge-conflict-patterns . Merge the base branch in and resolve, without a person, only the conflicts a DECLARED pattern covers — generated files, generated README regions, QA sidecars — then prove the result with the gate set. Refuses the whole merge when any conflict is authored or undeclared. Use for “merge main”, “resolve the conflicts”, “the PR is conflicted again”, “auto-resolve”, and when adding a pattern for a new kind of churn. Also governs what a merge steward does with a merge-train member it had to refuse: one deduplicated work item under the PR’s own epic, a hand-back to the owning session with a fail condition, one dispatched agent when nobody owns it, one PR comment, and the close. 55ec73f930ea.title: Mount remote harnesses at a pinned commit, only when trusted
55ec73f930ea.content: Lay down each declared remote mount — a source.remote layer in the root index.config.json, or, in a folio with no index, a remoteMounts entry on its declaration (both at once is refused) — and its dependency closure, from another repository at a full commit SHA. Write the lock, index.lock.json (a legacy <name>.mount-lock.json is read, and renamed onto it when rewritten), and, with an index, regenerate the root .gitignore block that ignores each mount path. It READS the declared mounts and never writes them: a tool that changes a mount writes through writeDeclaredMounts into index.config.json. Before anything is checked out, each mount must pass the trust gate (schemas/kg/mount-trust.ts, rule H8): a person’s consent recorded for THIS pin, or a signature in a declared trust network. No signature verifier exists yet, so a signature alone is could-not-determine and does not mount. Unsigned and unconsented is refused. --staging mounts for a preview and needs neither. A directory id an override or mountDefaults names may be one the layer declares in its <name>.json or one it declares FROM WITHIN a declared directory (skills/skills.json naming voices), resolved at the pin through instanceDirectories; an id in neither is refused at plan time. tools on an override names Tools by id and mounts each one runnable: its definition (<tools dir>/<id>/<id>.ts), its implementation (the inProcess.module, or the script its bun run cat <key> resolves to) and their import closure, walked by bootstrap-tools’ importClosure (the one closure walker), as every declared directory that closure touches — the lock still records directories only. A hydrated mount lays each chosen directory down as its published index.hydrated.jsonld only: read from the pin’s git tree when a commit carries it, otherwise fetched from the pin’s subgraph index package (the subgraph-index-<sha> release asset subgraph-index-package publishes), its tarball checked against its folio-binary-release/v1 record, its manifest against the repository, pin and harness asked for, and each file against its sha256, SubgraphHydratedSchema and the subgraph IRI; the lock records the package’s URL and sha256 so a replay fetches the same bytes. --check compares the disk against the lock and never fetches. When a run CHANGES the lock, it then re-renders the agent surface (skill:commands → .claude/commands/, agent-memory → .claude/agent-memory/ and .agents/) from the checkout root, so a re-pin commit carries the skills and memory the new layers define; a generator that fails fails the run, and --no-agent-surface opts out. |   |   | . | Tool | remote-mount | . | IRI | https://litlfred.github.io/folio-assistant/cat-harness/tools/remote-mount.jsonld | . | part of | https://litlfred.github.io/folio-assistant/cat-harness/cat-harness.jsonld | . | type | https://litlfred.github.io/cat-harness/v0/ns/Tool | . | declared by | cat-harness | . | source | cat-harness/tools/remote-mount/remote-mount.json | . | invoked | shell | . | qa | pass | .

ArchiMate models as knowledge-graph content: how a layer declares the Archi models it holds, what the archimate subgraph gives every model, view, element and relationship (an IRI, a thin page, and every view drawn as SVG from the model’s own diagram, and its metamodel derived and checked), how to version the models, how to wire them into a folio’s staging build and navbar, how to count and lower the crossed lines in a view before committing it, why every view carries a plain-language key, why names are the source’s own terms linked to their SKOS concepts, and why no Java, no Archi CLI and no Archi HTML report is ever part of the pipeline. 4680bd7284d0.title: Replay a committed mount lock with nothing but Node
4680bd7284d0.content: Lay down every remote mount index.lock.json records — each layer fetched at the lock’s full SHA (sparse, blob-filtered), each directory verified against its treeDigest, a mismatch undone and reported — importing only node:*, so it runs on a fresh clone before any layer is present. It never decides what to mount: remote-mount writes the lock (and checks trust); this only replays it. Refuses to write over a path with tracked files or bytes that no longer hash to the lock. Exit 0 mounted/current, 1 missing, 2 could-not-determine. |   |   | . | Tool | mount-from-lock | . | IRI | https://litlfred.github.io/folio-assistant/cat-harness/tools/mount-from-lock.jsonld | . | part of | https://litlfred.github.io/folio-assistant/cat-harness/cat-harness.jsonld | . | type | https://litlfred.github.io/cat-harness/v0/ns/Tool | . | declared by | cat-harness | . | source | cat-harness/tools/mount-from-lock/mount-from-lock.json | . | invoked | shell | . | qa | pass | .

f6e1c1f1a3ed.title: Skills it satisfies
f6e1c1f1a3ed.content: A skill states the capability; this Tool is one way to exercise it. Each skill’s declared input and output contract follows, where it has one. remote-mount . Bring a harness, and every layer it depends on, into a checkout that does not hold it, from another repository at a pinned commit, as declared directories with a lock: a source.remote entry in the downstream’s root index.config.json (legacy: remoteMounts on its declaration) and mountDefaults on the harness. Covers when to mount and when to subscribe instead, why there are no submodules and no .deps/, the transitive closure through needs and gitlinks, overrides by id, the lock, and the three states. Source: cat-harness/skills/kg/kg-core/remote-mount.md. Also satisfied by: build-instance-site, index-config-migrate, instantiate-harness, kg-retrieve-npm, npm, subgraph-index-package. The skill declares no I/O contract (schemas/skills/remote-mount/{input,output}.schema.json). kg-separation . Separate a Knowledge Graph into its own repository — as a CONTENT repository (files to read, no code) and a TOOLS repository (the code that writes and checks it) — once it is too large, or its consumers or cadence differ. The end-to-end method: the signals that trigger it, the preconditions, eleven stages each with the command that gates it, the owner’s decision points, how identifiers, QA and publication move, how the parent consumes the result, rollback, and the post-move sweep that a move between the pair owes before the parent re-pins. graph-detanglement owns stages 1–3; this skill owns the rest. Bootstrap + bootstrap-tools and cat-harness + the tools layer are the worked examples. Source: cat-harness/skills/kg/graph-management/kg-separation.md. Also satisfied by: declaration-resolution, package-exports, rewrite-moved-paths, separation-cutover-check. The skill declares no I/O contract (schemas/skills/kg-separation/{input,output}.schema.json).

ALWAYS exits 0: the sweep runs it as if ! …; then, and a non-zero exit would print the report AND declare it unchecked every time CI is red. | boolean · A boolean switch — projects to a bare flag, with no value word | . | in | warn | Flag |   | Report only, never fail. No .. segments. | . | out | report | Markdown |   | One row per workflow. Five verdicts, not two: green, red, running, superseded (a red whose workflow file changed after the failing run, so the verdict is against code that no longer exists), and possibly-stale (a red that has not re-run in a week). Three exit codes carry them to a caller that reads no rows: 0 nothing is red, 1 something is, 2 COULD NOT LOOK — the API was unreachable, or --out could not be written. A caller must never read 2 as either verdict. --markdown and --warn always exit 0 by design, so a caller wanting the verdict uses neither. | string · Markdown text. 3176a5ca09eb.title: Check declared credential needs against workflow use and expiry, by name
3176a5ca09eb.content: Compare each repository’s declared credential needs (credentials/needs.json, profile and registry) with the secrets.NAME expressions its workflows reference (GitHub Actions’ dollar-and-double-brace form, said in words because this text is rendered on a Jekyll page), with the secret names GitHub lists when a token allows it, and with any recorded expiry. NAMES ONLY — no value is ever read. Findings: used-not-declared, declared-not-used, declared-not-present, present-not-declared (reported, never deleted), naming advisories, and expiry (≤30 days minor, ≤7 major, expired critical). Exits 2 when anything could not be determined, which outranks clean; else 1 on a major or critical finding; else 0. |   |   | . | Tool | secrets-check | . | IRI | https://litlfred.github.io/folio-assistant/cat-harness/tools/secrets-check.jsonld | . | part of | https://litlfred.github.io/folio-assistant/cat-harness/cat-harness.jsonld | . | type | https://litlfred.github.io/cat-harness/v0/ns/Tool | . | declared by | cat-harness | . | source | cat-harness/tools/secrets-check/secrets-check.json | . | invoked | shell | . | qa | pass | .

f47238f52ec0.title: How it is deployed and reached
f47238f52ec0.content: . | Command line. From the repository root: bun run cat pdf:cover. cat pdf:cover runs python3 cat-harness-tools/scripts/pdf-cover.py (declared in cat-harness-tools/package.json). | GitHub Actions. No workflow in this checkout runs its command. | . As an API: its operation in the OpenAPI document and the MCP tool list of its layer. |   |   | . | install | cli: pip install pymupdf | . | runtime | python3, pymupdf | . | network | no | . | when to choose it |   | . | when | A listing needs a cover and the bytes are already held. It renders page 1 by default and calls that the cover, because page 1 is a determined answer and “the cover” is not — the same choice pdf-pages.py makes about sections. | . | limits | It decides nothing beyond the raster. WHICH documents get a cover, where the file lands, and what the catalogue must say about the derivation are the catalogue’s to declare — see the content core’s scripts/gen-covers.ts, which reads them from a layer’s catalogue and refuses to write bytes for a THUMBNAIL that does not declare itself derived. It also cannot tell you whether the page it rendered IS the cover; it can only tell you it is page 1. | . | cost | One PyMuPDF wheel, no network at run time, and a few milliseconds per page. Deterministic — identical input gives identical bytes, which is what lets a caller gate on --check rather than re-deciding. | .

6615de34a6d1.title: Skills it satisfies
6615de34a6d1.content: A skill states the capability; this Tool is one way to exercise it. Each skill’s declared input and output contract follows, where it has one. bean-coordination . Pointer to the bean-based session work-plan system (the beans CLI flat-file issue tracker, data under beans/). Operational usage lives in todo-manager.md / session-intent.md; this file is the canonical copy of the coordinator logic that downstream repositories sync from. Source: cat-harness/work-plan/skills/work-plan/bean-coordination.md. Also satisfied by: bean-claim-check, bean-query, beans-cli, drain-queue, open-work-lookup, sibling-sessions, work-plan-prime, workflow-complete, workflow-start. The skill declares no I/O contract (schemas/skills/bean-coordination/{input,output}.schema.json). todo-manager . Maintain and display work-in-progress task lists using the beans CLI issue tracker. Track implementation progress, open tasks, missing artifacts, and blocked items across a session. Source: cat-harness/work-plan/skills/work-plan/todo-manager.md. Also satisfied by: bean-query, beans-cli, work-plan-prime. The skill declares no I/O contract (schemas/skills/todo-manager/{input,output}.schema.json). pending-show . Show the current session’s pending work — work items list + ledger intent. Read-only. Source: cat-harness/sdlc/skills/sdlc-core/pending-show.md. Also satisfied by: beans-cli, work-plan-prime. The skill declares no I/O contract (schemas/skills/pending-show/{input,output}.schema.json). session-intent . Session-start intent declaration + session-end results recording, against the work plan’s goals (milestone work items) and their open work items. Enforces the durable-handoff discipline so any agent can pick up another’s thread. Source: cat-harness/sdlc/skills/sdlc-core/session-intent.md. Also satisfied by: beans-cli, work-plan-prime. The skill declares no I/O contract (schemas/skills/session-intent/{input,output}.schema.json). continual-progress . Make in-flight work trackable by others in real time — open a PR from the first commit, push small coherent increments continuously (never hoard uncommitted work), keep a live status checklist in the PR body, and post brief intent on the PR + any overlapping sibling PRs. Use on any multi-step or long-running task, especially when siblings/agents or the author may need to follow, cherry-pick, or take over mid-flight. Source: cat-harness/skills/conduct/conduct-core/continual-progress.md. Also satisfied by: gates, beans-cli. The skill declares no I/O contract (schemas/skills/continual-progress/{input,output}.schema.json). idle-backlog . Detail for integration-watcher, split out of it so the parent stays a short entry point. NOT a skill of its own — it is reached through the parent, and section numbers are the parent’s. Source: cat-harness/sdlc/skills/sdlc-core/integration-watcher/idle-backlog.md. Also satisfied by: beans-cli, drain-queue. The skill declares no I/O contract (schemas/skills/idle-backlog/{input,output}.schema.json).

f6edf49500bf.title: Check a bean is free, then claim it on every copy
f6edf49500bf.content: For one bean: fetch every bean copy, read the last three commits on its file, skip it if another agent committed within the window or its last note is a claim, look for an open PR naming it in every listed repository, and only then set it in-progress with a dated claim note as a plain commit on every copy. 394eb35d7593.title: Pin third-party GitHub Actions to full commit SHAs
394eb35d7593.content: Rewrite every third-party uses: owner/repo@ref outside the declared staging-only workflows to @<full commit SHA> # <ref>, so Dependabot keeps the pair current. A tag resolves to its PEELED commit (an annotated tag’s object is never pinned), else a branch head, by git ls-remote with argv. A ref that resolves to nothing, or to more than one commit, is refused and reported, never guessed. This repository’s own reusable workflows are first-party and left alone. Idempotent. |   |   | . | Tool | pin-actions | . | IRI | https://litlfred.github.io/folio-assistant/cat-harness/tools/pin-actions.jsonld | . | part of | https://litlfred.github.io/folio-assistant/cat-harness/cat-harness.jsonld | . | type | https://litlfred.github.io/cat-harness/v0/ns/Tool | . | declared by | cat-harness | . | source | cat-harness/tools/pin-actions/pin-actions.json | . | invoked | shell | . | qa | pass | .

ba1bfc298391.title: Build, check and (on request) publish a layer’s own site, or a branches/ preview
ba1bfc298391.content: From a checkout whose layers arrive by remote mount: mount the pinned closure, install, run the layer’s own gates (--pre), compose the harness chrome for THIS layer, run its source steps, build with Jekyll at the base path read from the git remote (/<repo>, or /<repo>/branches/<branch> for a preview), run the post-build steps (mount-instance-docs, pdf-viewer, set-html-lang, publish-id-lookup, rail-standalone-pages), and check that every relative or base-rooted link in every page resolves to a file under the site, reading each page with an HTML parser. Any failing step stops the run; a link that does not resolve means nothing is published. It never decides to publish: only --publish does, and then a root publish keeps branches/ and _render-log/ on the branch, and a preview replaces only its own branches/<branch>/. |   |   | . | Tool | build-instance-site | . | IRI | https://litlfred.github.io/folio-assistant/cat-harness/tools/build-instance-site.jsonld | . | part of | https://litlfred.github.io/folio-assistant/cat-harness/cat-harness.jsonld | . | type | https://litlfred.github.io/cat-harness/v0/ns/Tool | . | declared by | cat-harness | . | source | cat-harness/tools/build-instance-site/build-instance-site.json | . | invoked | shell | . | qa | pass | .

f49206cf375f.content: A skill states the capability; this Tool is one way to exercise it. Each skill’s declared input and output contract follows, where it has one. corpus-grep . Pre-declaration corpus check. Before declaring any item “open”, “gap”, “TODO”, “open problem”, “pending derivation” — or asserting in chat that something is unresolved in the corpus — run the four-path grep checklist. 986e2ac3016a.title: Apply a vocabulary mapping table
986e2ac3016a.content: Carry one source record into a target vocabulary by a declared folio-vocab-mapping/v1 table: each source field becomes the predicate its row names, in the table’s order, with a DERIVED target (such as dcterms:title rendering skos:prefLabel) copied from its authoritative one so the two cannot drift. A table is shaped like a FHIR ConceptMap: an existing ConceptMap, R4 or R5, is representable as one without loss (fromConceptMap), and a table can be produced as a ConceptMap (toConceptMap), which returns every loss rather than dropping anything silently. First consumer: glossary-export. |   |   | . | Tool | vocab-map | . | IRI | https://litlfred.github.io/folio-assistant/cat-harness/tools/vocab-map.jsonld | . | part of | https://litlfred.github.io/folio-assistant/cat-harness/cat-harness.jsonld | . | type | https://litlfred.github.io/cat-harness/v0/ns/Tool | . | declared by | cat-harness | . | source | cat-harness/tools/vocab-map/vocab-map.json | . | invoked | inProcess | . | qa | pass | .

63973b1c9b1c.title: Lower the tangles in ArchiMate views: re-route lines and swap same-size boxes in a row
63973b1c9b1c.content: Searches for a less tangled drawing of each view: a line may be re-routed straight or orthogonally (an L, or a Z through a free lane between boxes), and two same-size boxes in the same parent and row or column may swap places. A change is kept only if it lowers crossings + lines through boxes + lines drawn on top of each other. Without --apply it reports before and after per view; with it, the model is written back in place, only the moved boxes’ bounds and the re-routed lines’ bendpoints changing. |   |   | . | Tool | archimate-detangle | . | IRI | https://litlfred.github.io/folio-assistant/cat-harness/tools/archimate-detangle.jsonld | . | part of | https://litlfred.github.io/folio-assistant/cat-harness/cat-harness.jsonld | . | type | https://litlfred.github.io/cat-harness/v0/ns/Tool | . | declared by | cat-harness | . | source | cat-harness/tools/archimate-detangle/archimate-detangle.json | . | invoked | shell | . | qa | pass | .

1d21c271193c.title: Skills it satisfies
1d21c271193c.content: A skill states the capability; this Tool is one way to exercise it. Each skill’s declared input and output contract follows, where it has one. archimate-models . ArchiMate models as knowledge-graph content: how a layer declares the Archi models it holds, what the archimate subgraph gives every model, view, element and relationship (an IRI, a thin page, and every view drawn as SVG from the model’s own diagram, and its metamodel derived and checked), how to version the models, how to wire them into a folio’s staging build and navbar, how to count and lower the crossed lines in a view before committing it, why every view carries a plain-language key, why names are the source’s own terms linked to their SKOS concepts, and why no Java, no Archi CLI and no Archi HTML report is ever part of the pipeline. Read before adding, authoring, publishing or rendering an .archimate file, before citing an ArchiMate element from prose, and before reaching for Archi’s own tooling in CI. Source: cat-harness/skills/ui/ui-core/archimate-models.md. Also satisfied by: archimate-actors, archimate-blocks, archimate-check, archimate-crossings, archimate-metamodel, archimate-pages. 0c6defbb2e9b.content: A skill states the capability; this Tool is one way to exercise it. Each skill’s declared input and output contract follows, where it has one. merge-conflict-patterns . Merge the base branch in and resolve, without a person, only the conflicts a DECLARED pattern covers — generated files, generated README regions, QA sidecars — then prove the result with the gate set. Refuses the whole merge when any conflict is authored or undeclared. Use for “merge main”, “resolve the conflicts”, “the PR is conflicted again”, “auto-resolve”, and when adding a pattern for a new kind of churn. Also governs what a merge steward does with a merge-train member it had to refuse: one deduplicated work item under the PR’s own epic, a hand-back to the owning session with a fail condition, one dispatched agent when nobody owns it, one PR comment, and the close. 3aebcf027e52.title: Skills it satisfies
3aebcf027e52.content: A skill states the capability; this Tool is one way to exercise it. Each skill’s declared input and output contract follows, where it has one. prepare-merge-auto . Full prepare-merge → resolve → merge pipeline. Coordinates with sibling PRs, resolves review comments, asks structured questions only when blocked, then hands the merge to the merge-to-main sub-process, which merges only on the owner’s authorisation. Source: cat-harness/sdlc/skills/sdlc-core/prepare-merge-auto.md. Also satisfied by: github-pr-checks, github-pr-comment, github-pr-list, github-pr-request-review, gitlab-mr-comment, gitlab-mr-list, gitlab-mr-request-review, gitlab-mr-view. The skill declares no I/O contract (schemas/skills/prepare-merge-auto/{input,output}.schema.json). pickup . Pick up / continue work on one or more existing open PRs efficiently. Resolves each PR’s REAL branch + title + checklist + reviews + CI in one batched pass, classifies CI as billing-vs-real, then dispatches one worktree sub-agent per PR with a filled-in brief, and applies the safe class of review-nit fixes (eval→ast.literal_eval, dead-code/unused-var removal, etc.). Use when the user says “pick up PR N”, “continue 1543/1576/1571”, “work these PRs”, “address the review on PR N”, or “take over PR N”. Source: cat-harness/sdlc/skills/sdlc-core/pickup.md. Also satisfied by: github-pr-list, github-pr-request-review, gitlab-mr-list, gitlab-mr-request-review, gitlab-mr-view. The skill declares no I/O contract (schemas/skills/pickup/{input,output}.schema.json). watch . Background-watch a branch (default origin/main) or a GitHub PR for new activity while you work, and on every event report whether to integrate / whether it conflicts with the current branch / whether it lets you simplify exposition / proofs / computations . Source: cat-harness/sdlc/skills/sdlc-core/watch.md. Also satisfied by: github-pr-checks, gitlab-mr-view. The skill declares no I/O contract (schemas/skills/watch/{input,output}.schema.json). coordinate . Coordinate work across multiple in-flight Claude PRs working toward a shared goal. Post intent + asks on related PRs, identify cherry-pickable work, respond to code-review comments on your own PR, periodically triage sibling PR activity (new comments, CI status, new commits), watch main + newly created branches/PRs, escalate inconsistent findings to the author, and keep a coordination ledger up to date. 1ecba589de60.title: Is this repository’s cutover from the monorepo complete? Measured, condition by condition
1ecba589de60.content: Run in a separated repository. Six conditions, each decided by an existing gate: mounts (every declared layer on disk at its pin — remote-mount --check), declarations (every path a declaration names resolves — declaration-resolution), monorepo-paths (no wiring still names the monorepo: livesAt on it, a submodule of it, a reusable workflow called from it, a path into its old checkout — the one condition implemented here), import-direction and reference-direction (no layer reaches a layer above it), and site (the site builds from the mounts alone, every link resolving — build-instance-site --no-mount, only with --site). Findings inside a MOUNTED layer are listed and not counted: a defect in a layer pinned from upstream is fixed upstream and re-pinned. Exit 0 complete, 1 a condition failed, 2 a condition could not be determined or was not run — without --site the answer is never 0. |   |   | . | Tool | separation-cutover-check | . | IRI | https://litlfred.github.io/folio-assistant/cat-harness/tools/separation-cutover-check.jsonld | . | part of | https://litlfred.github.io/folio-assistant/cat-harness/cat-harness.jsonld | . | type | https://litlfred.github.io/cat-harness/v0/ns/Tool | . | declared by | cat-harness | . | source | cat-harness/tools/separation-cutover-check/separation-cutover-check.json | . | invoked | shell | . | qa | pass | .

48c32c6efc4c.content: A skill states the capability; this Tool is one way to exercise it. Each skill’s declared input and output contract follows, where it has one. kg-separation . Separate a Knowledge Graph into its own repository — as a CONTENT repository (files to read, no code) and a TOOLS repository (the code that writes and checks it) — once it is too large, or its consumers or cadence differ. The end-to-end method: the signals that trigger it, the preconditions, eleven stages each with the command that gates it, the owner’s decision points, how identifiers, QA and publication move, how the parent consumes the result, rollback, and the post-move sweep that a move between the pair owes before the parent re-pins. graph-detanglement owns stages 1–3; this skill owns the rest. Bootstrap + bootstrap-tools and cat-harness + the tools layer are the worked examples. Source: cat-harness/skills/kg/graph-management/kg-separation.md. a23de4ef6237.title: Every reference a journey or a workshop names resolves
a23de4ef6237.content: Read every user-scenario and workshop node in the checkout through the layers’ declared directories, with the journeys viewer’s own resolver, and resolve what each names: actors (personas, a step’s lead, experiences[].actor, handoff.from/to, illustrationStyle.cast[].actor), user stories, realisedBy BPMN files (instance-relative) and the element ids in them, uses blocks in a directory declaring building-blocks, req: requirements, FHIR examples and a step’s dak assets (data sets, decision tables, indicators) in a fhir-artifact-index (could not determine while the index is built at publish), illustration.src files, follows/partOf/parts/includes journeys (parts and includes forming no cycle; an includes held against the call activity its step’s realisedBy names, could not determine when the call names no process), the trustLadder code list and each record.state code of it, and ArchiMate views; and each workshop’s scenarios, steps[] {scenario, step} and <scenario>#<step> refs; each device screen’s owner and personCard actors, its steps[] {scenario, step}, and the FHIR examples its qr and recordList blocks name; and every persona’s avatar image path. Every journey is a DAK user scenario (the kind specialises it): its DAK personas, the roles its persona actors play, must be non-empty and each a declared role; a persona may be an actor or (0.4.0) a role. What is derived is not also written: a listed part’s follows or partOf, personas equal to the parts’, a lead equal to the lanes’ first actor, are each a redundant finding, and a 0.4.0 step with no experiences whose lanes no persona plays is a finding. A node that does not parse is a finding. One line per finding, naming the layer, file and step. Exit 0 every reference resolves (or no layer holds a journey or a workshop, which is said); 1 one does not; 2 the declarations could not be read. |   |   | . | Tool | journey-refs | . | IRI | https://litlfred.github.io/folio-assistant/cat-harness/tools/journey-refs.jsonld | . | part of | https://litlfred.github.io/folio-assistant/cat-harness/cat-harness.jsonld | . | type | https://litlfred.github.io/cat-harness/v0/ns/Tool | . | declared by | cat-harness | . | source | cat-harness/tools/journey-refs/journey-refs.json | . | invoked | shell | . | qa | pass | .

2df5f878a0d9.title: Tools — cat-harness
2df5f878a0d9.content: The Tool nodes cat-harness declares in its tools graph — one instance’s slice of every instance’s tools. As an API: OpenAPI document · MCP tool list · API reference. A skill states a capability generically: what an actor needs to know to perform a task. A Tool is one concrete way to exercise it, with an installation, an invocation and typed inputs and outputs. One skill may be satisfied by several tools, and one tool may satisfy several skills. They are separate graphs and this is the tools one. The relation between them is satisfies, and it runs from a tool to a skill — this tool is one way to do that, never this skill is a tool. 194Tool nodes 73skills satisfied 166invoked as a shell command 29reachable over MCP

1111e00507ca.title: Skills it satisfies
1111e00507ca.content: A skill states the capability; this Tool is one way to exercise it. Each skill’s declared input and output contract follows, where it has one. ig-build-pipeline . The bare FHIR IG pipeline — FSH to SUSHI to the IG Publisher to a pages branch, with no pre-processing and no post-processing. What this layer runs, what it emits, and the list of things it deliberately refuses to know about. Owns the AST cache lifecycle: an IG site is built from the AST on its cache branch, the publish refuses a stale one, and the reusable ig-ast-refresh.yml is the one writer. Owns what an IG reader may read: contentTypes.ig.include in the repository’s index.config.json, and the legacy warning for a repository that declares none. Read before adding anything to fhir-harness, before onboarding, converting or changing the workflows of an IG repository, and before publishing an IG site. Source: fhir-harness/skills/fhir-ig-base/ig-build-pipeline.md. 6346252b7eb8.title: Skills it satisfies
6346252b7eb8.content: A skill states the capability; this Tool is one way to exercise it. Each skill’s declared input and output contract follows, where it has one. ig-build-pipeline . The bare FHIR IG pipeline — FSH to SUSHI to the IG Publisher to a pages branch, with no pre-processing and no post-processing. What this layer runs, what it emits, and the list of things it deliberately refuses to know about. Owns the AST cache lifecycle: an IG site is built from the AST on its cache branch, the publish refuses a stale one, and the reusable ig-ast-refresh.yml is the one writer. Owns what an IG reader may read: contentTypes.ig.include in the repository’s index.config.json, and the legacy warning for a repository that declares none. Read before adding anything to fhir-harness, before onboarding, converting or changing the workflows of an IG repository, and before publishing an IG site. Source: fhir-harness/skills/fhir-ig-base/ig-build-pipeline.md. f7a57ab9e2fc.content: Dispatch an IG repository’s ig-ast-refresh.yml, which calls fhir-harness’s reusable .github/workflows/ig-ast-refresh.yml: mount the layers the IG’s index.lock.json pins, restore and judge the cache for ref, and when it is not valid (or force) run the caller’s optional pre-export overlay command and build the IG with the pinned Publisher AST exporter (the AST is recorded against the clean commit’s inputs, the overlay’s changes put back), check the new AST is valid for its commit, and seed cat/fhir-harness/fhir-ast/<package id> with ig-cache seed --push — only from a commit on the default branch with the tip’s inputs. dcf99ee20156.title: Write one JSON-LD node per IG artefact, and check a built site’s nodes
dcf99ee20156.content: write turns an artefact index into artifact/<Type>-<id>.jsonld under a docs root, with no .json twin: one folio-ig-artifact-jsonld/v1 node per artefact, in borrowed vocabularies only (the FHIR RDF class, dcterms, schema.org, PROV), naming the artefact’s canonical URL, its representations and, for a compiled copy, what built it. With --root-resources (the IG site’s default) the first representation is the reduced <Type>-<id>.json the site serves at its root (local), the second the full copy in the AST cache by raw URL (mirror), and each index entry names the root file (schema:contentUrl). check is the kind’s QA: over a BUILT site, every artefact has its node and no node is an orphan, each node is its own file’s, no .json twin is served beside it, and every local resource it names is on the site. It also writes and checks the index node, artifact/index.jsonld (folio-ig-artifact-index-jsonld/v1): every artefact once, each entry naming its node. 31c3853f76ea.title: Build an IG repository’s own site from its cached AST, with no instance declaration
31c3853f76ea.content: The three checkout scripts the platform’s site build runs for a repository that holds an IG and only mounts layers (index.config.json): ig-site:ast restores the AST from the IG’s cache branch (ig-cache.sh restore) and judges it, refusing a stale, cannot-tell or absent one (a stale one is accepted for a preview by default, refused with SITE_ACCEPT_STALE_AST=0, and never accepted for the root); ig-site:compose derives the artefact index from the AST (binding any IG API sidecars a layer above left in $SITE_WORK/ig-api/), writes the thin artefact pages, stages the IG’s input/ and sushi-config.yaml (menu read at build time, palette from the webpage theme of the top layer the repository mounts, edit links from its origin) and composes it at the ROOT of the host site source; ig-site:publisher-pages serves each of the AST’s resources once, as <Type>-<id>.json at the root (no ast-data/ mirror) — reduced (minified, no narrative, no ELM data, the ELM attachment pointing at the full copy) when the pages read the full resources by raw URL from the AST cache commit, and off with SITE_ROOT_RESOURCES=0 — the artefact index (or fhir-artifact-index/index.ref.json, pointing at the cache’s copy) and the sidecars (or none, read from the cache), refuses a page wearing the IG Publisher’s chrome, repairs repeated element ids and stamps folio-build.json. Never runs the Publisher and never reads its output. Compose lists the pages it puts in the site in FOLIO_SITE_UPSTREAM_PAGES, so the site build reports the IG’s own dead links rather than refusing the publish over them. |   |   | . | Tool | ig-repo-site | . | IRI | https://litlfred.github.io/folio-assistant/fhir-harness/tools/ig-repo-site.jsonld | . | part of | https://litlfred.github.io/folio-assistant/fhir-harness/fhir-harness.jsonld | . | type | https://litlfred.github.io/cat-harness/v0/ns/Tool | . | declared by | fhir-harness | . | source | fhir-harness/tools/ig-repo-site/ig-repo-site.ts | . | invoked | shell | . | qa | qa-reports | .

a2a2c44893a5.title: Skills it satisfies
a2a2c44893a5.content: A skill states the capability; this Tool is one way to exercise it. Each skill’s declared input and output contract follows, where it has one. ig-build-pipeline . The bare FHIR IG pipeline — FSH to SUSHI to the IG Publisher to a pages branch, with no pre-processing and no post-processing. What this layer runs, what it emits, and the list of things it deliberately refuses to know about. Owns the AST cache lifecycle: an IG site is built from the AST on its cache branch, the publish refuses a stale one, and the reusable ig-ast-refresh.yml is the one writer. Owns what an IG reader may read: contentTypes.ig.include in the repository’s index.config.json, and the legacy warning for a repository that declares none. Read before adding anything to fhir-harness, before onboarding, converting or changing the workflows of an IG repository, and before publishing an IG site. 96c2fb88961c.title: Cut an IG release as a GitHub draft that carries its packages and AST, and report a version left untagged or unreleased
96c2fb88961c.content: Gather a release’s files from a full Publisher build (package.tgz and its R4/R4B variants, and ast-data.zip, the IG’s AST with the Libraries’ ELM), say from sushi-config.yaml whether it is a pre-release, and make or refresh the GitHub DRAFT release for the tag with the files uploaded. The owner publishes the draft; a published release is never changed. check is the catch-up the AST refresh of the default branch runs (advisory): it reports a current version with no v<version> tag, naming the commit that set it for the owner to tag, and a tag with no release, for the owner to run ig-release.yml by hand. It never tags and never releases: the tag is the owner’s governance step (ig-release.bpmn). |   |   | . | Tool | ig-release | . | IRI | https://litlfred.github.io/folio-assistant/fhir-harness/tools/ig-release.jsonld | . | part of | https://litlfred.github.io/folio-assistant/fhir-harness/fhir-harness.jsonld | . | type | https://litlfred.github.io/cat-harness/v0/ns/Tool | . | declared by | fhir-harness | . | source | fhir-harness/tools/ig-release/ig-release.ts | . | invoked | shell | . | qa | qa-reports | .

4478a88d1c6a.title: Skills it satisfies
4478a88d1c6a.content: A skill states the capability; this Tool is one way to exercise it. Each skill’s declared input and output contract follows, where it has one. ig-build-pipeline . The bare FHIR IG pipeline — FSH to SUSHI to the IG Publisher to a pages branch, with no pre-processing and no post-processing. What this layer runs, what it emits, and the list of things it deliberately refuses to know about. Owns the AST cache lifecycle: an IG site is built from the AST on its cache branch, the publish refuses a stale one, and the reusable ig-ast-refresh.yml is the one writer. Owns what an IG reader may read: contentTypes.ig.include in the repository’s index.config.json, and the legacy warning for a repository that declares none. Read before adding anything to fhir-harness, before onboarding, converting or changing the workflows of an IG repository, and before publishing an IG site. Source: fhir-harness/skills/fhir-ig-base/ig-build-pipeline.md. Also satisfied by: build-ig-site, ig-artifact-jsonld, ig-ast-refresh, ig-index-build, ig-page-render-qa, ig-repo-site, ig-site-data, ingest-ig-menu, jsonld-vocabularies, logical-model-schemas, stage-ig-sites, strip-library-binaries, strip-library-content, terminology-index, valueset-schemas. 61625fc3b917.title: Skills it satisfies
61625fc3b917.content: A skill states the capability; this Tool is one way to exercise it. Each skill’s declared input and output contract follows, where it has one. ig-build-pipeline . The bare FHIR IG pipeline — FSH to SUSHI to the IG Publisher to a pages branch, with no pre-processing and no post-processing. What this layer runs, what it emits, and the list of things it deliberately refuses to know about. Owns the AST cache lifecycle: an IG site is built from the AST on its cache branch, the publish refuses a stale one, and the reusable ig-ast-refresh.yml is the one writer. Owns what an IG reader may read: contentTypes.ig.include in the repository’s index.config.json, and the legacy warning for a repository that declares none. Read before adding anything to fhir-harness, before onboarding, converting or changing the workflows of an IG repository, and before publishing an IG site. Source: fhir-harness/skills/fhir-ig-base/ig-build-pipeline.md. 54396fd36a6e.title: Skills it satisfies
54396fd36a6e.content: A skill states the capability; this Tool is one way to exercise it. Each skill’s declared input and output contract follows, where it has one. ig-build-pipeline . The bare FHIR IG pipeline — FSH to SUSHI to the IG Publisher to a pages branch, with no pre-processing and no post-processing. What this layer runs, what it emits, and the list of things it deliberately refuses to know about. Owns the AST cache lifecycle: an IG site is built from the AST on its cache branch, the publish refuses a stale one, and the reusable ig-ast-refresh.yml is the one writer. Owns what an IG reader may read: contentTypes.ig.include in the repository’s index.config.json, and the legacy warning for a repository that declares none. Read before adding anything to fhir-harness, before onboarding, converting or changing the workflows of an IG repository, and before publishing an IG site. Source: fhir-harness/skills/fhir-ig-base/ig-build-pipeline.md. b2308a44890f.title: Skills it satisfies
b2308a44890f.content: A skill states the capability; this Tool is one way to exercise it. Each skill’s declared input and output contract follows, where it has one. ig-build-pipeline . The bare FHIR IG pipeline — FSH to SUSHI to the IG Publisher to a pages branch, with no pre-processing and no post-processing. What this layer runs, what it emits, and the list of things it deliberately refuses to know about. Owns the AST cache lifecycle: an IG site is built from the AST on its cache branch, the publish refuses a stale one, and the reusable ig-ast-refresh.yml is the one writer. Owns what an IG reader may read: contentTypes.ig.include in the repository’s index.config.json, and the legacy warning for a repository that declares none. Read before adding anything to fhir-harness, before onboarding, converting or changing the workflows of an IG repository, and before publishing an IG site. a34ec217a0d7.title: Skills it satisfies
a34ec217a0d7.content: A skill states the capability; this Tool is one way to exercise it. Each skill’s declared input and output contract follows, where it has one. ig-build-pipeline . The bare FHIR IG pipeline — FSH to SUSHI to the IG Publisher to a pages branch, with no pre-processing and no post-processing. What this layer runs, what it emits, and the list of things it deliberately refuses to know about. Owns the AST cache lifecycle: an IG site is built from the AST on its cache branch, the publish refuses a stale one, and the reusable ig-ast-refresh.yml is the one writer. Owns what an IG reader may read: contentTypes.ig.include in the repository’s index.config.json, and the legacy warning for a repository that declares none. Read before adding anything to fhir-harness, before onboarding, converting or changing the workflows of an IG repository, and before publishing an IG site. Source: fhir-harness/skills/fhir-ig-base/ig-build-pipeline.md. Also satisfied by: build-ig-site, ig-artifact-jsonld, ig-ast-refresh, ig-index-build, ig-page-render-qa, ig-pages, ig-repo-site, ig-site-data, ingest-ig-menu, jsonld-vocabularies, logical-model-schemas, stage-ig-sites, strip-library-binaries, strip-library-content, valueset-schemas. 92bfd93596fe.title: Tools — fhir-harness
92bfd93596fe.content: The Tool nodes fhir-harness declares in its tools graph — one instance’s slice of every instance’s tools. As an API: OpenAPI document · MCP tool list · API reference. A skill states a capability generically: what an actor needs to know to perform a task. A Tool is one concrete way to exercise it, with an installation, an invocation and typed inputs and outputs. One skill may be satisfied by several tools, and one tool may satisfy several skills. They are separate graphs and this is the tools one. The relation between them is satisfies, and it runs from a tool to a skill — this tool is one way to do that, never this skill is a tool. 37Tool nodes 9skills satisfied 37invoked as a shell command 0reachable over MCP

4995f727814c.title: Skills it satisfies
4995f727814c.content: A skill states the capability; this Tool is one way to exercise it. Each skill’s declared input and output contract follows, where it has one. publish-extracted-statements . The standard step of adding source documents to a folio’s working artifact: every statement extracted from a library source is published readably in the artifact’s own pages AND in the shared extraction viewer, each with a link to its library entry and to the section it came from, and CI fails when the generated pages are stale. Generic across content types; each type’s adapter says only how its pages look. Executable form: processes/library/publish-extracted-statements.bpmn. Source: folio-assistant-core/skills/library/ingestion/publish-extracted-statements.md. Also satisfied by: l1-statement-lists. The skill declares no I/O contract (schemas/skills/publish-extracted-statements/{input,output}.schema.json).

895df29e6cd8.title: Validate draft MeSH headings against NLM’s authority
895df29e6cd8.content: Stage three of skill-pipeline-subject-indexing for MeSH: look up every candidate heading of a draft (a preferred heading, an entry term, or a descriptor id, with an optional qualifier) in NLM’s MeSH authority at id.nlm.nih.gov, current year. Each candidate comes back resolved (in the preferred form), qualifier-not-allowed (descriptor kept, qualifier dropped), ambiguous (options listed for a person) or not-found (dropped). 21ad8fcfc106.title: Check a review log and its repository’s issues for changes
21ad8fcfc106.content: The mechanical check a review-log watcher runs on every poll. Given a drafting sheet’s Contributor Feedback values and the folio repository, it reads the repository’s open and closed issues (leaving out pull requests, issues labelled no-sheet and, with --author, issues someone else opened) and compares a digest of them and of the cells people set (Title, Selected Sections, Contributor Feedback, Disposition, Ready for agent, Ready for merge, Dispositions confirmed; on a public-comment log also Committee Feedback, TWG (CS), TWG (human) and Change Set (human)) with the last check’s. Unchanged: it prints {"status":"unchanged"} and exits 0. Changed: it exits 10 and lists what changed (issue opened, updated or closed; a cell’s old and new text), the Contributor Feedback rows to append, one per issue that no row’s Issue cell links yet (Title the issue’s title, the first Contributor Feedback column @login (#N): first paragraph, Issue the issue’s URL; a closed issue’s row marked closed), and closedRows, the rows linking a closed issue, which the watcher hides with their text struck through. A read with no Issue column (a public-comment log’s Review Change Sets) tracks only issues labelled change-set unless --label says otherwise, and appends no rows: each open issue is reported as an issue-unlinked change instead. It writes no sheet and no issue: the watcher appends the rows and does the agent pass. With --accept it stores the new state for the next poll to compare against. |   |   | . | Tool | review-log-watch | . | IRI | https://litlfred.github.io/folio-assistant/folio-assistant-core/tools/review-log-watch.jsonld | . | part of | https://litlfred.github.io/folio-assistant/folio-assistant-core/folio-assistant-core.jsonld | . | type | https://litlfred.github.io/cat-harness/v0/ns/Tool | . | declared by | folio-assistant-core | . | source | folio-assistant-core/tools/review-log-watch/review-log-watch.ts | . | invoked | shell | . | qa | qa-reports | .

d26a7f8c8e8d.title: Spreadsheet tabular metadata
d26a7f8c8e8d.content: Read a workbook into a folio-tabular-csvw/v1 record, one CSVW table per rectangular block of cells. Blocks are split on empty rows, then on empty columns, so several tables on one sheet are found, each anchored at its real top-left cell (fac:anchor: sheet, A1 cell, row, column). Dates are read through the number formats in styles.xml, not misread as integer serials. A malformed part is refused rather than half-read. Reads the ZIP with node:zlib and SpreadsheetML with fast-xml-parser. 6c8adb10dc0c.title: Move a review comment’s status
6c8adb10dc0c.content: A review-process task moves one review-comment/1.0.0 todo’s status (address, send back, resolve, adjudicate, withdraw) through transition(), which refuses any move the named BPMN task may not make. The comment is written to the folio’s todos graph (its declared todo-feedback directory) and, with --commit, committed to the edit-set’s FEATURE branch. Refused on the base branch and on a detached HEAD. |   |   | . | Tool | folio-review-comment-move | . | IRI | https://litlfred.github.io/folio-assistant/folio-assistant-core/tools/folio-review-comment-move.jsonld | . | part of | https://litlfred.github.io/folio-assistant/folio-assistant-core/folio-assistant-core.jsonld | . | type | https://litlfred.github.io/cat-harness/v0/ns/Tool | . | declared by | folio-assistant-core | . | source | folio-assistant-core/tools/folio-review-comment-move/folio-review-comment-move.ts | . | invoked | shell | . | qa | qa-reports | .

79662773814e.title: Skills it satisfies
79662773814e.content: A skill states the capability; this Tool is one way to exercise it. Each skill’s declared input and output contract follows, where it has one. review-comments . Reviewer comments on a folio’s edit-set, from a tagged pull-request comment to a structured todo on the review page. Covers the tag a reviewer types, how the comments are ingested into review-comment/1.0.0 todos, where the published review-comments.json comes from and when it refreshes, how a comment follows a renamed block and survives a removed one, who may change a comment’s status, and how to change this process. Use when a reviewer asks how to comment on a block, when the review page shows no comments or a wrong one, when editing the ingestion, or when a folio’s staging workflow is set up. Source: folio-assistant-core/skills/content/content-lifecycle-ext/review-comments.md. Also satisfied by: folio-review-comments, folio-review-coverage. 634c3eb309be.title: Verify Data Sharing Agreement hash, citation, and vocabulary terms
634c3eb309be.content: Verify a Data Sharing Agreement (DSA) directory or single version: checks that every JSON-LD term in agreement.jsonld and dcat.jsonld is defined in the SHA-256-pinned official W3C ODRL 2.2, W3C DCAT 3 (with SPDX 2.2.2 and ADMS), or DCMI Metadata Terms contexts; checks that the ODRL 2.2 Agreement’s uid is the version’s fixed-version URL and its dcterms:source cites the DCAT 3 dcat:Distribution whose spdx:checksum is checked; verifies that the SHA-256 digest of agreement.md matches spdx:checksumValue; and checks dcat:previousVersion and hash distinctness across versions. |   |   | . | Tool | check-dsa-hash | . | IRI | https://litlfred.github.io/folio-assistant/folio-assistant-core/tools/check-dsa-hash.jsonld | . | part of | https://litlfred.github.io/folio-assistant/folio-assistant-core/folio-assistant-core.jsonld | . | type | https://litlfred.github.io/cat-harness/v0/ns/Tool | . | declared by | folio-assistant-core | . | source | folio-assistant-core/tools/check-dsa-hash/check-dsa-hash.ts | . | invoked | shell | . | qa | qa-reports | .

df442bf0bb45.title: Skills it satisfies
df442bf0bb45.content: A skill states the capability; this Tool is one way to exercise it. Each skill’s declared input and output contract follows, where it has one. dsa-checksum . Compute and record the SHA-256 cryptographic digest of a signed Data Sharing Agreement’s legal text as a W3C DCAT 3 spdx:checksum (spdx:Checksum with spdx:checksumAlgorithm_sha256 and 64-character lowercase hex spdx:checksumValue), verified by check:dsa-hash (DSA building block B3, process steps P2.2 Task_Hash and P2.2a Task_HashSummary). Source: folio-assistant-core/dsa/skills/dsa/dsa-checksum.md. The skill declares no I/O contract (schemas/skills/dsa-checksum/{input,output}.schema.json). dsa-odrl-source . Bind a computable Data Sharing Agreement’s W3C ODRL 2.2 Agreement to its signed legal text distribution using DCMI Metadata Terms dcterms:source, naming the exact dcat:Distribution whose spdx:checksum is checked (DSA building block B3, process step P2.3 Task_OdrlCitesText). Source: folio-assistant-core/dsa/skills/dsa/dsa-odrl-source.md. The skill declares no I/O contract (schemas/skills/dsa-odrl-source/{input,output}.schema.json). dsa-dcat-record . Write the W3C DCAT 3 dcat:Resource and dcat:Distribution catalogue record for a Data Sharing Agreement (dcat:downloadURL, spdx:checksum, odrl:hasPolicy) and link versions with dcat:version and dcat:previousVersion (DSA building block B3, process step P2.4–5 Task_Catalogue). Source: folio-assistant-core/dsa/skills/dsa/dsa-dcat-record.md. The skill declares no I/O contract (schemas/skills/dsa-dcat-record/{input,output}.schema.json). dsa-catalogue-status . Set the life-cycle status (adms:status, W3C DCAT 3 §6.4.30) on a Data Sharing Agreement’s DCAT 3 catalogue record when the agreement is amended, renewed, terminated, or expires, while keeping all published versions readable at their immutable URLs (DSA building block B3, process step P14.5 Task_SetStatus). Source: folio-assistant-core/dsa/skills/dsa/dsa-catalogue-status.md. The skill declares no I/O contract (schemas/skills/dsa-catalogue-status/{input,output}.schema.json).

c76119f22e28.title: Skills it satisfies
c76119f22e28.content: A skill states the capability; this Tool is one way to exercise it. Each skill’s declared input and output contract follows, where it has one. review-comments . Reviewer comments on a folio’s edit-set, from a tagged pull-request comment to a structured todo on the review page. Covers the tag a reviewer types, how the comments are ingested into review-comment/1.0.0 todos, where the published review-comments.json comes from and when it refreshes, how a comment follows a renamed block and survives a removed one, who may change a comment’s status, and how to change this process. Use when a reviewer asks how to comment on a block, when the review page shows no comments or a wrong one, when editing the ingestion, or when a folio’s staging workflow is set up. Source: folio-assistant-core/skills/content/content-lifecycle-ext/review-comments.md. Also satisfied by: folio-review-comment-move, folio-review-coverage. The skill declares no I/O contract (schemas/skills/review-comments/{input,output}.schema.json).

30456d2c6d95.title: Build the review sheet’s Apps Script and a document’s Config tab
30456d2c6d95.content: Builds Code.gs (--script), the one Google Apps Script every review sheet runs (from review-sheet.gs), and one document’s Config tab rows (--config), filled from the folio’s review/public-comment/sheet-sync.json, its review anchors and the draft’s pdf-line-map.json. The script keeps a public-comment review sheet’s links and joins current: each comment No. links to its comment page; Sections, Page and Line no(s) link to the page of the frozen review draft; Review Change Sets joins its comments, suggested revisions, feedback and dispositions, each No. n linking to its row; and on both tabs Agentic status lists each pull request of the change-set, linked, with its status and what it changed, from the Agent tab. It reads the document’s URLs, tab and column names and data from the sheet’s Config tab (visible, locked to the owner), which the agent writes from these rows. A person pastes the script (one file) into the sheet once (Extensions > Apps Script) and runs installTriggers; from then on the sheet rebuilds itself within about a minute of an edit, with no agent. With "mode": "drafting" in the config it builds the drafting sheet instead: one Contributor Feedback tab where each row is a change set (ids assigned by the script), Sections picked from the document’s table of contents and linked to it, and Issue and Agentic status from the Agent tab. |   |   | . | Tool | review-sheet-sync | . | IRI | https://litlfred.github.io/folio-assistant/folio-assistant-core/tools/review-sheet-sync.jsonld | . | part of | https://litlfred.github.io/folio-assistant/folio-assistant-core/folio-assistant-core.jsonld | . | type | https://litlfred.github.io/cat-harness/v0/ns/Tool | . | declared by | folio-assistant-core | . | source | folio-assistant-core/tools/review-sheet-sync/review-sheet-sync.ts | . | invoked | shell | . | qa | qa-reports | .

2db167369097.title: CSV tabular metadata

a9c11343eeab.title: Dublin Core renderings
a9c11343eeab.content: Render every folio-dublin-core/v1 record a catalogue item names as Dublin Core XML (qualified DC, per DCMI’s XML guidelines) and as JSON-LD bound to DCMI Metadata Terms. Both are written into the instance’s published root (<instanceRoot>/dublin-core/<stem>.dc.xml and .dc.jsonld), so the site mount publishes them beside the item pages. Deterministic. --check fails on a missing, stale or orphaned rendering. e9f344459d8f.title: Skills it satisfies
e9f344459d8f.content: A skill states the capability; this Tool is one way to exercise it. Each skill’s declared input and output contract follows, where it has one. dublin-core-renderings . Render a catalogue’s Dublin Core records in the two standard forms an outside reader can use: Dublin Core XML, which a harvester reads, and JSON-LD bound to DCMI Metadata Terms. Each rendering is published beside the item’s page. Covers which records get one, which XML form is used and why, how every field maps from the record’s own data (never composed), what cannot be expressed and how that is reported, and the gate. Read this before changing the mapping, adding a catalogue layer, or linking a rendering from a page. Source: folio-assistant-core/skills/library/catalogue/dublin-core-renderings.md. The skill declares no I/O contract (schemas/skills/dublin-core-renderings/{input,output}.schema.json).

b96a54378f5b.title: Tools — folio-assistant-core
b96a54378f5b.content: The Tool nodes folio-assistant-core declares in its tools graph — one instance’s slice of every instance’s tools. As an API: OpenAPI document · MCP tool list · API reference. A skill states a capability generically: what an actor needs to know to perform a task. A Tool is one concrete way to exercise it, with an installation, an invocation and typed inputs and outputs. One skill may be satisfied by several tools, and one tool may satisfy several skills. They are separate graphs and this is the tools one. The relation between them is satisfies, and it runs from a tool to a skill — this tool is one way to do that, never this skill is a tool. 30Tool nodes 25skills satisfied 30invoked as a shell command 0reachable over MCP

c0e8c672f5cd.title: Skills it satisfies
c0e8c672f5cd.content: A skill states the capability; this Tool is one way to exercise it. Each skill’s declared input and output contract follows, where it has one. process-state . Track where you are inside a running process — which task, in which swimlane, under which role — and recover deliberately when you find yourself outside it. Read before completing a workflow step, and whenever something unexpected interrupts one. Covers what to do about notes and stickies you re-anchored while off-process, which leave no trace in the artefact. Source: cat-harness/skills/process/workflow/process-state.md. Also satisfied by: workflow-complete, workflow-gate, workflow-list, workflow-next, workflow-start. The skill declares no I/O contract (schemas/skills/process-state/{input,output}.schema.json).

5539357e541d.title: Tools — cat-harness-tools
5539357e541d.content: The Tool nodes cat-harness-tools declares in its tools graph — one instance’s slice of every instance’s tools. As an API: OpenAPI document · MCP tool list · API reference. A skill states a capability generically: what an actor needs to know to perform a task. A Tool is one concrete way to exercise it, with an installation, an invocation and typed inputs and outputs. One skill may be satisfied by several tools, and one tool may satisfy several skills. They are separate graphs and this is the tools one. The relation between them is satisfies, and it runs from a tool to a skill — this tool is one way to do that, never this skill is a tool. 1Tool nodes 1skills satisfied 0invoked as a shell command 1reachable over MCP

63daeb8814bb.title: Publish a Lean render under a folio site, with the harness rail
63daeb8814bb.content: Stage a doc-gen4 render under a folio’s built site (<site>/<route>/, default lean/) and give every page the harness navbar and rail by running cat-harness/scripts/rail-standalone-pages.ts --foreign-site over the site — the same rail stage-folio-local.ts applies to the folio’s own pages. 962a71747c4d.title: Publish the dynamic Lean viewer: doc-gen4 declaration data as knowledge-graph shards
962a71747c4d.content: Ingest doc-gen4’s per-module declaration data (.lake/build/doc-data/declaration-data-<Module>.bmp) into JSON-LD shards — one per module, with declaration nodes, imports edges and formalizes edges to the content blocks whose lean.ref names each declaration — and publish them under the folio’s site with a single viewer page that loads modules, signature chunks and the search list on demand. Signatures are chunked 500 declarations per file so a 12,804-declaration module stays usable. With --base it writes a STAGING overlay: only modules whose content hash differs from the published base, plus overlay.json; the viewer loads the rest from the base. Rails the viewer page with the same pass as lean-render-publish. |   |   | . | Tool | lean-kg-publish | . | IRI | https://litlfred.github.io/folio-assistant/folio-assistant-sci/tools/lean-kg-publish.jsonld | . | part of | https://litlfred.github.io/folio-assistant/folio-assistant-sci/folio-assistant-sci.jsonld | . | type | https://litlfred.github.io/cat-harness/v0/ns/Tool | . | declared by | folio-assistant-sci | . | source | folio-assistant-sci/tools/lean-kg-publish/lean-kg-publish.ts | . | invoked | shell | . | qa | qa-reports | .
